atra snāsyati yaḥ samyaksāgare lavaṇāṃbhasi ..
aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpsyati mānavaḥ .. 86 ..
śrīsomeśasamudrasya aṃtare ye mṛtā narāḥ ..
pāpino'pi gamiṣyaṃti svargaṃ nirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ .. 87 ..
evaṃ bhaviṣyati sadā tava madvacanādvibho ..
prayacchasva dvijeṃdrāṇāṃ ratnāni vividhāni ca .. 88 ..
tena tuṣṭā varaṃ bhūyaḥ pradāsyaṃti tavepsitam .. 89 ..
16.29.d:
भविष्यति नृणां लोके तव सौख्यविवर्द्धनम् ..
पितॄणां तव तोयेन यः करिष्यति तर्पणम् ..
पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 93 ..
यावत्त्वं तिष्ठसे लोके यावच्चद्रार्कतारकाः ..
तवोदकामृतैस्तृप्तास्तावत्स्थास्यंति पूर्वजाः .. 84 ..
माघे मासि च यः स्नायान्नैरंतर्येण भावितः ..
पौंडरीकफलं तस्य दिवसेदिवसे भवेत् .. 89 ..
यात्रायामथवान्यत्र पर्वकाले शशिग्रहे ..
अत्र स्नास्यति यः सम्यक्सागरे लवणांभसि ..
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्स्यति मानवः .. 86 ..
श्रीसोमेशसमुद्रस्य अंतरे ये मृता नराः ..
पापिनोऽपि गमिष्यंति स्वर्गं निर्धूतकल्मषाः .. 87 ..
एवं भविष्यति सदा तव मद्वचनाद्विभो ..
प्रयच्छस्व द्विजेंद्राणां रत्नानि विविधानि च .. 88 ..
तेन तुष्टा वरं भूयः प्रदास्यंति तवेप्सितम् .. 89 ..
16.29.m:
It will promote well-being for men in the world. / Whoever performs the water-offering to the ancestors with your water / according to the previously stated rite—hear the meritorious fruit for him:
As long as you remain in the world, and as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure, / so long will his ancestors remain satisfied with your waters resembling nectar.
And whoever, filled with devotion, bathes continually in the month of Māgha, / shall obtain the fruit of a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice day after day.
Whether on a pilgrimage or elsewhere, on a festival day or during an eclipse of the moon, / the man who properly bathes here in the ocean of salt water / shall attain the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Those men who die in the area between illustrious Someśa and the ocean, / even if they are sinners, shall go to heaven, their impurities shaken off.
Thus it shall always be for you, O lord, by my word. / Bestow jewels of various kinds upon the chiefs of the twice-born.
Pleased by that, they will in turn grant you your desired boon."

16.29.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā bāḍhamityeva sāgaraḥ ..
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ suratnāni dadau śraddhā samanvitaḥ ..7.1.29.90..
brāhmaṇairbrahmaṇo vākyamaśeṣaṃ samanuṣṭhitam ..
kṣurakarma tathā kṛtvā snānaṃ sarve'pi cakrire .. 91 ..
evaṃ pavitratāṃ prāptastīrthatvaṃ lava ṇodadhiḥ ..
tasya madhye mahādevi liṃgānāṃ paṃcakoṭayaḥ .. 92 ..
asminmanvaṃtare devi adṛśyāḥ sāgare kṛtāḥ ..
agnikuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva tathānyatpadmakaṃ saraḥ ..93 ..
16.29.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा बाढमित्येव सागरः ..
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सुरत्नानि ददौ श्रद्धा समन्वितः ..7.1.29.90..
ब्राह्मणैर्ब्रह्मणो वाक्यमशेषं समनुष्ठितम् ..
क्षुरकर्म तथा कृत्वा स्नानं सर्वेऽपि चक्रिरे .. 91 ..
एवं पवित्रतां प्राप्तस्तीर्थत्वं लव णोदधिः ..
तस्य मध्ये महादेवि लिंगानां पंचकोटयः .. 92 ..
अस्मिन्मन्वंतरे देवि अदृश्याः सागरे कृताः ..
अग्निकुण्डं च तत्रैव तथान्यत्पद्मकं सरः ..93 ..
16.29.m:
Īśvara said: / Hearing the words of the Grandfather, the ocean said 'So be it,' / and, endowed with faith, gave fine jewels to the brahmins.
The brahmins carried out the word of Brahmā in full. / Having undergone the rite of tonsure, all of them took their ritual ablution.
In this way the salt ocean attained sanctity and the status of a sacred ford. / Within it, O great Goddess, are fifty million liṅgas.
In this Manvantara, O Goddess, they were made invisible in the ocean; / and right there is a fire altar, as well as another lake named Padmaka.

16.29.s:
madhye tu prāvṛtaṃ sarvamasminmanvaṃtare priye ..
cakramainākayormadhye diśi dakṣiṇamucyate .. 94 ..
16.29.d:
मध्ये तु प्रावृतं सर्वमस्मिन्मन्वंतरे प्रिये ..
चक्रमैनाकयोर्मध्ये दिशि दक्षिणमुच्यते .. 94 ..
16.29.m: Everything in the middle, however, is concealed in this Manvantara, O beloved. / Between Cakra and Maināka, in the southern direction it is declared:

16.29.s:
śātakumbhamaye kumbhe dhanuṣāyutavistṛte .. ..
tatra kuṃbhasya madhyastho vaḍavānalasaṃjñitaḥ .. 95 ..
16.29.d:
शातकुम्भमये कुम्भे धनुषायुतविस्तृते .. ..
तत्र कुंभस्य मध्यस्थो वडवानलसंज्ञितः .. 95 ..
16.29.m: in a jar made of gold, ten thousand bow-lengths in width, / dwelling in the middle of that jar is the one named the submarine fire (Vaḍavānala).

16.29.s:
sūcīvaktro mahākāyaḥ sa jalaṃ pibate sadā ..
etadaṃtaramāsādya agnitīrthaṃ pracakṣate .. 96 ..
16.29.d:
सूचीवक्त्रो महाकायः स जलं पिबते सदा ..
एतदंतरमासाद्य अग्नितीर्थं प्रचक्षते .. 96 ..
16.29.m: Having a mouth like a needle and an immense body, it constantly drinks the water. / Reaching this interior, it is known as Agnitīrtha.

16.29.s:
tasya madhye mahāsāraṃ vāḍavaṃ yatra vai mukham ..
śrīsomeśāddakṣiṇato dhanvaṃtaraśatāvadhi ..
uttarānmānasātpūrvaṃ yāvadeva kṛtasmaram .. 97 ..
16.29.d:
तस्य मध्ये महासारं वाडवं यत्र वै मुखम् ..
श्रीसोमेशाद्दक्षिणतो धन्वंतरशतावधि ..
उत्तरान्मानसात्पूर्वं यावदेव कृतस्मरम् .. 97 ..
16.29.m: In the middle of it is the mighty essence where the submarine mouth is, / extending for a distance of one hundred bow-lengths south of illustrious Someśa, / and to the east from northern Mānasa as far as Kṛtasmara.

16.29.s:
etadgopyaṃ varārohe na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit ..
brahmaghnopi viśudhyeta śrutvaitannātra saṃśayaḥ .. 98 ..
16.29.d:
एतद्गोप्यं वरारोहे न देयं यस्य कस्यचित् ..
ब्रह्मघ्नोपि विशुध्येत श्रुत्वैतन्नात्र संशयः .. 98 ..
16.29.m: This is a secret, O fair-hipped lady; it should not be given to just anyone. / Even one who has killed a brahmin would be purified upon hearing this; of this there is no doubt.

16.29.s:
evaṃ śāpo varo dattaḥ sāgarasya yathā dvijaiḥ ..
pūrvaṃ ruṣṭaistatastuṣṭaistatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ mayā ..99 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye samudasyāpeyatākāraṇa varṇanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..29..
16.29.d:
एवं शापो वरो दत्तः सागरस्य यथा द्विजैः ..
पूर्वं रुष्टैस्ततस्तुष्टैस्तत्सर्वं कथितं मया ..99 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये समुदस्यापेयताकारण वर्णनंनामैकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ..29..
16.29.m:
Thus, how the curse and the boon were given to the ocean by the twice-born / who were first angered and then pleased—all of that has been told by me.
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, entitled "Description of the Reason for the Ocean's Undrinkability," in the first [sub-section], the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the seventh [section], the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

16.30.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
snātvā tatrāgnitīrtheṣu kaṃ devaṃ pūrvamarccayet ..
nirvighnā jāyate yena yātrā nṛṇāṃ sureśvara ..
tanme yātrāvidhānaṃ tu yathāvadvaktumarhasi .. 1 ..
16.30.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
स्नात्वा तत्राग्नितीर्थेषु कं देवं पूर्वमर्च्चयेत् ..
निर्विघ्ना जायते येन यात्रा नृणां सुरेश्वर ..
तन्मे यात्राविधानं तु यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि .. 1 ..
16.30.m: The Goddess said: / Having bathed there at Agnitīrtha, which god should one worship first, / by means of which a person's pilgrimage becomes free from obstacles, O Lord of gods? / You ought to tell me the proper procedure for that pilgrimage as it truly is.

16.30.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
evaṃ snātvā vidhānena dattvārghyaṃ ca mahodadhau ..
saṃpūjya gaṃdhapuṣpaiśca vastraiḥ puṣpāvalepanaiḥ .. 2 ..
16.30.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
एवं स्नात्वा विधानेन दत्त्वार्घ्यं च महोदधौ ..
संपूज्य गंधपुष्पैश्च वस्त्रैः पुष्पावलेपनैः .. 2 ..
16.30.m: Īśvara said: / Having thus performed the ritual ablution according to rule, and having offered an arghya into the great ocean, / and worshipped with fragrant flowers, garments, and floral unguents, 2

16.30.s:
hiraṇmayaṃ yathāśaktyā prakṣipettatra kaṃkaṇam ..
tataḥ pitṝṃstarpayitvā gaccheddevaṃ kapardinam .. 3 ..
16.30.d:
हिरण्मयं यथाशक्त्या प्रक्षिपेत्तत्र कंकणम् ..
ततः पितॄंस्तर्पयित्वा गच्छेद्देवं कपर्दिनम् .. 3 ..
16.30.m: one should cast a golden bracelet there according to one's ability. / Then, having offered libations to the ancestors, one should go to the god Kapardin. 3

16.30.s:
puṣpairdhūpaistathā gandhairvastraiḥ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ ..
gaṇānāṃ tveti mantreṇa arghyaṃ cāsmai nivedayet .. 4 ..
16.30.d:
पुष्पैर्धूपैस्तथा गन्धैर्वस्त्रैः संपूज्य भक्तितः ..
गणानां त्वेति मन्त्रेण अर्घ्यं चास्मै निवेदयेत् .. 4 ..
16.30.m: Having worshipped him with devotion by means of flowers, incenses, perfumes, and garments, / one should offer an arghya to him with the mantra beginning with "gaṇānāṃ tvā". 4

16.30.s:
śūdrāṇāmatha deveśi maṃtraścāṣṭākṣaraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
tatra someśvaraṃ gaccheddevaṃ pāpaharaṃ param .. 5 ..
16.30.d:
शूद्राणामथ देवेशि मंत्रश्चाष्टाक्षरः स्मृतः ..
तत्र सोमेश्वरं गच्छेद्देवं पापहरं परम् .. 5 ..
16.30.m: For śūdras, O goddess of gods, the eight-syllable mantra is prescribed. / There one should go to Someśvara, the supreme god who removes sins. 5

16.30.s:
snāpayitvā vidhānena japecca śatarudriyam ..
tathā rudrānsapañcāṃgāstathānyā rudrasaṃhitāḥ .. 6 ..
16.30.d:
स्नापयित्वा विधानेन जपेच्च शतरुद्रियम् ..
तथा रुद्रान्सपञ्चांगास्तथान्या रुद्रसंहिताः .. 6 ..
16.30.m: Having bathed him according to rule, one should recite the Śatarudrīya, / and likewise the Rudra hymns with their five limbs, and other Rudra collections. 6

16.30.s:
snāpayetpayasā caiva dadhnā ghṛtayutena ca ..
madhunekṣurasenaiva kuṃkumena vilepayet .. 7 ..
16.30.d:
स्नापयेत्पयसा चैव दध्ना घृतयुतेन च ..
मधुनेक्षुरसेनैव कुंकुमेन विलेपयेत् .. 7 ..
16.30.m: One should bathe him with milk, curd combined with ghee, / and with honey and sugarcane juice, and anoint him with saffron. 7

16.30.s:
karpūrośīramiśreṇa mṛganābhiyutena ca ..
candanena sugandhena pūjyaṃ saṃpūjayettataḥ .. 8 ..
16.30.d:
कर्पूरोशीरमिश्रेण मृगनाभियुतेन च ..
चन्दनेन सुगन्धेन पूज्यं संपूजयेत्ततः .. 8 ..
16.30.m: Then one should worship the adorable Lord with fragrant sandalwood, / mixed with camphor and uśīra, and combined with musk. 8

16.30.s:
dhūpairbahuvidhairdevaṃ dhūpayitvā yathāvidhi ..
vastraiḥ saṃveṣṭayetpaścāddadyānnaivedyamuttamam .. 9 ..
16.30.d:
धूपैर्बहुविधैर्देवं धूपयित्वा यथाविधि ..
वस्त्रैः संवेष्टयेत्पश्चाद्दद्यान्नैवेद्यमुत्तमम् .. 9 ..
16.30.m: Having fumigated the god with various incenses according to the prescribed rite, / one should then wrap him in garments and present an excellent food offering. 9

16.30.s:
ārārtikaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā nṛtyaṃ kuryādyathecchayā ..
aṣṭāṃgaṃ praṇipatyaivaṃ gītavādyādikaṃ tataḥ .. 7.1.30.10 ..
16.30.d:
आरार्तिकं ततः कृत्वा नृत्यं कुर्याद्यथेच्छया ..
अष्टांगं प्रणिपत्यैवं गीतवाद्यादिकं ततः .. 7.1.30.10 ..
16.30.m: Having then performed the wave-offering of lights, one may dance as one wishes, / prostrating with the eight limbs, and then perform songs, instrumental music, and the like. 10

16.30.s:
dharmaśravaṇasaṃyuktaṃ kāryaṃ prekṣaṇakaṃ vibhoḥ ..
tato dadyāddvijātibhyastapasvibhyaśca śaktitaḥ .. 11 ..
16.30.d:
धर्मश्रवणसंयुक्तं कार्यं प्रेक्षणकं विभोः ..
ततो दद्याद्द्विजातिभ्यस्तपस्विभ्यश्च शक्तितः .. 11 ..
16.30.m: A theatrical performance for the Lord, accompanied by hearing the sacred teaching, should be arranged. / Then one should give to twice-born persons and ascetics according to one's ability. 11

16.30.s:
dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇebhyaśca dānaṃ kārpaṭikeṣu ca ..
vṛṣabhastatra dātavyaḥ pravṛtte krūrakarmaṇi ..
upavāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāttasminnahani bhāmini .. 12 ..
16.30.d:
दीनांधकृपणेभ्यश्च दानं कार्पटिकेषु च ..
वृषभस्तत्र दातव्यः प्रवृत्ते क्रूरकर्मणि ..
उपवासं ततः कुर्यात्तस्मिन्नहनि भामिनि .. 12 ..
16.30.m: Gifts should be given to the poor, the blind, the wretched, and to pilgrims. / A bull should be gifted there when a cruel act has commenced. / Then one should observe a fast on that day, O beautiful lady. 12

16.30.s:
yasminnahani paśyeta devaṃ someśvaraṃ naraḥ ..
sā tithirvarṣamekaṃ tu upoṣyā bhaktitatparaiḥ .. 13 ..
16.30.d:
यस्मिन्नहनि पश्येत देवं सोमेश्वरं नरः ..
सा तिथिर्वर्षमेकं तु उपोष्या भक्तितत्परैः .. 13 ..
16.30.m: The lunar day on which a person beholds the god Someśvara / should be observed as a fast for one year by those intent on devotion. 13

16.30.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā naro bhaktyā labhate janmanaḥ phalam ..
tathā ca sarvatīrthānāṃ sakalaṃ labhate phalam .. ..14..
16.30.d:
एवं कृत्वा नरो भक्त्या लभते जन्मनः फलम् ..
तथा च सर्वतीर्थानां सकलं लभते फलम् .. ..14..
16.30.m: Having acted thus with devotion, a man obtains the fruit of human birth, / and he likewise obtains the entire fruit of all the sacred fords. 14

16.30.s:
uddharetpitṛvargaṃ ca mātṛvargaṃ ca bhāmini ..
bālye vayasi yatpāpaṃ vārdhakye yauvane'pi vā .. 15 ..
16.30.d:
उद्धरेत्पितृवर्गं च मातृवर्गं च भामिनि ..
बाल्ये वयसि यत्पापं वार्धक्ये यौवनेऽपि वा .. 15 ..
16.30.m: He redeems his paternal family and his maternal family, O beautiful lady. / Whatever sin was committed in childhood, in old age, or in youth, 15

16.30.s:
kṣālayeccaiva tatsarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā someśvaraṃ naraḥ ..
na duḥkhito na dāridro durbhago vā na jāyate .. 16 ..
16.30.d:
क्षालयेच्चैव तत्सर्वं दृष्ट्वा सोमेश्वरं नरः ..
न दुःखितो न दारिद्रो दुर्भगो वा न जायते .. 16 ..
16.30.m: a man washes away all that merely by beholding Someśvara; / he is never miserable, nor poor, nor unfortunate. 16

16.30.s:
saptajanmāntareṇaiva dṛṣṭe someśvare vibhau ..
dhanadhānyasamāyukte sphīte sañjāyate kule .. 17 ..
16.30.d:
सप्तजन्मान्तरेणैव दृष्टे सोमेश्वरे विभौ ..
धनधान्यसमायुक्ते स्फीते सञ्जायते कुले .. 17 ..
16.30.m: When the all-pervading Someśvara is beheld, within seven births / he is born in an affluent family, richly endowed with wealth and grain. 17

16.30.s:
bhaktirbhavati bhūyo'pi somanāthaṃ prati prabhum ..
kṣīreṇa snapanaṃ pūrvaṃ tato dhārāsamudbhavam .. 18 ..
16.30.d:
भक्तिर्भवति भूयोऽपि सोमनाथं प्रति प्रभुम् ..
क्षीरेण स्नपनं पूर्वं ततो धारासमुद्भवम् .. 18 ..
16.30.m: Devotion toward the Lord Somanātha arises again and again. / First the ceremonial bath with milk, and then that which arises from a continuous stream [is performed]. 18

16.30.s:
prathame prathame yāme mahāsnā namataḥ param ..
madhyāhne devadevasya ye prapaśyanti mānavāḥ ..
saṃdhyāmārārtikaṃ bhūyo na jāyante ca mānuṣāḥ .. 19 ..
16.30.d:
प्रथमे प्रथमे यामे महास्ना नमतः परम् ..
मध्याह्ने देवदेवस्य ये प्रपश्यन्ति मानवाः ..
संध्यामारार्तिकं भूयो न जायन्ते च मानुषाः .. 19 ..
16.30.m: After this, the great bath is performed during the first watch; / those mortals who behold the twilight wave-offering of lights of the God of gods at midday / are never born as humans again. 19

16.30.s:
matvā kaliyugaṃ raudraṃ bahupāpaṃ varānane ..
nānyena tarate durgāṃ karmaṇā durgatiṃ naraḥ .. 7.1.30.20 ..
16.30.d:
मत्वा कलियुगं रौद्रं बहुपापं वरानने ..
नान्येन तरते दुर्गां कर्मणा दुर्गतिं नरः .. 7.1.30.20 ..
16.30.m: Considering the Kali age to be terrible and full of manifold sins, O fair-faced lady, / a man does not cross over this difficult misery through any other act. 20

16.30.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetra māhātmye someśvaramāhātmye someśvarapūjāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma triṃśodhyāyaḥ .. 30 ..
16.30.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्र माहात्म्ये सोमेश्वरमाहात्म्ये सोमेश्वरपूजामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिंशोध्यायः .. 30 ..
16.30.m: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, entitled "Description of the Greatness of the Worship of Someśvara," in the Greatness of Someśvara, in the Greatness of Prabhāsa Field, in the first Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the seventh section Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa containing eighty-one thousand verses. 30

16.31.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
sakārapaṃcakaṃ proktaṃ yattvayā mama śaṃkara ..
kathaṃ tadatra saṃvṛttametanme saṃśayaṃ mahat .. 1 ..
16.31.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
सकारपंचकं प्रोक्तं यत्त्वया मम शंकर ..
कथं तदत्र संवृत्तमेतन्मे संशयं महत् .. 1 ..
16.31.m: The goddess said: / That group of five beginning with 'sa' which was spoken of by you, O Śaṃkara, / how did that come to be here? This is a great doubt of mine. 1

16.31.s:
kathaṃ vātra samāyātā kutaścāpi sarasvatī ..
kathaṃ sa vāḍavo jātaḥ kasminkāle kathaṃ hyabhūt ..
tatsarvaṃ vistareṇedaṃ yathāvadvaktumarhasi .. 2 ..
16.31.d:
कथं वात्र समायाता कुतश्चापि सरस्वती ..
कथं स वाडवो जातः कस्मिन्काले कथं ह्यभूत् ..
तत्सर्वं विस्तरेणेदं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि .. 2 ..
16.31.m: Or how did Sarasvatī arrive here, and from where? / How was that submarine fire born, at what time, and in what manner did it come to be? / You ought to tell me all this in detail and as it truly happened. 2

16.31.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu devi yathā jātā tasminkṣetre sarasvatī ..
yataścaiva samudbhūtā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .. 3 ..
16.31.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
शृणु देवि यथा जाता तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे सरस्वती ..
यतश्चैव समुद्भूता सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .. 3 ..
16.31.m: Īśvara said: / Hear, O goddess, how Sarasvatī was born in that sacred field, / and from where she, the destroyer of all sins, arose: 3

16.31.s: hiraṇyā vajriṇī nyaṃkuḥ kapilā ca sarasvatī .. 4 ..
16.31.d: हिरण्या वज्रिणी न्यंकुः कपिला च सरस्वती .. 4 ..
16.31.m: Hiraṇyā, Vajriṇī, Nyaṅku, Kapilā, and Sarasvatī. 4

16.31.s:
ṛṣibhiḥ pañcabhiścātra samāhūtā yathā purā ..
vāḍavenāgninā yuktā yathā jātā śṛṇuṣva tat .. 5 ..
16.31.d:
ऋषिभिः पञ्चभिश्चात्र समाहूता यथा पुरा ..
वाडवेनाग्निना युक्ता यथा जाता शृणुष्व तत् .. 5 ..
16.31.m: Hear how she was summoned here in ancient times by five seers, / and how she became united with the submarine fire. 5

16.31.s:
purā devāsure yuddhe nivṛtte somakāraṇāt ..
pitāmahasya vacanāttārāṃ candraḥ samarpayat .. 6 ..
16.31.d:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे निवृत्ते सोमकारणात् ..
पितामहस्य वचनात्तारां चन्द्रः समर्पयत् .. 6 ..
16.31.m: Formerly, when the war between gods and asuras ceased on account of Soma, / the Moon surrendered Tārā in accordance with the word of the Grandfather. 6

16.31.s:
tato yātāḥ surāḥ svargaṃ paśyanto'dhomukhā mahīm ..
dadṛśuste tato devā bhūmyāṃ svargamivāparam .. 7 ..
16.31.d:
ततो याताः सुराः स्वर्गं पश्यन्तोऽधोमुखा महीम् ..
ददृशुस्ते ततो देवा भूम्यां स्वर्गमिवापरम् .. 7 ..
16.31.m: Then the gods set out for heaven, looking downward upon the earth; / then those gods beheld upon earth what seemed like a second heaven: 7

16.31.s:
āśramaṃ munimukhyasya dadhīcerloka viśrutam ..
sarvarttukusumopetaṃ pādapairupaśobhitam ..
ketakīkuṭajodbhūta bakulāmodamoditam .. 8 ..
16.31.d:
आश्रमं मुनिमुख्यस्य दधीचेर्लोक विश्रुतम् ..
सर्वर्त्तुकुसुमोपेतं पादपैरुपशोभितम् ..
केतकीकुटजोद्भूत बकुलामोदमोदितम् .. 8 ..
16.31.m: the hermitage of Dadhīci, the foremost of sages, famous throughout the world, / endowed with flowers of all seasons, adorned with trees, / delighting with the fragrance of ketakī, kuṭaja, and bakula blossoms. 8

16.31.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ samāsādya tadāśramapadaṃ guru ..
kautukāddraṣṭumārabdhāḥ sarve devā manoramam .. 9 ..
16.31.d:
एवंविधं समासाद्य तदाश्रमपदं गुरु ..
कौतुकाद्द्रष्टुमारब्धाः सर्वे देवा मनोरमम् .. 9 ..
16.31.m: Having reached such a venerable hermitage grounds, / all the gods began to view it with curiosity and delight. 9

16.31.s:
te ca tīrthāśrame tasminyānānyutsṛjya saṃyatāḥ ..
pravṛttāstamṛṣiṃ draṣṭuṃ prākṛtāḥ puruṣā yathā .. 7.1.31.10 ..
16.31.d:
ते च तीर्थाश्रमे तस्मिन्यानान्युत्सृज्य संयताः ..
प्रवृत्तास्तमृषिं द्रष्टुं प्राकृताः पुरुषा यथा .. 7.1.31.10 ..
16.31.m: Leaving their aerial chariots at that sacred hermitage, self-restrained, / they proceeded to see that seer just like ordinary men. 10

16.31.s:
dṛṣṭavaṃtaḥ surāḥ sarve pitāmahamivāparam ..
tatasta ṛṣiṇā sarve pādyārghyādibhirarccitāḥ .. 11 ..
16.31.d:
दृष्टवंतः सुराः सर्वे पितामहमिवापरम् ..
ततस्त ऋषिणा सर्वे पाद्यार्घ्यादिभिरर्च्चिताः .. 11 ..
16.31.m: All the gods beheld [him], resembling another Grandfather; / then all of them were honoured by the seer with water for the feet, arghya, and other rites. 11

16.31.s:
yathoktamāsanaṃ bhejuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
teṣāṃ madhye samutthāya śakraḥ provāca taṃ munim .. 12 ..
16.31.d:
यथोक्तमासनं भेजुः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
तेषां मध्ये समुत्थाय शक्रः प्रोवाच तं मुनिम् .. 12 ..
16.31.m: All the gods along with Indra took their seats as instructed. / Rising in their midst, Indra addressed that sage: 12

16.31.s:
āyudhāni vimucyāgre bhavāngṛhṇātvimāni hi ..
tanniśamya vacaḥ prāha dadhīciḥ pākaśāsanam .. 13 ..
16.31.d:
आयुधानि विमुच्याग्रे भवान्गृह्णात्विमानि हि ..
तन्निशम्य वचः प्राह दधीचिः पाकशासनम् .. 13 ..
16.31.m: "Relinquishing the weapons before you, please take charge of these." / Hearing that statement, Dadhīci said to the subduer of Pāka: 13

16.31.s:
muktāstrāṇi mamābhyāśe yūyaṃ yāta triviṣṭapam ..
taṃ śakraḥ prāha caitāni kāryakāle hyupasthite .. 14 ..
16.31.d:
मुक्तास्त्राणि ममाभ्याशे यूयं यात त्रिविष्टपम् ..
तं शक्रः प्राह चैतानि कार्यकाले ह्युपस्थिते .. 14 ..
16.31.m: "Leaving the weapons in my presence, go to heaven." / To him Indra said: "And when the time of need arises, 14

16.31.s:
deyāni te punaḥ śatrūnabhijeṣyāmahe raṇe ..
punaḥpunastataḥ śakraḥ saṃdiśya munisattamam .. 15 ..
16.31.d:
देयानि ते पुनः शत्रूनभिजेष्यामहे रणे ..
पुनःपुनस्ततः शक्रः संदिश्य मुनिसत्तमम् .. 15 ..
16.31.m: they must be returned by you, so that we may vanquish our enemies in battle." / Then, repeatedly enjoining the best of sages, Indra said: 15

16.31.s:
asmākameva deyāni na cānyasya tvayā mune..
bāḍhamityudite śakramuktavānmunisattamaḥ..16..
16.31.d:
अस्माकमेव देयानि न चान्यस्य त्वया मुने..
बाढमित्युदिते शक्रमुक्तवान्मुनिसत्तमः..16..
16.31.m: "They must be given only to us, and not to anyone else by you, O sage." / When Indra said, "Very well," the best of sages replied to him: 16

16.31.s:
dāsyāmi te samastāni yuddhakāle viśeṣataḥ..
nāsya mithyā bhavedvākyamiti matvā śacīpatiḥ..
muktvāstrāṇi tadabhyāśe punaḥ svargaṃ gatastadā..17..
16.31.d:
दास्यामि ते समस्तानि युद्धकाले विशेषतः..
नास्य मिथ्या भवेद्वाक्यमिति मत्वा शचीपतिः..
मुक्त्वास्त्राणि तदभ्याशे पुनः स्वर्गं गतस्तदा..17..
16.31.m: "I will give them all to you, especially at the time of battle." / Thinking, "His word will not prove false," the husband of Śacī, / having left the weapons near him, then returned to heaven. 17

16.31.s:
astrārpaṇaṃ yaḥ prayataḥ prayatnācchṛṇoti rājā bhuvi bhāvitātātmā ..
so'bhyeti yuddhe vijayaṃ paraṃ hi sutāṃśca dharmārthayaśobhirāmāḥ .. 18 ..
16.31.d:
अस्त्रार्पणं यः प्रयतः प्रयत्नाच्छृणोति राजा भुवि भावितातात्मा ..
सोऽभ्येति युद्धे विजयं परं हि सुतांश्च धर्मार्थयशोभिरामाः .. 18 ..
16.31.m: A purified king on earth whose soul is cultivated, who hears with diligence of this entrustment of weapons, / attains supreme victory in battle, and sons charming with righteousness, wealth, and renown. 18

16.31.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhā sakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye vaḍavānalotpattivṛttānte dadhīcimaharṣaye sarvadevakṛtasvasvaśastrasamarpaṇavarṇanaṃnāmaikatriṃśodhyāyaḥ.. 31 ..
16.31.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभा सखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वडवानलोत्पत्तिवृत्तान्ते दधीचिमहर्षये सर्वदेवकृतस्वस्वशस्त्रसमर्पणवर्णनंनामैकत्रिंशोध्यायः.. 31 ..
16.31.m: Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, entitled "Description of the Surrender of Their Respective Weapons by All the Gods to the Great Seer Dadhīci in the Account of the Origin of the Submarine Fire," in the Greatness of Prabhāsa Field, in the first Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, in the seventh section Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa containing eighty-one thousand verses. 31

16.32.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tatasteṣu prayāteṣu devadeveṣvasau muniḥ ..
śatavarṣāṇi tatrasthastapase prasthito dvijaḥ .. 1 ..
16.32.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवदेवेष्वसौ मुनिः ..
शतवर्षाणि तत्रस्थस्तपसे प्रस्थितो द्विजः .. 1 ..
16.32.m: Īśvara said: / Then, when those gods of gods had departed, that sage, / the twice-born, having stayed there for a hundred years, set out for austerity,

16.32.s:
āśramāduttarāttasmāddivyāṃ diśamathottarām..
subhadrāpi mahābhāgā tasya yā paricārikā .. 2 ..
16.32.d:
आश्रमादुत्तरात्तस्माद्दिव्यां दिशमथोत्तराम्..
सुभद्रापि महाभागा तस्य या परिचारिका .. 2 ..
16.32.m: from that northern hermitage towards the divine northern quarter. / Subhadrā also, of great fortune, who was his attendant,

16.32.s:
astrādāne'samarthā sā ṛṣiṃ provāca bhāminī ..
nāhaṃ netuṃ samarthāsmi śastrāṇyālabhya pāṇinā ..3..
16.32.d:
अस्त्रादानेऽसमर्था सा ऋषिं प्रोवाच भामिनी ..
नाहं नेतुं समर्थास्मि शस्त्राण्यालभ्य पाणिना ..3..
16.32.m: unable to carry the weapons, that lovely woman said to the seer: / 'I am not able to carry the weapons, grasping them in my hand.'

16.32.s:
jalena saha tadvīryaṃ pītavānsa ṛṣistataḥ ..
ātmasaṃsthāni sarvāṇi divyānyastrāṇyasau muniḥ ..
kārayitvottarāmāśāṃ jagāma tapasāṃ nidhiḥ .. 4 ..
16.32.d:
जलेन सह तद्वीर्यं पीतवान्स ऋषिस्ततः ..
आत्मसंस्थानि सर्वाणि दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्यसौ मुनिः ..
कारयित्वोत्तरामाशां जगाम तपसां निधिः .. 4 ..
16.32.m: Then that seer drank their energy along with water; / having made all those divine weapons abide within himself, / that sage, a treasure-house of austerities, went to the northern direction.

16.32.s:
gaṃgādharaṃ śuklatanuṃ sarppairākīrṇavigraham ..
śivavatsukhadaṃ puṃsāmapaśyatsa himācalam .. 5 ..
16.32.d:
गंगाधरं शुक्लतनुं सर्प्पैराकीर्णविग्रहम् ..
शिववत्सुखदं पुंसामपश्यत्स हिमाचलम् .. 5 ..
16.32.m: He beheld the Himācala, which was like Śiva: / holding the Gaṅgā, of white body, its mass covered with serpents, giving happiness to men.

16.32.s:
tathāśramaṃ dadarśoccairaśvatthaiḥ paripālitam ..
caṃdrabhāgopakaṃṭhasthaṃ samitpuṣpakuśānvitam .. 6 ..
16.32.d:
तथाश्रमं ददर्शोच्चैरश्वत्थैः परिपालितम् ..
चंद्रभागोपकंठस्थं समित्पुष्पकुशान्वितम् .. 6 ..
16.32.m: He also saw a hermitage towering high, protected by aśvattha trees, / situated on the banks of the Candrabhāgā, supplied with sacrificial fuel, flowers, and kuśa grass.

16.32.s:
sa tasminmuniśādūlo hyavasanmunibhiḥ saha ..
subhadrayā ca saṃyuktaścaṃdraścaṃdrikayā yathā .. 7 ..
16.32.d:
स तस्मिन्मुनिशादूलो ह्यवसन्मुनिभिः सह ..
सुभद्रया च संयुक्तश्चंद्रश्चंद्रिकया यथा .. 7 ..
16.32.m: That tiger among sages dwelt there together with the sages / and accompanied by Subhadrā, as the moon with moonlight.

16.32.s:
ekadā vasatastasya subhadrā paricārikā ..
snānārthaṃ yātumārabdhā caturthe'hni rajasvalā .. 8 ..
16.32.d:
एकदा वसतस्तस्य सुभद्रा परिचारिका ..
स्नानार्थं यातुमारब्धा चतुर्थेऽह्नि रजस्वला .. 8 ..
16.32.m: Once, as he was dwelling [there], his attendant Subhadrā, / having menstruated, on the fourth day set out to go for a bath.

16.32.s:
vrajantyā ca tayā dṛṣṭaṃ kaupīnācchādanaṃ punaḥ ..
parityaktaṃ viditvaivaṃ daivayogādgṛhāṇa sā .. 9 ..
16.32.d:
व्रजन्त्या च तया दृष्टं कौपीनाच्छादनं पुनः ..
परित्यक्तं विदित्वैवं दैवयोगाद्गृहाण सा .. 9 ..
16.32.m: And while going, she saw a loincloth covering / that had been discarded; knowing it to be thus, by fate she took it.

16.32.s:
paridhāya punaḥ sā tu kaupīnaṃ retasāyutam ..
ekāṃte snātumārabdhā jalābhyāśe yathāsukham .. 7.1.32.10 ..
16.32.d:
परिधाय पुनः सा तु कौपीनं रेतसायुतम् ..
एकांते स्नातुमारब्धा जलाभ्याशे यथासुखम् .. 7.1.32.10 ..
16.32.m: Having put on that loincloth filled with semen, / she began to bathe in solitude near the water at her pleasure.

16.32.s:
tato devī yathākāmamakasmādvīkṣate hi sā ..
svodarasthaṃ samutpannaṃ garbhaṃ gurubharālasā .. 11 ..
16.32.d:
ततो देवी यथाकाममकस्माद्वीक्षते हि सा ..
स्वोदरस्थं समुत्पन्नं गर्भं गुरुभरालसा .. 11 ..
16.32.m: Then, suddenly and unexpectedly, that lady saw / an embryo born within her womb, she being languid with a heavy burden.

16.32.s:
śocayitvātmanātmānamagarbhāhamihāgatā ..
tatkena mandabhāginyā mamaivaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ kṛtam.. 12 ..
16.32.d:
शोचयित्वात्मनात्मानमगर्भाहमिहागता ..
तत्केन मन्दभागिन्या ममैवं दूषणं कृतम्.. 12 ..
16.32.m: Grieving in her mind [she thought]: 'I came here without a womb [bearing child]; / then by whom has this defilement been brought upon an unfortunate woman like me?'

16.32.s:
lajjābhibhūtā sā tatra praviśyāśvatthavāṭikām ..
tatra taṃ suṣuve garbhamavijñāya kuto hyayam .. 13 ..
16.32.d:
लज्जाभिभूता सा तत्र प्रविश्याश्वत्थवाटिकाम् ..
तत्र तं सुषुवे गर्भमविज्ञाय कुतो ह्ययम् .. 13 ..
16.32.m: Overwhelmed with shame, having entered an aśvattha grove there, / she brought forth that fetus, not knowing: 'Whence indeed is this?'

16.32.s:
punareva hi sā snātvā avijñāyātmaduṣkṛtam..
śāpaṃ dātuṃ samārabdhā garbhakarttari duḥsaham .. 14 ..
16.32.d:
पुनरेव हि सा स्नात्वा अविज्ञायात्मदुष्कृतम्..
शापं दातुं समारब्धा गर्भकर्त्तरि दुःसहम् .. 14 ..
16.32.m: Then, having bathed again, unaware of her own misdeed, / she began to utter an unbearable curse upon the maker of the fetus:

16.32.s:
jñānādvā yadi vājñānādyeneyaṃ dūṣaṇā kṛtā ..
so'dyaiva paṃcatāṃ yātu yadyahaṃ syāṃ pativratā .. 15 ..
16.32.d:
ज्ञानाद्वा यदि वाज्ञानाद्येनेयं दूषणा कृता ..
सोऽद्यैव पंचतां यातु यद्यहं स्यां पतिव्रता .. 15 ..
16.32.m: 'Whether knowingly or unknowingly, whoever has caused this defilement, / may he meet his death this very day, if I am a devoted wife!

16.32.s:
yadyahaṃ manasā vāpi kāmaye nāparaṃ patim ..
etena satyavākyena yātu jāraḥ svayaṃ kṣayam .. .. 16 ..
16.32.d:
यद्यहं मनसा वापि कामये नापरं पतिम् ..
एतेन सत्यवाक्येन यातु जारः स्वयं क्षयम् .. .. 16 ..
16.32.m: If even in my mind I do not desire another husband, / by this statement of truth let the paramour perish on his own!'

16.32.s:
evaṃ śaptvā tu taṃ devī hyajñātvā garbhakāriṇam ..
punaryātuṃ samārabdhā taddadhīciniketanam .. 17 ..
16.32.d:
एवं शप्त्वा तु तं देवी ह्यज्ञात्वा गर्भकारिणम् ..
पुनर्यातुं समारब्धा तद्दधीचिनिकेतनम् .. 17 ..
16.32.m: Having thus cursed him, not knowing the maker of the fetus, / that lady began to return to that abode of Dadhīci.

16.32.s:
tatra cārkapratīkāśaṃ garbhamutsṛjya sā tadā ..
prāptā tapovanaṃ ramyaṃ yatrāsau munipuṃgavaḥ .. 18 ..
16.32.d:
तत्र चार्कप्रतीकाशं गर्भमुत्सृज्य सा तदा ..
प्राप्ता तपोवनं रम्यं यत्रासौ मुनिपुंगवः .. 18 ..
16.32.m: And abandoning the fetus there, which was radiant like the sun, / she arrived at that charming penance-grove where that bull among sages was.

16.32.s:
atrāṃtare sarvadevā lokapālā mahābalāḥ ..
astrāṇāṃ kāraṇārthāya munerāśramamāgatāḥ .. .. 19 ..
16.32.d:
अत्रांतरे सर्वदेवा लोकपाला महाबलाः ..
अस्त्राणां कारणार्थाय मुनेराश्रममागताः .. .. 19 ..
16.32.m: In the meantime, all the gods and the mighty world-protectors / arrived at the sage's hermitage for the sake of the weapons.

16.32.s:
uvāca taṃ muniṃ śakro nyāso yastava suvrata ..
datto'smābhistu śastrāṇāṃ tāni kṣipraṃ prayaccha naḥ .. 7.1.32.20 ..
16.32.d:
उवाच तं मुनिं शक्रो न्यासो यस्तव सुव्रत ..
दत्तोऽस्माभिस्तु शस्त्राणां तानि क्षिप्रं प्रयच्छ नः .. 7.1.32.20 ..
16.32.m: Śakra said to that sage: 'O you of good vows, the deposit of weapons / that was given by us to you, give those quickly to us.'

16.32.s:
ṛṣirāha purā yatra sthāpitāni mamāśrame ..
tatraiva tāni tiṣṭhaṃti na cānītāni vāsava .. 21 ..
16.32.d:
ऋषिराह पुरा यत्र स्थापितानि ममाश्रमे ..
तत्रैव तानि तिष्ठंति न चानीतानि वासव .. 21 ..
16.32.m: The seer said: 'O Vāsava, where they were placed formerly in my hermitage, / there alone they remain; they have not been brought here.

16.32.s:
yattu teṣāṃ balaṃ vīryaṃ saṃgrāme śatrusūdana ..
tanmayā pītamakhilaṃ saha toyena vāsava .. 22..
16.32.d:
यत्तु तेषां बलं वीर्यं संग्रामे शत्रुसूदन ..
तन्मया पीतमखिलं सह तोयेन वासव .. 22..
16.32.m: However, that strength and power of theirs in battle, O slayer of foes, / that was completely drunk by me together with water, O Vāsava.

16.32.s:
evaṃ sthite mayā'strāṇi yadi deyāni te'nagha ..
tatosthīni prayacchāmi tadākārāṇi suvrata .. 23 ..
16.32.d:
एवं स्थिते मयाऽस्त्राणि यदि देयानि तेऽनघ ..
ततोस्थीनि प्रयच्छामि तदाकाराणि सुव्रत .. 23 ..
16.32.m: Such being the case, if weapons are to be given by me to you, O sinless one, / then, O you of good vows, I shall give my bones, which have their forms.'

16.32.s:
evamuktaḥ sahasrākṣastamāha munisattamam ..
nānyeṣu tadbalaṃ raudraṃ yattu teṣu vyavasthitam .. 24 ..
16.32.d:
एवमुक्तः सहस्राक्षस्तमाह मुनिसत्तमम् ..
नान्येषु तद्बलं रौद्रं यत्तु तेषु व्यवस्थितम् .. 24 ..
16.32.m: Thus addressed, the thousand-eyed [Indra] said to that best of sages: / 'That fierce strength which resided in them does not exist in any other [weapons],

16.32.s:
yasmātteṣu vinikṣipya sahasrāṃśaṃ svatejasām ..
asmākaṃ dattavānrudro rakṣārthaṃ jagatāṃ śivaḥ .. 25 ..
16.32.d:
यस्मात्तेषु विनिक्षिप्य सहस्रांशं स्वतेजसाम् ..
अस्माकं दत्तवान्रुद्रो रक्षार्थं जगतां शिवः .. 25 ..
16.32.m: because Rudra, the benevolent Śiva, having infused into them / a thousandth part of his own splendor, gave [them] to us for the protection of the worlds.

16.32.s:
tadvayaṃ tāni sarvāṇi gṛhītvā ca vyavasthitāḥ ..
lokasya rakṣaṇārthāya saṃjñeyaṃ tena lokapāḥ .. 26 ..
16.32.d:
तद्वयं तानि सर्वाणि गृहीत्वा च व्यवस्थिताः ..
लोकस्य रक्षणार्थाय संज्ञेयं तेन लोकपाः .. 26 ..
16.32.m: Therefore, taking all of them, we stood / for the protection of the world; hence the name "world-protectors" [applies to us].

16.32.s:
amīṣāmapi śastrāṇā muttamaṃ vajramiṣyate ..
taddhāraṇādyato'smākaṃ devarājatvamiṣyate .. 27 ..
16.32.d:
अमीषामपि शस्त्राणा मुत्तमं वज्रमिष्यते ..
तद्धारणाद्यतोऽस्माकं देवराजत्वमिष्यते .. 27 ..
16.32.m: Even among these weapons, the thunderbolt is considered the best; / because from bearing it our sovereignty over the gods is maintained.

16.32.s:
vajrādapyuttamaṃ cakraṃ yattadviṣṇuparigrahe ..
daityadānavasaṃghānāṃ tadāyatto jayo'bhavat .. 28 ..
16.32.d:
वज्रादप्युत्तमं चक्रं यत्तद्विष्णुपरिग्रहे ..
दैत्यदानवसंघानां तदायत्तो जयोऽभवत् .. 28 ..
16.32.m: And better than the thunderbolt is the discus, which is held by Viṣṇu; / victory over the hosts of Daityas and Dānavas was dependent on that.

16.32.s:
tasmāttāni yathāsmābhiḥ prāpyate munisattama ..
tathā kuruṣva saṃcintya kāryaṃ kāryavidāṃ vara .. 29 ..
16.32.d:
तस्मात्तानि यथास्माभिः प्राप्यते मुनिसत्तम ..
तथा कुरुष्व संचिन्त्य कार्यं कार्यविदां वर .. 29 ..
16.32.m: Therefore, O best of sages, O best of those who know what must be done, / deliberate and act in such a way that they may be obtained by us.'

16.32.s:
evamukte muniḥ prāha taṃ śakraṃ purataḥ sthitam ..
tatprāptyarthamupāyaṃ tu kathayāmi tavāparam .. 7.1.32.30 ..
16.32.d:
एवमुक्ते मुनिः प्राह तं शक्रं पुरतः स्थितम् ..
तत्प्राप्त्यर्थमुपायं तु कथयामि तवापरम् .. 7.1.32.30 ..
16.32.m: When this was said, the sage spoke to that Śakra who stood before him: / 'I shall tell you another means for obtaining them.

16.32.s:
yānyetāni mamāsthīni yūyaṃ taistāni sarvaśaḥ ..
nirmāpayadhvaṃ śastrāṇi tadākārāṇi sarvaśaḥ .. 31 ..
16.32.d:
यान्येतानि ममास्थीनि यूयं तैस्तानि सर्वशः ..
निर्मापयध्वं शस्त्राणि तदाकाराणि सर्वशः .. 31 ..
16.32.m: These bones of mine that exist—from them / have weapons completely fashioned by you all, possessing their respective forms.

16.32.s:
etāni tatsamutthāni teṣāmapyadhikaṃ balam ..
sādhayiṣyati bhavatāṃ saṃgrāme yanmamehitam .. .. 32 ..
16.32.d:
एतानि तत्समुत्थानि तेषामप्यधिकं बलम् ..
साधयिष्यति भवतां संग्रामे यन्ममेहितम् .. .. 32 ..
16.32.m: These, originating from them, having strength even greater than theirs, / will accomplish for you in battle whatever is desired by me.'

16.32.s:
tamuvāca tataḥ śakro dadhīciṃ tapasonidhim ..
prāṇahāraṃ prakartuṃ te nāhaṃ śakto yamicchasi .. 33 ..
16.32.d:
तमुवाच ततः शक्रो दधीचिं तपसोनिधिम् ..
प्राणहारं प्रकर्तुं ते नाहं शक्तो यमिच्छसि .. 33 ..
16.32.m: Then Śakra said to him, to Dadhīci, the treasure-house of austerities: / 'I am not able to take away your life, which you desire [to give].

16.32.s:
na cāmṛtasya te'sthīni grahītuṃ śaktirasti naḥ ..
tasmātsarvaṃ samālocya yatkartavyaṃ taducyatām .. 34 ..
16.32.d:
न चामृतस्य तेऽस्थीनि ग्रहीतुं शक्तिरस्ति नः ..
तस्मात्सर्वं समालोच्य यत्कर्तव्यं तदुच्यताम् .. 34 ..
16.32.m: Nor do we have the power to take the bones of you while un-dead; / therefore, having considered everything, let that which ought to be done be spoken.'

16.32.s:
evamukto muniḥ prāha etadeva kalevaram ..
tyajāmi svayamevāhaṃ deva kāryārthasiddhaye .. 35 ..
16.32.d:
एवमुक्तो मुनिः प्राह एतदेव कलेवरम् ..
त्यजामि स्वयमेवाहं देव कार्यार्थसिद्धये .. 35 ..
16.32.m: Thus addressed, the sage said: 'I myself shall renounce / this very body for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.

16.32.s:
adhruvaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāmāśrayaṃ sujugupsitam ..
yadā hyetattadā yuktaḥ parityāgo'sya sāṃpratam .. 36 ..
16.32.d:
अध्रुवं सर्वदुःखानामाश्रयं सुजुगुप्सितम् ..
यदा ह्येतत्तदा युक्तः परित्यागोऽस्य सांप्रतम् .. 36 ..
16.32.m: Since this [body] is impermanent, the receptacle of all miseries, and utterly repulsive, / its abandonment right now is proper.

16.32.s:
asya tyāgena me duḥkhaṃ saṃsārotthaṃ na jāyate ..
yasmājjanmāṃtare jāto mṛtopi hi bhavetpunaḥ .. 37 ..
16.32.d:
अस्य त्यागेन मे दुःखं संसारोत्थं न जायते ..
यस्माज्जन्मांतरे जातो मृतोपि हि भवेत्पुनः .. 37 ..
16.32.m: By renouncing it, no misery arising from worldly existence will be born for me; / for one who is born in another life would certainly die again.

16.32.s:
bhāryā bhaginī duhitā svakarmaphalayojanāt ..
jātā tenaiva saṃsāre ratikārye jugupsitā .. 38 ..
16.32.d:
भार्या भगिनी दुहिता स्वकर्मफलयोजनात् ..
जाता तेनैव संसारे रतिकार्ये जुगुप्सिता .. 38 ..
16.32.m: A wife, a sister, or a daughter is born in worldly existence / through the conjunction of the fruits of one's own deeds, repulsive in sexual union.

16.32.s:
yasmācca svayamevaitadvapustyajati vai dhruvam ..
tasmādasya parityāgo varaḥ kāryo'cirātsvayam .. 39 ...
16.32.d:
यस्माच्च स्वयमेवैतद्वपुस्त्यजति वै ध्रुवम् ..
तस्मादस्य परित्यागो वरः कार्योऽचिरात्स्वयम् .. 39 ...
16.32.m: And because this body will certainly cast itself off on its own, / therefore it is better that its abandonment be done soon by myself.'

16.32.s:
evaṃ puraṃdarasyāgre saṃkīrtya sa mahāmuniḥ ..
dadhīciḥ prāṇasaṃhāraṃ kṛtavānsatvaraṃ tadā .. 7.1.32.40 ..
16.32.d:
एवं पुरंदरस्याग्रे संकीर्त्य स महामुनिः ..
दधीचिः प्राणसंहारं कृतवान्सत्वरं तदा .. 7.1.32.40 ..
16.32.m: Having spoken thus before Puraṃdara, that great sage / Dadhīci then swiftly brought about the cessation of his own life breaths.

16.32.s:
gatāsuṃ taṃ viditvaivaṃ vibudhāstatkalevaram.. māṃ
saśoṇitanirmuktaṃ kathaṃ kāryaṃ vyaciṃtayan .. 41 ..
16.32.d:
गतासुं तं विदित्वैवं विबुधास्तत्कलेवरम्.. मां
सशोणितनिर्मुक्तं कथं कार्यं व्यचिंतयन् .. 41 ..
16.32.m: Knowing him thus to be dead, the gods deliberated / on how his body should be made free of flesh and blood.

16.32.s:
tatastadasthiśuddhyarthamuvācedaṃ sureśvaraḥ ..
gaurīṇāṃ karkaśā jihvā tā etadutkhidaṃtviti .. 42 ..
16.32.d:
ततस्तदस्थिशुद्ध्यर्थमुवाचेदं सुरेश्वरः ..
गौरीणां कर्कशा जिह्वा ता एतदुत्खिदंत्विति .. 42 ..
16.32.m: Then, for the purification of those bones, the lord of the gods said this: / 'The tongues of white cows are rough; let them lick this away.'

16.32.s:
tatastairvibudhairnaṃdā yadā lokeṣu saṃsthitā..
dhyātā tadopayātā sā sakhībhiḥ parivāritā..43..
16.32.d:
ततस्तैर्विबुधैर्नंदा यदा लोकेषु संस्थिता..
ध्याता तदोपयाता सा सखीभिः परिवारिता..43..
16.32.m: Then, when Nandā, who resided in the worlds, was meditated upon / by those gods, she came forth surrounded by her companions.

16.32.s:
naṃdā subhadrā surabhiḥ suśīlā sumanāstathā..
iti gomātaraḥ paṃca golokācca samāgatāḥ..44..
16.32.d:
नंदा सुभद्रा सुरभिः सुशीला सुमनास्तथा..
इति गोमातरः पंच गोलोकाच्च समागताः..44..
16.32.m: Nandā, Subhadrā, Surabhi, Suśīlā, and Sumanas— / thus the five mother cows arrived from Goloka.

16.32.s:
ūcustānvibudhānsarvānasmābhiryatprayojanam..
karttavyaṃ tatkariṣyāmaḥ kathyatāṃ suvicāritam.. 45..
16.32.d:
ऊचुस्तान्विबुधान्सर्वानस्माभिर्यत्प्रयोजनम्..
कर्त्तव्यं तत्करिष्यामः कथ्यतां सुविचारितम्.. 45..
16.32.m: They said to all the gods: "Whatever task needs to be done by us, / we shall do it; tell us after considering well."

16.32.s:
devā ūcuḥ..
yadetadṛṣiṇā tyaktaṃ svayameva kalevaram..
etanmāṃsādinirmuktaṃ kriyatāmasthipaṃjaram..46..
16.32.d:
देवा ऊचुः..
यदेतदृषिणा त्यक्तं स्वयमेव कलेवरम्..
एतन्मांसादिनिर्मुक्तं क्रियतामस्थिपंजरम्..46..
16.32.m: The gods said: / "This corpse that has been abandoned voluntarily by the seer, / let it be stripped of flesh and the rest, and made into a skeleton of bones."

16.32.s:
tatkṛtvā garhitaṃ karma devādeśātsudāruṇam ..
punaḥ pitāmahaṃ draṣṭuṃ gatāstāḥ surasattamāḥ .. 47 ..
16.32.d:
तत्कृत्वा गर्हितं कर्म देवादेशात्सुदारुणम् ..
पुनः पितामहं द्रष्टुं गतास्ताः सुरसत्तमाः .. 47 ..
16.32.m: Having performed that terrible and blameworthy deed at the command of the gods, / they, the best of divine cows, went again to see Pitāmaha.

16.32.s:
tatastu dāruṇaṃ karma yacca tābhiranuṣṭhitam ..
pitāmahasya tatsarvaṃ samācakhyuryathātatham .. 48 ..
16.32.d:
ततस्तु दारुणं कर्म यच्च ताभिरनुष्ठितम् ..
पितामहस्य तत्सर्वं समाचख्युर्यथातथम् .. 48 ..
16.32.m: Then they accurately reported to Pitāmaha / all that terrible deed which had been carried out by them.

16.32.s:
tacchrutvā vibudhānsarvānsamāhūya pitāmahaḥ ..
sarvagātreṣvaspṛśata surabhīḥ śuddhikāmyayā .. 49 ..
16.32.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विबुधान्सर्वान्समाहूय पितामहः ..
सर्वगात्रेष्वस्पृशत सुरभीः शुद्धिकाम्यया .. 49 ..
16.32.m: Hearing that, Pitāmaha summoned all the gods / and touched the divine cows on all their limbs, wishing for their purification.

16.32.s:
tāstu tairvibudhaiḥ spṛṣṭāḥ supūtāḥ samavasthitāḥ ..
mukhamekaṃ paraṃ tāsāṃ na spṛṣṭamaśuci smṛtam .. 7.1.32.50 ..
16.32.d:
तास्तु तैर्विबुधैः स्पृष्टाः सुपूताः समवस्थिताः ..
मुखमेकं परं तासां न स्पृष्टमशुचि स्मृतम् .. 7.1.32.50 ..
16.32.m: Touched by those gods, they remained completely pure; / only their mouth was not touched, for it was remembered as impure.

16.32.s:
apavitraṃ bhavettāsāṃ mukhamekaṃ jugupsitam ..
śeṣaṃ śarīraṃ sarvāsāṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tu suraiḥ kṛtam .. 51 ..
16.32.d:
अपवित्रं भवेत्तासां मुखमेकं जुगुप्सितम् ..
शेषं शरीरं सर्वासां विशिष्टं तु सुरैः कृतम् .. 51 ..
16.32.m: Let their single mouth be impure and despised; / but the rest of their body was rendered superior by the gods.

16.32.s:
sarasvatyā tu tāḥ proktā bhavaṃtyo brahmaghātikāḥ ..
anyathā kāraṇātkasmānna spṛṣṭamamarairmukham .. 52 ..
16.32.d:
सरस्वत्या तु ताः प्रोक्ता भवंत्यो ब्रह्मघातिकाः ..
अन्यथा कारणात्कस्मान्न स्पृष्टममरैर्मुखम् .. 52 ..
16.32.m: Sarasvatī, however, said to them: "You are slayers of a brahmin! / Otherwise, for what reason was your mouth not touched by the immortals?"

16.32.s:
tatastābhistu sā proktā devī tatra sarasvatī ..
naitatte vacanaṃ yuktaṃ vaktumevaṃvidhaṃ mukham .. 53 ..
16.32.d:
ततस्ताभिस्तु सा प्रोक्ता देवी तत्र सरस्वती ..
नैतत्ते वचनं युक्तं वक्तुमेवंविधं मुखम् .. 53 ..
16.32.m: Then the goddess Sarasvatī was spoken to by them there: / "It is not proper for you to speak such words to our face.

16.32.s:
asmākameva hṛdayamanena vacasā tvayā ..
nirdagdhaṃ yena tasmāttvamacirāddāhamāpsyasi .. 54 ..
16.32.d:
अस्माकमेव हृदयमनेन वचसा त्वया ..
निर्दग्धं येन तस्मात्त्वमचिराद्दाहमाप्स्यसि .. 54 ..
16.32.m: Because our heart has been burned by you with this speech, / for that reason you shall soon suffer burning!"

16.32.s:
śāpaṃ dattvā tatastasyāḥ sarasvatyāstu tāstadā ..
golokaṃ gatavatyastu surabhyaḥ surapūjitāḥ .. 55 ..
16.32.d:
शापं दत्त्वा ततस्तस्याः सरस्वत्यास्तु तास्तदा ..
गोलोकं गतवत्यस्तु सुरभ्यः सुरपूजिताः .. 55 ..
16.32.m: Having thus pronounced a curse upon Sarasvatī, / those divine cows, worshipped by the gods, then went to Goloka.

16.32.s:
āhūya viśvakarmāṇaṃ takṣāṇaṃ surasattamāḥ ..
asmākaṃ kuru śastrāṇi tamāhuryuddhakāraṇāt .. 56 ..
16.32.d:
आहूय विश्वकर्माणं तक्षाणं सुरसत्तमाः ..
अस्माकं कुरु शस्त्राणि तमाहुर्युद्धकारणात् .. 56 ..
16.32.m: Summoning Viśvakarman the architect, the best of the gods / said to him: "Make weapons for us for the sake of battle."

16.32.s:
etadvacanamākarṇya tāni pūtairnavairdṛḍhaiḥ ...
astrāṇi kārayāmāsa dardhocerasthisaṃcayaiḥ .. 57 ..
16.32.d:
एतद्वचनमाकर्ण्य तानि पूतैर्नवैर्दृढैः ...
अस्त्राणि कारयामास दर्धोचेरस्थिसंचयैः .. 57 ..
16.32.m: Hearing this speech, he fashioned those weapons / from the purified, fresh, and solid collection of Dadhīca's bones.

16.32.s:
pramāṇākārayuktāni devānāṃ tāni saṃyuge ..
ajeyāni yathā cāsaṃstathā cāsau vinirmame ... .. 58 ..
16.32.d:
प्रमाणाकारयुक्तानि देवानां तानि संयुगे ..
अजेयानि यथा चासंस्तथा चासौ विनिर्ममे ... .. 58 ..
16.32.m: He crafted them endowed with the proper dimensions and forms / so that they would be invincible for the gods in battle.

16.32.s:
vajramiṃdrasya śaktiṃ ca vahnerdaṃḍaṃ yamasya ca ..
khaḍgaṃ tu niṛteḥ pāśaṃ samyakcakre pracetasaḥ ..59..
16.32.d:
वज्रमिंद्रस्य शक्तिं च वह्नेर्दंडं यमस्य च ..
खड्गं तु निऋतेः पाशं सम्यक्चक्रे प्रचेतसः ..59..
16.32.m: He made Indra's thunderbolt, Agni's spear, and Yama's staff, / Nirṛti's sword, and properly crafted the noose of Pracetas;

16.32.s:
vāyordhvajaṃ kuberasya gadāṃ gurvīṃ ca nirmame ..
viśvakarmā tathā śūlamīśānasya ca nirmame .. 7.1.32.60 ..
16.32.d:
वायोर्ध्वजं कुबेरस्य गदां गुर्वीं च निर्ममे ..
विश्वकर्मा तथा शूलमीशानस्य च निर्ममे .. 7.1.32.60 ..
16.32.m: He made Vāyu's banner, Kubera's heavy mace, / and Viśvakarman likewise fashioned Īśāna's trident.

16.32.s:
gṛhītvaitāni vai devāḥ śastrāṇyastrabalaṃ tadā ..
vijetuṃ ca tato daityāndānavāṃśca gatāstadā .. ... 61 ..
16.32.d:
गृहीत्वैतानि वै देवाः शस्त्राण्यस्त्रबलं तदा ..
विजेतुं च ततो दैत्यान्दानवांश्च गतास्तदा .. ... 61 ..
16.32.m: Taking up those weapons and the power of the missiles, / the gods then marched to conquer the Daityas and Dānavas.

16.32.s:
atrāṃtare subhadrāpi dadhīceraurdhvadaihikam ..
kṛtvā tairmunibhiḥ sārdhamanveṣṭuṃ sā gatā sutam .. 62 ..
16.32.d:
अत्रांतरे सुभद्रापि दधीचेरौर्ध्वदैहिकम् ..
कृत्वा तैर्मुनिभिः सार्धमन्वेष्टुं सा गता सुतम् .. 62 ..
16.32.m: Meanwhile, Subhadrā also, having performed Dadhīci's funeral rites / together with those sages, went to look for her son.

16.32.s:
aśvatthavāṭikāyāṃ ca tamapaśya nmanoramam ..
dṛṣṭvā roditi jīvaṃtaṃ muktvā bāṣpamathāciram .. 63 ..
16.32.d:
अश्वत्थवाटिकायां च तमपश्य न्मनोरमम् ..
दृष्ट्वा रोदिति जीवंतं मुक्त्वा बाष्पमथाचिरम् .. 63 ..
16.32.m: And she saw him looking charming in an aśvattha grove; / seeing him alive, she shed tears and wept immediately.

16.32.s:
aṃbetyābhāṣya tenoktā mā rodīstvaṃ yaśasvini ..
sarvaṃ purākṛtasyaitatphalaṃ tava mamāpi hi .. 64 ..
16.32.d:
अंबेत्याभाष्य तेनोक्ता मा रोदीस्त्वं यशस्विनि ..
सर्वं पुराकृतस्यैतत्फलं तव ममापि हि .. 64 ..
16.32.m: Addressing her with, "Mother!", he said to her: "Do not weep, illustrious lady! / All this is the fruit of past actions, both yours and mine.

16.32.s:
yadyathā yatra yeneha karma janmāṃtarārjitam ..
tadavaśyaṃ hi bhoktavyaṃ tyaja śokamato'khilam .. 65 ..
16.32.d:
यद्यथा यत्र येनेह कर्म जन्मांतरार्जितम् ..
तदवश्यं हि भोक्तव्यं त्यज शोकमतोऽखिलम् .. 65 ..
16.32.m: Whatever karma was earned in another birth, in whatever manner, wherever, and by whomever, / that must inevitably be experienced; therefore cast off all sorrow.

16.32.s:
matparityāgalajjā ca na te kāryeha sundari ..
phalaṃ purākṛtasyaitadbhoktavyaṃ tanmayāpi hi .. 66 ..
mātarmamopari kuru putrasnehaṃ yaśasvini ..
bālasya hi parityāgā nmātā doṣeṇa lipyate .. 57 ..
16.32.d:
मत्परित्यागलज्जा च न ते कार्येह सुन्दरि ..
फलं पुराकृतस्यैतद्भोक्तव्यं तन्मयापि हि .. 66 ..
मातर्ममोपरि कुरु पुत्रस्नेहं यशस्विनि ..
बालस्य हि परित्यागा न्माता दोषेण लिप्यते .. 57 ..
16.32.m:
You should not feel shame here at abandoning me, O beautiful lady; / this was the fruit of past deeds, which had to be experienced by me as well.
O mother, show a mother's affection toward me, O illustrious lady; / for a mother is tainted with sin by the abandonment of her child."

16.32.s:
bālenābhihitā sā tu dhyātvā devaṃ janārddanam ..
kṛtāṃjaliruvācedaṃ kathyatāṃ me suniścitam .. 68 ..
16.32.d:
बालेनाभिहिता सा तु ध्यात्वा देवं जनार्द्दनम् ..
कृतांजलिरुवाचेदं कथ्यतां मे सुनिश्चितम् .. 68 ..
16.32.m: Addressed by the child, she meditated upon the god Janārdana / and with joined palms spoke this: "Tell me with certainty:

16.32.s:
na vijānāmyahaṃ tathyaṃ kasyāyaṃ vīryasaṃbhavaḥ ..
tasmātkathaya deveśa mama te niścitaṃ vacaḥ .. 69 ..
16.32.d:
न विजानाम्यहं तथ्यं कस्यायं वीर्यसंभवः ..
तस्मात्कथय देवेश मम ते निश्चितं वचः .. 69 ..
16.32.m: I do not know the truth: from whose seed was he born? / Therefore, Lord of the gods, tell me your definitive word."

16.32.s:
āhokte mātaraṃ kṛṣṇaḥ subhadrāṃ vai janārddanaḥ ..
dadhīcestanayaścāyaṃ bhartuste kṣetrasaṃbhavaḥ .. 7.1.32.70 ..
16.32.d:
आहोक्ते मातरं कृष्णः सुभद्रां वै जनार्द्दनः ..
दधीचेस्तनयश्चायं भर्तुस्ते क्षेत्रसंभवः .. 7.1.32.70 ..
16.32.m: When this was spoken, Kṛṣṇa Janārdana said to the mother, Subhadrā: / "This is indeed the son of Dadhīci, born in your husband's field."

16.32.s:
tasyotpattiṃ viditvaivaṃ subhadrā hṛṣṭamānasā ..
bālamaṃke samāropya arodīdārtayā girā .. 71 ..
16.32.d:
तस्योत्पत्तिं विदित्वैवं सुभद्रा हृष्टमानसा ..
बालमंके समारोप्य अरोदीदार्तया गिरा .. 71 ..
16.32.m: Knowing his origin thus, Subhadrā, with a glad heart, / placed the child on her lap and wept with an anguished voice.

16.32.s:
āha bālaka utpannaḥ śokasya vada kāraṇam..
athoktaḥ stanyarahitaṃ kathaṃ te jīvitaṃ dhṛtam .. 72 ..
16.32.d:
आह बालक उत्पन्नः शोकस्य वद कारणम्..
अथोक्तः स्तन्यरहितं कथं ते जीवितं धृतम् .. 72 ..
16.32.m: The newborn boy said: "Tell me the cause of your sorrow." / Then she said: "Deprived of breastmilk, how did you sustain your life?

16.32.s:
yasmāccaturvidhā sṛṣṭirjīvānāṃ brahmaṇā kṛtā ..
jarāyujāṃḍajodbhijja svedajāśca tathā smṛtāḥ .. 73 ..
16.32.d:
यस्माच्चतुर्विधा सृष्टिर्जीवानां ब्रह्मणा कृता ..
जरायुजांडजोद्भिज्ज स्वेदजाश्च तथा स्मृताः .. 73 ..
16.32.m: For a fourfold creation of living beings was made by Brahmā; / they are remembered as womb-born, egg-born, plant-born, and sweat-born.

16.32.s:
narastrīnapuṃsakākhyāśca jātibhedā jarāyujāḥ ..
catuṣpadāśca paśavo grāmyāścāraṇyajāstathā .. 74 ..
16.32.d:
नरस्त्रीनपुंसकाख्याश्च जातिभेदा जरायुजाः ..
चतुष्पदाश्च पशवो ग्राम्याश्चारण्यजास्तथा .. 74 ..
16.32.m: The womb-born are classified into male, female, and neuter forms of species, / as well as four-footed beasts, both domestic and wild;

16.32.s:
aṇḍajāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarve mīnāḥ kūrmasarīsṛpāḥ ..
svedajā matkuṇā yūkā daṃśāśca maśakāstathā .. 75 ..
16.32.d:
अण्डजाः पक्षिणः सर्वे मीनाः कूर्मसरीसृपाः ..
स्वेदजा मत्कुणा यूका दंशाश्च मशकास्तथा .. 75 ..
16.32.m: The egg-born are all birds, fish, turtles, and reptiles; / the sweat-born are bugs, lice, stinging flies, and gnats;

16.32.s:
udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ proktāstṛṇagulmalatā dayaḥ ..
anye'pyevaṃ yathāyogamaṃtarbhūtāḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 76 ..
16.32.d:
उद्भिज्जाः स्थावराः प्रोक्तास्तृणगुल्मलता दयः ..
अन्येऽप्येवं यथायोगमंतर्भूताः सहस्रशः .. 76 ..
16.32.m: The plant-born are said to be immovable things: grasses, shrubs, creepers, and the rest; / and thousands of others are included appropriately in this way.

16.32.s:
aṇḍajāḥ pakṣapātena jīvaṃti śiśavo bhuvi ..
ūṣmaṇā svedajāḥ sarve udbhijjāḥ salilena hi .. 77 ..
16.32.d:
अण्डजाः पक्षपातेन जीवंति शिशवो भुवि ..
ऊष्मणा स्वेदजाः सर्वे उद्भिज्जाः सलिलेन हि .. 77 ..
16.32.m: The offspring of egg-born creatures live on earth by the brooding of wings; / all sweat-born live by warmth, and the plant-born indeed by water.

16.32.s:
samudāyena bhūtānāṃ pañcānāmudbhijaṃ bhuvi ..
jarāyujāśca stanyena vinā jīvitumakṣamāḥ .. 78 ..
16.32.d:
समुदायेन भूतानां पञ्चानामुद्भिजं भुवि ..
जरायुजाश्च स्तन्येन विना जीवितुमक्षमाः .. 78 ..
16.32.m: The plant-born on earth live through the aggregation of the five elements, / and the womb-born are unable to live without breastmilk.

16.32.s:
vinā tena kathaṃ putra tvayā prāṇā vidhāritāḥ ..
tāṃ tathā jananīṃ prāha sa ca bāṣpāvilekṣaṇām..79..
16.32.d:
विना तेन कथं पुत्र त्वया प्राणा विधारिताः ..
तां तथा जननीं प्राह स च बाष्पाविलेक्षणाम्..79..
16.32.m: Without that, O son, how were your vital breaths preserved?" / And he spoke to that mother whose eyes were filled with tears:

16.32.s:
aśvatthaphalaniryāsapānātprāṇā mayā dhṛtāḥ ..
gauṇaṃ tadā tayā tasya pippalādeti kalpitam ..7.1.32.80..
nāma tena jagatyasminnityaṃ khyātaṃ mahātmanaḥ ..
tatrasthairmunibhistasya kṛtāḥ sarvairyathākramam ..81..
16.32.d:
अश्वत्थफलनिर्यासपानात्प्राणा मया धृताः ..
गौणं तदा तया तस्य पिप्पलादेति कल्पितम् ..7.1.32.80..
नाम तेन जगत्यस्मिन्नित्यं ख्यातं महात्मनः ..
तत्रस्थैर्मुनिभिस्तस्य कृताः सर्वैर्यथाक्रमम् ..81..
16.32.m: "My vital breaths were sustained by drinking the sap of the fruits of the aśvattha tree." / Then a descriptive name, Pippalāda, was given to him by her, / by which name that great soul is forever famous in this world. / By all the sages residing there, in proper sequence,

16.32.s:
saṃskārāḥ pippalādasya vedoktā veda pāragaiḥ..
ṣaḍaṃgopāṃgasaṃyuktā vedāstena samuddhṛtāḥ ..
tadāśramanivāsibhyo munibhyaśca supuṣkalāḥ ..82..
16.32.d:
संस्काराः पिप्पलादस्य वेदोक्ता वेद पारगैः..
षडंगोपांगसंयुक्ता वेदास्तेन समुद्धृताः ..
तदाश्रमनिवासिभ्यो मुनिभ्यश्च सुपुष्कलाः ..82..
16.32.m: the life-cycle rituals of Pippalāda were performed as prescribed by the Vedas by those who had crossed to the other shore of the Vedas. / The Vedas with their six limbs and secondary limbs were comprehensively preserved by him / and abundantly taught to the sages dwelling in that hermitage.

16.32.s:
punastatra sthitaścāsau dṛṣṭvā munikumārakān..
svapitraṃkagatānprāha jananīṃ tāṃ śucismitām ..83..
16.32.d:
पुनस्तत्र स्थितश्चासौ दृष्ट्वा मुनिकुमारकान्..
स्वपित्रंकगतान्प्राह जननीं तां शुचिस्मिताम् ..83..
16.32.m: Remaining there, seeing the sons of the sages / sitting on their fathers' laps, he said to that mother of bright smiles:

16.32.s:
pitā me kutra bhadraṃ te subhadre kathaya sphuṭam ..
tadekāṃtasthito yena bālakrīḍāṃ karomyaham .. .. 84 ..
16.32.d:
पिता मे कुत्र भद्रं ते सुभद्रे कथय स्फुटम् ..
तदेकांतस्थितो येन बालक्रीडां करोम्यहम् .. .. 84 ..
16.32.m: "Where is my father, Subhadrā? May you be blessed, tell me clearly, / so that, sitting by his side in private, I may play childhood games."

16.32.s:
evaṃ sā jananī tena yadā pṛṣṭā tapasvinī ..
tadā roditumārabdhā nottaraṃ kiñcidabravīt .. 85 ..
16.32.d:
एवं सा जननी तेन यदा पृष्टा तपस्विनी ..
तदा रोदितुमारब्धा नोत्तरं किञ्चिदब्रवीत् .. 85 ..
16.32.m: When that ascetic mother was questioned in this way by him, / she then began to weep and spoke no answer at all.

16.32.s:
rudantīṃ tāṃ samālokya kuddho'sau munidārakaḥ ..
kimasau kutsitaḥ kaścidyena nākhyāsi taṃ mama .. 86 ..
16.32.d:
रुदन्तीं तां समालोक्य कुद्धोऽसौ मुनिदारकः ..
किमसौ कुत्सितः कश्चिद्येन नाख्यासि तं मम .. 86 ..
16.32.m: Beholding her weeping, the sage's boy became angry: / "Is he some despicable person, that you do not reveal him to me?"

16.32.s:
ityukte sutamāhaivaṃ vibudhaiste pitā hataḥ ..
kopaṃ tyajasva bhadraṃ te dadhīciḥ kathito mayā ..87..
16.32.d:
इत्युक्ते सुतमाहैवं विबुधैस्ते पिता हतः ..
कोपं त्यजस्व भद्रं ते दधीचिः कथितो मया ..87..
16.32.m: When this was said, she spoke thus to her son: "Your father was killed by the gods. / Renounce your anger, may you be blessed; Dadhīci was spoken of by me."

16.32.s:
kopavahnipradīptātmā prāha tāṃ jananīṃ punaḥ ..
kimapakṛtaṃ surāṇāṃ matpitrā kathayasva tat ..88..
16.32.d:
कोपवह्निप्रदीप्तात्मा प्राह तां जननीं पुनः ..
किमपकृतं सुराणां मत्पित्रा कथयस्व तत् ..88..
16.32.m: His self ablaze with the fire of anger, he spoke to his mother again: / "What harm was done to the gods by my father? Tell me that!"

16.32.s:
.. subhadrovāca .. ..
śastrāṇāṃ kāraṇānmūḍhairhato'sau munipuṃgavaḥ ..
prayacchannapi cānyāni tadākārāṇi suvrata .. 89 ..
16.32.d:
.. सुभद्रोवाच .. ..
शस्त्राणां कारणान्मूढैर्हतोऽसौ मुनिपुंगवः ..
प्रयच्छन्नपि चान्यानि तदाकाराणि सुव्रत .. 89 ..
16.32.m:
Subhadrā said:
That best of sages was slain by the foolish ones for the sake of weapons, / even though he offered them others of the same form, O one of noble vows.

16.32.s:
śrutvaitadvacanaṃ so'pi munirugratapāstadā ..
pitā me yo hato devaisteṣāṃ kṛtyāṃ mahābalām .. 7.1.32.90 ..
16.32.d:
श्रुत्वैतद्वचनं सोऽपि मुनिरुग्रतपास्तदा ..
पिता मे यो हतो देवैस्तेषां कृत्यां महाबलाम् .. 7.1.32.90 ..
16.32.m: Having heard those words, that sage of fierce austerities then [thought]: / "Because my father was slain by the gods, [I will summon] a mighty kṛtyā against them;

16.32.s:
utthāpya pātayiṣyāmi mūrddhni prāṇāpahārikām ..
pitāmahamahaṃ muktvā naiva hanyo bhavedyadi .. 91 ..
16.32.d:
उत्थाप्य पातयिष्यामि मूर्द्ध्नि प्राणापहारिकाम् ..
पितामहमहं मुक्त्वा नैव हन्यो भवेद्यदि .. 91 ..
16.32.m: raising her up, I will hurl her down upon their heads, depriving them of life. / Excepting Grandfather [Brahmā], if there be none who should be slain,

16.32.s:
anyānpramathayiṣyāmi kṛtyāśastreṇa saṃgatān ..
śaraṇaṃ yadi yāsyaṃti gīrvāṇā madbhayāturāḥ ..
tathāpi pātayiṣyāmi tenaiva saha saṃgatān .. 92 ..
16.32.d:
अन्यान्प्रमथयिष्यामि कृत्याशस्त्रेण संगतान् ..
शरणं यदि यास्यंति गीर्वाणा मद्भयातुराः ..
तथापि पातयिष्यामि तेनैव सह संगतान् .. 92 ..
16.32.m: I will crush the others joined [with them] by means of the weapon of the kṛtyā. / If the gods, terrified through fear of me, go for refuge, / even so I will strike them down along with him [they resort to]."

16.32.s:
matvaivaṃ tamṛṣiṃ kuddhaṃ sarve te surasattamāḥ ..
brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptā bhayena mahatā'rdditāḥ .. 93 ..
16.32.d:
मत्वैवं तमृषिं कुद्धं सर्वे ते सुरसत्तमाः ..
ब्रह्माणं शरणं प्राप्ता भयेन महताऽर्द्दिताः .. 93 ..
16.32.m: Knowing that the seer was enraged in this way, all those foremost gods, / afflicted by great fear, sought refuge with Brahmā.

16.32.s:
tāṃstasya śaraṇaṃ prāptāñjñātvā devaḥ kṛpānvitaḥ ...
tatraiva gatvā tvaritaṃ prāha devāñjanārddanaḥ .. 94 ..
16.32.d:
तांस्तस्य शरणं प्राप्ताञ्ज्ञात्वा देवः कृपान्वितः ...
तत्रैव गत्वा त्वरितं प्राह देवाञ्जनार्द्दनः .. 94 ..
16.32.m: Knowing that they had sought his refuge, the compassionate god, / Janārdana, having gone swiftly to that very place, spoke to the gods:

16.32.s:
bhavatāṃ rakṣaṇopāyaściṃtito'tra mayā'dhunā ..
tena tāṃ mohayiṣyāmi kṛtyāṃ haṃtumupasthitām ..95...
16.32.d:
भवतां रक्षणोपायश्चिंतितोऽत्र मयाऽधुना ..
तेन तां मोहयिष्यामि कृत्यां हंतुमुपस्थिताम् ..95...
16.32.m: "A means to protect you has now been devised here by me; / by it I will delude that kṛtyā who has arrived to slay."

16.32.s:
atrāṃtare pippalādaḥ piturvairamanusmaran ..
haṃtuṃ surānvyavasitaḥ praviveśa himācalam .. 96 ..
16.32.d:
अत्रांतरे पिप्पलादः पितुर्वैरमनुस्मरन् ..
हंतुं सुरान्व्यवसितः प्रविवेश हिमाचलम् .. 96 ..
16.32.m: Meanwhile, Pippalāda, remembering the hostility against his father, / determined to slay the gods, entered the Himālayas.

16.32.s:
śrutvā tadapriyaṃ vākyaṃ māturvaktrādvinirgatam ..
pippalādaḥ punaryātastasmātsthānāddhimācalam .. 97 ..
16.32.d:
श्रुत्वा तदप्रियं वाक्यं मातुर्वक्त्राद्विनिर्गतम् ..
पिप्पलादः पुनर्यातस्तस्मात्स्थानाद्धिमाचलम् .. 97 ..
16.32.m: Having heard those unpleasant words coming from his mother's mouth, / Pippalāda went once again from that place to the Himālayas.

16.32.s:
svargasopānavatpuṃsāṃ sthalībhūtamivāṃbaram ..
śeṣasyābhogasaṃkāśaṃ prāpto'sau tuhinācalam .. 98 ..
16.32.d:
स्वर्गसोपानवत्पुंसां स्थलीभूतमिवांबरम् ..
शेषस्याभोगसंकाशं प्राप्तोऽसौ तुहिनाचलम् .. 98 ..
16.32.m: Like a staircase to heaven for men, as though the sky had become solid ground, / resembling the coil of Śeṣa, he reached the mountain of snow.

16.32.s:
pratijñāṃ kurute yatra sthitaḥ sthāṇurivācalaḥ ..
haṃtāro ye mama pitustānhaniṣyāmi cāraṇāt .. 99 ..
16.32.d:
प्रतिज्ञां कुरुते यत्र स्थितः स्थाणुरिवाचलः ..
हंतारो ये मम पितुस्तान्हनिष्यामि चारणात् .. 99 ..
16.32.m: Remaining there, unmoving like a tree-trunk, he made a vow: / "I will swiftly slay those who are the slayers of my father,

16.32.s:
kṛtyāśastreṇa sakalānamaratvena garvitān ..
tasminsthitaḥ prakupitaḥ śivāyatanasaṃsadi .. 7.1.32.100 ..
16.32.d:
कृत्याशस्त्रेण सकलानमरत्वेन गर्वितान् ..
तस्मिन्स्थितः प्रकुपितः शिवायतनसंसदि .. 7.1.32.100 ..
16.32.m: all who are proud of their immortality, with the weapon of a kṛtyā." / Remaining there, enraged, in the precinct of the sanctuary of Śiva,

16.32.s:
atrasthaḥ sādhayiṣyāmi tāṃ kṛtyāṃ ciṃtayanhṛdi ..
kṛtyāṃ vā sādhayiṣyāmi yāsye vā yamasādanam .. 101 ..
16.32.d:
अत्रस्थः साधयिष्यामि तां कृत्यां चिंतयन्हृदि ..
कृत्यां वा साधयिष्यामि यास्ये वा यमसादनम् .. 101 ..
16.32.m: he thought in his heart: "Standing here, I will accomplish that kṛtyā; / I will either accomplish the kṛtyā or go to the realm of Yama.

16.32.s:
nirdvandvo nirbhayo bhūtvā nirāhāro hyaharniśam ..
savyena pāṇinā savyaṃ nirmathyorumahaṃ punaḥ .. 102 ..
16.32.d:
निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्भयो भूत्वा निराहारो ह्यहर्निशम् ..
सव्येन पाणिना सव्यं निर्मथ्योरुमहं पुनः .. 102 ..
16.32.m: Free from duality, fearless, taking no food day and night, / continuously churning my left thigh with my left hand,

16.32.s:
tasmādutpādayiṣyāmi mahākṛtyāmiti sthitaḥ ..
saṃvatsare tasya gate ūrugātrādviniḥsṛtā .. 103 ..
16.32.d:
तस्मादुत्पादयिष्यामि महाकृत्यामिति स्थितः ..
संवत्सरे तस्य गते ऊरुगात्राद्विनिःसृता .. 103 ..
16.32.m: I will produce from it a great kṛtyā." Resolved thus, he stood. / When a year had passed for him, there emerged from the limb of his thigh

16.32.s:
vaḍavā gurubhārārttā vāḍavenānvitā tadā ..
ūro rnirgatya sā tasmātsuṣuve sumahābalam ..104..
16.32.d:
वडवा गुरुभारार्त्ता वाडवेनान्विता तदा ..
ऊरो र्निर्गत्य सा तस्मात्सुषुवे सुमहाबलम् ..104..
16.32.m: a mare, afflicted by a heavy burden, accompanied then by the submarine fire. / Having emerged from that thigh, she gave birth to one of very great strength.

16.32.s:
vaḍavā svodarādgarbhaṃ jvālāmālāsamākulam ..
vimucya tamṛṣestasya puro garbhaṃ samujjavalam ..105..
16.32.d:
वडवा स्वोदराद्गर्भं ज्वालामालासमाकुलम् ..
विमुच्य तमृषेस्तस्य पुरो गर्भं समुज्जवलम् ..105..
16.32.m: The mare released the embryo, filled with wreaths of flames, / from her belly—that blazing embryo—before the seer.

16.32.s:
punargatā kvāpi tadā na jñātā muninā hi sā ..
vaḍavānalo narastasyāḥ sa garbho niḥsṛtastadā ..106..
16.32.d:
पुनर्गता क्वापि तदा न ज्ञाता मुनिना हि सा ..
वडवानलो नरस्तस्याः स गर्भो निःसृतस्तदा ..106..
16.32.m: Then she departed somewhere again, nor was she known [further] by the sage. / He was the submarine fire in human form; that embryo emerged then,

16.32.s:
kalpāṃta iva bhūtānāṃ kālāgniriva varcasā ..
vidyutpuñjapratīkāśaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā purataḥ sthitam .. 107 ..
16.32.d:
कल्पांत इव भूतानां कालाग्निरिव वर्चसा ..
विद्युत्पुञ्जप्रतीकाशं तं दृष्ट्वा पुरतः स्थितम् .. 107 ..
16.32.m: resembling the fire of time at the end of the world-age for all creatures in brilliance, / like a mass of lightning. Seeing him standing before him,

16.32.s:
sa cāpi vismito'tyaṃtaṃ kimetaditi ciṃtayan ..
tatastena puraḥsthena vāḍavena ca vahninā .. .. 108 ..
16.32.d:
स चापि विस्मितोऽत्यंतं किमेतदिति चिंतयन् ..
ततस्तेन पुरःस्थेन वाडवेन च वह्निना .. .. 108 ..
16.32.m: he too was greatly astonished, thinking, "What is this?" / Then, by that submarine fire standing before him,

16.32.s:
ṛṣiḥ proktaḥ pippalādaḥ sādhito'haṃ tvayā balāt ..
idānīṃ te mayā kāryaṃ karttavyaṃ yatsamāhitam .. 109 ..
16.32.d:
ऋषिः प्रोक्तः पिप्पलादः साधितोऽहं त्वया बलात् ..
इदानीं ते मया कार्यं कर्त्तव्यं यत्समाहितम् .. 109 ..
16.32.m: the seer Pippalāda was addressed: "I have been accomplished by you through force; / now I must perform the deed that you desire.

16.32.s:
kariṣyāmīha tatsarvama sādhyamapi sādhyatām ..
svoruṃ nirmathya janito yena saṃvatsarādaham ..
tātoruṇā vihīno'pi kariṣye tvatsamīhitam .. 7.1.32.110 ..
16.32.d:
करिष्यामीह तत्सर्वम साध्यमपि साध्यताम् ..
स्वोरुं निर्मथ्य जनितो येन संवत्सरादहम् ..
तातोरुणा विहीनोऽपि करिष्ये त्वत्समीहितम् .. 7.1.32.110 ..
16.32.m: I will accomplish all of that here; even the impossible shall become possible. / Since I was born after a year by your churning your own thigh, / though devoid of a father's thigh, I will fulfill your wish."

16.32.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya muniḥ kopasamanvitaḥ ..
provāca vibudhānsarvānmaddattānbhakṣaya svayam .. 111 ..
16.32.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य मुनिः कोपसमन्वितः ..
प्रोवाच विबुधान्सर्वान्मद्दत्तान्भक्षय स्वयम् .. 111 ..
16.32.m: Having heard those words of his, the sage, filled with wrath, / said: "Devour yourself all the gods that are delivered by me!"

16.32.s:
piturvadhātkrodhakṛtāvadhānaṃ matvā surā raudramatīva ghoram ..
sametya sarve puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ samāśritāste sahasā sabhāryāḥ .. 112 ..
16.32.d:
पितुर्वधात्क्रोधकृतावधानं मत्वा सुरा रौद्रमतीव घोरम् ..
समेत्य सर्वे पुरुषं पुराणं समाश्रितास्ते सहसा सभार्याः .. 112 ..
16.32.m: Perceiving him focused on wrath because of his father's slaying, exceedingly dreadful and terrible, / all the gods, having assembled with their wives, hastily took refuge with the Primeval Person.

16.32.s:
sa tānsamāśvāsya surānvariṣṭhaṃ kopānalaṃ tatra yayau prahṛṣṭaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ vai ravipuṃjakāśamuvāca viṣṇurvacanaṃ variṣṭham .. 113 ..
16.32.d:
स तान्समाश्वास्य सुरान्वरिष्ठं कोपानलं तत्र ययौ प्रहृष्टः ..
दृष्ट्वा च तं वै रविपुंजकाशमुवाच विष्णुर्वचनं वरिष्ठम् .. 113 ..
16.32.m: Having consoled those gods, delighted, he went there to the foremost fire of wrath; / and seeing him who shone like a cluster of suns, Viṣṇu spoke these most excellent words:

16.32.s:
ahaṃ sureśāna tavaiva pārśvaṃ visarjito jātabhayaiśca devaiḥ ..
mattaḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ vacanaṃ hi pathyaṃ yaccāraṇānāṃ bhavato'pi pathyam .. 114 ..
16.32.d:
अहं सुरेशान तवैव पार्श्वं विसर्जितो जातभयैश्च देवैः ..
मत्तः शृणु त्वं वचनं हि पथ्यं यच्चारणानां भवतोऽपि पथ्यम् .. 114 ..
16.32.m: "O Lord of the gods, I have been dispatched to your presence by the gods who have become fearful. / Listen from me to words that are wholesome—wholesome for the celestial bards and for you as well.

16.32.s:
jñātaṃ balaṃ te vibudhairaciṃtyaṃ vināśanaṃ cātmavatāṃ hyavaśyam ..
evaṃ sthite kuru vākyaṃ surāṇāmekaikamaddhi prativāsaraṃ tvam .. 115 ..
16.32.d:
ज्ञातं बलं ते विबुधैरचिंत्यं विनाशनं चात्मवतां ह्यवश्यम् ..
एवं स्थिते कुरु वाक्यं सुराणामेकैकमद्धि प्रतिवासरं त्वम् .. 115 ..
16.32.m: Your power, inconceivable and the inevitable destruction of embodied beings, is known to the gods; / such being the case, follow the advice regarding the gods: devour [them] one by one each day.

16.32.s:
mukhyānāṃ koṭayastriṃśatsurāṇāṃ balaśālinām ..
kathaṃ tu bhakṣaṇaṃ teṣāṃ yugapattvaṃ kariṣyasi .. 116 ..
16.32.d:
मुख्यानां कोटयस्त्रिंशत्सुराणां बलशालिनाम् ..
कथं तु भक्षणं तेषां युगपत्त्वं करिष्यसि .. 116 ..
16.32.m: There are thirty crores of chief, mighty gods; / how will you devour them all at once?

16.32.s:
tasmādekaikaśasteṣāṃ karttavyaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ tvayā ..
naikena bhavatā śakyā vidhātuṃ bhakṣaṇakriyā .. 117 ..
16.32.d:
तस्मादेकैकशस्तेषां कर्त्तव्यं भक्षणं त्वया ..
नैकेन भवता शक्या विधातुं भक्षणक्रिया .. 117 ..
16.32.m: Therefore, the devouring of them should be done by you one by one. / It is not possible for you alone to carry out the act of devouring all at once.

16.32.s:
tathā ca pāṃḍurogitvaṃ hutabhukprāptavānpurā ..
atibhakṣaṇaṃ na yuktaṃ tasmātkuru matiṃ mama .. 118 ..
16.32.d:
तथा च पांडुरोगित्वं हुतभुक्प्राप्तवान्पुरा ..
अतिभक्षणं न युक्तं तस्मात्कुरु मतिं मम .. 118 ..
16.32.m: Moreover, the Consumer of Offerings [Fire] contracted jaundice in ancient times; / excessive eating is not proper; therefore, follow my counsel.

16.32.s:
tathā ca yugapatteṣu bhakṣiteṣu punastvayā ..
pratyahaṃ bhakṣaṇopāyaściṃtitavyo bubhukṣayā .. 119 ..
saphalaiva pratijñā te nānṛtaṃ munibhāṣitam ..
evaṃ kṛte'pi te sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati samīhitam ..7.1.32.12....
16.32.d:
तथा च युगपत्तेषु भक्षितेषु पुनस्त्वया ..
प्रत्यहं भक्षणोपायश्चिंतितव्यो बुभुक्षया .. 119 ..
सफलैव प्रतिज्ञा ते नानृतं मुनिभाषितम् ..
एवं कृतेऽपि ते सर्वं भविष्यति समीहितम् ..7.1.32.12....
16.32.m:
Furthermore, if they are devoured all at once by you, / a means of eating will have to be thought of every day due to hunger.
Your vow will indeed be fruitful; what was spoken by the sage will not be false; / even when this is done, all your desires will come to pass."

16.32.s:
tatkariṣyāyahaṃ sarvamāhaivaṃ sa janārdanaḥ ..
ekaikaśaḥ sa vibudhānbhakṣayiṣyati vāḍavaḥ .. 121 ..
16.32.d:
तत्करिष्यायहं सर्वमाहैवं स जनार्दनः ..
एकैकशः स विबुधान्भक्षयिष्यति वाडवः .. 121 ..
16.32.m: "I will do all that," said Janārdana; / "that submarine fire will devour the gods one by one."

16.32.s:
tataḥ surāḥ sureśānaṃ taṃ viṣṇumamitaujasam ..
praṇamyāhuryathāyuktaṃ śobhanaṃ bhavatā kṛtam .. 122 ..
16.32.d:
ततः सुराः सुरेशानं तं विष्णुममितौजसम् ..
प्रणम्याहुर्यथायुक्तं शोभनं भवता कृतम् .. 122 ..
16.32.m: Then the gods, having bowed to Viṣṇu, the lord of gods, of immeasurable splendor, / said: "What was fitting has been done well by you.

16.32.s:
bhūyo'dya punarevāsya doṣasyopaśamakriyām ..
kartuṃ tvameva śakto'si nānyastrātā divauka sām.. 123 ..
16.32.d:
भूयोऽद्य पुनरेवास्य दोषस्योपशमक्रियाम् ..
कर्तुं त्वमेव शक्तोऽसि नान्यस्त्राता दिवौक साम्.. 123 ..
16.32.m: Again today, you alone are capable of performing the act of pacifying this fault; / there is no other protector for the dwellers of heaven."

16.32.s:
tataḥ pītāṃbaradharaḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ ..
yuṣmadbhayaṃ hariṣyāmi tatsurānāha mādhavaḥ .. 124 ..
16.32.d:
ततः पीतांबरधरः शंखचक्रगदाधरः ..
युष्मद्भयं हरिष्यामि तत्सुरानाह माधवः .. 124 ..
16.32.m: Then Mādhava, who wears yellow garments and holds the conch, discus, and mace, / spoke to the gods: "I will remove your fear."

16.32.s: śrutvaitadvibudhāḥ sarve harṣeṇotphulla locanāḥ .. 125 ..
16.32.d: श्रुत्वैतद्विबुधाः सर्वे हर्षेणोत्फुल्ल लोचनाः .. 125 ..
16.32.m: Having heard this, all the gods had their eyes wide open with joy.

16.32.s:
tatastānvibudhāndṛṣṭvā provāca sa tu vāḍavaḥ ..
kimidānīṃ mayā kāryaṃ bhavatāṃ kathyatāṃ hi tat .. 126 ..
16.32.d:
ततस्तान्विबुधान्दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच स तु वाडवः ..
किमिदानीं मया कार्यं भवतां कथ्यतां हि तत् .. 126 ..
16.32.m: Then, seeing those gods, the submarine fire spoke: / "What deed must now be done by me for you? Let that be spoken!"

16.32.s:
atrāntare viśvatanurmahaujā vimohayaṃstaṃ jvalanaṃ svabuddhyā ..
provāca pūrvaṃ vihitā yadāpastā bhakṣayasveti mahānubhāvaḥ .. 127 ..
16.32.d:
अत्रान्तरे विश्वतनुर्महौजा विमोहयंस्तं ज्वलनं स्वबुद्ध्या ..
प्रोवाच पूर्वं विहिता यदापस्ता भक्षयस्वेति महानुभावः .. 127 ..
16.32.m: Meanwhile, the glorious one possessing the universe as his form and endowed with great energy, deluding that fire with his intellect, / spoke: "Devour the waters that were created first!"

16.32.s:
etadvyavasitaṃ viṣṇoryaḥ śṛṇoti samāhitaḥ ..
so'ticārabhayānmukto jñānaṃ muktimavāpnuyāt .. 128 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye vaḍavānalavaṃcanavṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāma dvātriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 32 .. .. ..
16.32.d:
एतद्व्यवसितं विष्णोर्यः शृणोति समाहितः ..
सोऽतिचारभयान्मुक्तो ज्ञानं मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् .. 128 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वडवानलवंचनवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनाम द्वात्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 32 .. .. ..
16.32.m:
Whoever, with a concentrated mind, listens to this resolve of Viṣṇu, / is freed from the fear of transgression and attains knowledge and liberation.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, named 'Description of the Episode of the Deception of the Submarine Fire', in the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, the first [part] of the seventh Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

16.33.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
piturvadhāmarṣasujāta manyunā yadyatkṛtaṃ karma purā maharṣiṇā ..
dadhīciputreṇa suraprasādhinā sarvaṃ śrutaṃ taddhi mayā samādhinā .. 1 ..
16.33.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
पितुर्वधामर्षसुजात मन्युना यद्यत्कृतं कर्म पुरा महर्षिणा ..
दधीचिपुत्रेण सुरप्रसाधिना सर्वं श्रुतं तद्धि मया समाधिना .. 1 ..
16.33.m:
The Goddess said:
Whatever deed was done of old by the great seer, born of wrath and indignation at his father's slaying, / that son of Dadhīci who subdued the gods—all that I have indeed heard through absorption.

16.33.s:
punaḥpunarvai vibudhaiḥ samānaṃ yadvṛttamāsītkimapi pradhānam ..
kāryaṃ hi tatsarvamanukrameṇa vijñātumicchāmi kutūhalena .. 2 ..
16.33.d:
पुनःपुनर्वै विबुधैः समानं यद्वृत्तमासीत्किमपि प्रधानम् ..
कार्यं हि तत्सर्वमनुक्रमेण विज्ञातुमिच्छामि कुतूहलेन .. 2 ..
16.33.m: Whatever chief task repeatedly occurred that was fitting for the gods, / all that I wish to know in proper order out of curiosity.

16.33.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
ukto yadāsau vibudhaiḥ samastairāpaḥ purā tvaṃ bhuvi bhakṣayasva ..
yato'marāṇāṃ prathamaṃ hi jātā āpo'grajāḥ sarvasurāsurebhyaḥ .. 3 ..
16.33.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
उक्तो यदासौ विबुधैः समस्तैरापः पुरा त्वं भुवि भक्षयस्व ..
यतोऽमराणां प्रथमं हि जाता आपोऽग्रजाः सर्वसुरासुरेभ्यः .. 3 ..
16.33.m:
Īśvara said:
When he was told of old by all the gods: "Devour the waters on the earth, / since the waters were born first of the immortals, the firstborn of all gods and asuras";

16.33.s:
tenaivamuktastu mahātmanā tadā pradarśayadhvaṃ mama tā yataḥ sthitāḥ ..
pītvā surāḥ sarvamahaṃ purastātkṛtyaṃ kariṣye surabhakṣaṇaṃ hi .. 4 ..
16.33.d:
तेनैवमुक्तस्तु महात्मना तदा प्रदर्शयध्वं मम ता यतः स्थिताः ..
पीत्वा सुराः सर्वमहं पुरस्तात्कृत्यं करिष्ये सुरभक्षणं हि .. 4 ..
16.33.m: addressed thus by the great-souled one, he then [said]: "Show me where they abide. / Having drunk them, O gods, I shall afterwards accomplish the deed: the consumption of the gods.

16.33.s:
tatrāpi netuṃ yadi māṃ samarthā yatrāsate vāricayāḥ sametāḥ ..
ato'nyathā nāhamalīkavādī prāṇe prayāte munivākyakārī .. 5 ..
16.33.d:
तत्रापि नेतुं यदि मां समर्था यत्रासते वारिचयाः समेताः ..
अतोऽन्यथा नाहमलीकवादी प्राणे प्रयाते मुनिवाक्यकारी .. 5 ..
16.33.m: If you are able to lead me thither, where the collected waters reside; / otherwise I, who do not speak falsehood and obey the sage's words, [will do so] even as life departs."

16.33.s:
āhokte puṃḍarīkākṣa aurvaṃ hi vāḍavaṃ tadā ..
tvāṃ prāpayiṣye yatrāpaḥ kena yānena vāḍava .. 6 ..
16.33.d:
आहोक्ते पुंडरीकाक्ष और्वं हि वाडवं तदा ..
त्वां प्रापयिष्ये यत्रापः केन यानेन वाडव .. 6 ..
16.33.m: When that was spoken, the lotus-eyed one then said to Aurva, the submarine fire: / "I will bring you to where the waters are. By what conveyance, O submarine fire [will you go]?"

16.33.s:
.. vāḍava uvāca .. ..
nāhaṃ hayādibhiryānairgaṃtuṃ tatra samutsahe ..
kumārīkarasaṃparkamekaṃ muktvā mataṃ hi me .. 7 ..
16.33.d:
.. वाडव उवाच .. ..
नाहं हयादिभिर्यानैर्गंतुं तत्र समुत्सहे ..
कुमारीकरसंपर्कमेकं मुक्त्वा मतं हि मे .. 7 ..
16.33.m:
The submarine fire said:
"I cannot bear to go thither on conveyances such as horses; / my resolved desire is only the touch of a maiden's hand."

16.33.s:
.. viṣṇuruvāca .. ..
etatte sulabhaṃ yānaṃ tāṃ kanyāmānayāmyaham ..
yā tvāṃ netuṃ samarthā syādapāṃ sthānaṃ suniścitam .. 8 ..
16.33.d:
.. विष्णुरुवाच .. ..
एतत्ते सुलभं यानं तां कन्यामानयाम्यहम् ..
या त्वां नेतुं समर्था स्यादपां स्थानं सुनिश्चितम् .. 8 ..
16.33.m:
Viṣṇu said:
"That conveyance is easily obtained by you. I shall bring that maiden / who will certainly be able to carry you to the abode of the waters."

16.33.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
surabhīśāpasaṃtaptā prāgupāttadaśāphalā ..
sarasvatī yānabhūtā tasya sā viṣṇunā kṛtā .. 9 ..
16.33.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
सुरभीशापसंतप्ता प्रागुपात्तदशाफला ..
सरस्वती यानभूता तस्य सा विष्णुना कृता .. 9 ..
16.33.m:
Īśvara said:
Afflicted by the curse of Surabhi, experiencing the fruit of a condition acquired previously, / Sarasvatī was made his conveyance by Viṣṇu.

16.33.s:
tato'bravīdvibhurgaṃgāṃ pārśvataḥ samupasthitām ..
enaṃ vahniṃ mahābhāge vegānnaya mahodadhim..
nānyā śaktā samānetuṃ tvāṃ vinā lokapāvani .. 7.1.33.10 ..
16.33.d:
ततोऽब्रवीद्विभुर्गंगां पार्श्वतः समुपस्थिताम् ..
एनं वह्निं महाभागे वेगान्नय महोदधिम्..
नान्या शक्ता समानेतुं त्वां विना लोकपावनि .. 7.1.33.10 ..
16.33.m: Then the Lord spoke to Gaṅgā, who was standing at his side: / "O fortunate one, take this fire swiftly to the great ocean. / No other woman is capable of bringing it except you, O purifier of the worlds."

16.33.s:
.. gaṅgovāca .. ..
nāsti me bhagavañchakti raurvaṃ voḍhuṃ jagatpate..
raudrarūpī mahāneṣa dahatyevānalo bhṛśam .. 11 ..
16.33.d:
.. गङ्गोवाच .. ..
नास्ति मे भगवञ्छक्ति रौर्वं वोढुं जगत्पते..
रौद्ररूपी महानेष दहत्येवानलो भृशम् .. 11 ..
16.33.m:
Gaṅgā said:
"I do not have the power, O Lord, to carry Aurva, O Lord of the universe. / Fierce of form and mighty, this fire burns intensely indeed."

16.33.s:
tatastu yamunāṃ prāha sindhuṃ tasyā hyanantaram ..
anyā nadīśca vividhāḥ pṛthakpṛthagudāradhīḥ .. 12 ..
16.33.d:
ततस्तु यमुनां प्राह सिन्धुं तस्या ह्यनन्तरम् ..
अन्या नदीश्च विविधाः पृथक्पृथगुदारधीः .. 12 ..
16.33.m: Then the noble-minded one spoke to Yamunā, and immediately after her to Sindhu, / and to various other rivers one by one.

16.33.s:
aśaktāstāḥ samānetuṃ pṛṣṭāśca surasattamaiḥ ..
tataḥ sarasvatīṃ prāha devadevo janārddanaḥ ..
tvameva vraja kalyāṇi pratīcyāṃ lavaṇodadhau .. 13 ..
16.33.d:
अशक्तास्ताः समानेतुं पृष्टाश्च सुरसत्तमैः ..
ततः सरस्वतीं प्राह देवदेवो जनार्द्दनः ..
त्वमेव व्रज कल्याणि प्रतीच्यां लवणोदधौ .. 13 ..
16.33.m: When questioned by the best of the gods, they were unable to lead him. / Then the god of gods, Janārdana, said to Sarasvatī: / "Go yourself, O auspicious one, to the western salt ocean.

16.33.s:
evaṃ kṛte surāḥ sarve bhaviṣyanti bhayojjhitāḥ ..
anyathā vāḍavenaite dahyaṃte svena tejasā .. 14 ..
16.33.d:
एवं कृते सुराः सर्वे भविष्यन्ति भयोज्झिताः ..
अन्यथा वाडवेनैते दह्यंते स्वेन तेजसा .. 14 ..
16.33.m: When this is done, all the gods will become free from fear. / Otherwise, they will be burned by the submarine fire with its own splendor.

16.33.s:
tasmāttvaṃ rakṣa vibudhāne tasmāttumulādbhayāt ..
māteva bhava suśroṇi surāṇāmabhayapradā .. 15 ..
16.33.d:
तस्मात्त्वं रक्ष विबुधाने तस्मात्तुमुलाद्भयात् ..
मातेव भव सुश्रोणि सुराणामभयप्रदा .. 15 ..
16.33.m: Therefore protect the gods from this tumultuous terror; / like a mother, O woman of beautiful hips, grant fearlessness to the gods."

16.33.s:
evamuktā hi sā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
āha nāhaṃ svatantrāsmi pitā me dhriyate cirāt .. 16 ..
16.33.d:
एवमुक्ता हि सा तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
आह नाहं स्वतन्त्रास्मि पिता मे ध्रियते चिरात् .. 16 ..
16.33.m: Being thus addressed by that mighty Viṣṇu, / she said: "I am not independent; my father has lived for a long time.

16.33.s:
tasyāhaṃ kāriṇī nityaṃ kumārī ca dhṛtavratā ..
kālatrayepyasvatantrā śrūyate vibudhaiḥ sutā .. 17 ..
16.33.d:
तस्याहं कारिणी नित्यं कुमारी च धृतव्रता ..
कालत्रयेप्यस्वतन्त्रा श्रूयते विबुधैः सुता .. 17 ..
16.33.m: I am ever his obedient maiden, having observed vows. / A daughter is known by the wise to be non-independent in all three periods of time.

16.33.s:
pitrādeśaṃ vinā nāhaṃ padamekamapi kvacit ..
gacchāmi tasmātko'pyanya upāyaściṃtyatāṃ hare .. 18 ..
16.33.d:
पित्रादेशं विना नाहं पदमेकमपि क्वचित् ..
गच्छामि तस्मात्कोऽप्यन्य उपायश्चिंत्यतां हरे .. 18 ..
16.33.m: Without my father's command I do not take even a single step anywhere. / Therefore, O Hari, let some other means be considered."

16.33.s:
tatsvarūpaṃ viditvaivaṃ samabhyetya pitāmaham ..
tamabravīdvāsudevo devakāryamidaṃ kuru .. 19 ..
16.33.d:
तत्स्वरूपं विदित्वैवं समभ्येत्य पितामहम् ..
तमब्रवीद्वासुदेवो देवकार्यमिदं कुरु .. 19 ..
16.33.m: Having thus learned her true nature, Vāsudeva approached the Grandfather / and said to him: "Perform this task for the gods.

16.33.s:
nānyathā śakyate netuṃ vāḍavo'gnirmahābalaḥ ..
adṛṣṭadoṣāṃ muktvemāṃ kumārīṃ tanayāṃ tava .. 7.1.33.20 ..
16.33.d:
नान्यथा शक्यते नेतुं वाडवोऽग्निर्महाबलः ..
अदृष्टदोषां मुक्त्वेमां कुमारीं तनयां तव .. 7.1.33.20 ..
16.33.m: In no other way can the very mighty submarine fire be conveyed, / leaving aside this maiden, your daughter, who has no seen blemish."

16.33.s:
tacchrutvā viṣṇunā proktaṃ kumārīṃ tanayāṃ tadā ..
śirasyādhāya sasnehamuvāca prapitāmahaḥ .. 21 ..
16.33.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विष्णुना प्रोक्तं कुमारीं तनयां तदा ..
शिरस्याधाय सस्नेहमुवाच प्रपितामहः .. 21 ..
16.33.m: Hearing that which was spoken by Viṣṇu, the Great-grandfather / then placed his hand on the head of the maiden, his daughter, and said with affection:

16.33.s:
yāhi devi surānsarvānrakṣa tvaṃ bhayamāgatān ..
vinikṣipa tvaṃ nītvainaṃ vāḍavaṃ lavaṇāṃbhasi ..
piturvākyaṃ hi sā śrutvā provāca śrutilakṣaṇā ..22..
16.33.d:
याहि देवि सुरान्सर्वान्रक्ष त्वं भयमागतान् ..
विनिक्षिप त्वं नीत्वैनं वाडवं लवणांभसि ..
पितुर्वाक्यं हि सा श्रुत्वा प्रोवाच श्रुतिलक्षणा ..22..
16.33.m: "Go, O goddess! Protect all the gods who have succumbed to fear. / Having carried this submarine fire, cast it into the salty waters." / Hearing her father's words, she whose mark is the Veda said:

16.33.s:
.. sarasvatyuvāca .. ..
eṣāsmi prasthitā tāta tava vākyā dasaṃśayam..
raudro'yaṃ vāḍavo vahnistanuṃ me bhakṣayiṣyati .. 23 ..
16.33.d:
.. सरस्वत्युवाच .. ..
एषास्मि प्रस्थिता तात तव वाक्या दसंशयम्..
रौद्रोऽयं वाडवो वह्निस्तनुं मे भक्षयिष्यति .. 23 ..
16.33.m:
Sarasvatī said:
"Here I have set forth, dear father, in accordance with your command, without doubt. / Yet this fierce submarine fire will consume my body.
