16.33.s:
prāptaṃ kaliyugaṃ raudraṃ sāṃprataṃ pṛthivītale ..
lokaḥ pāpasamācāraḥ sparśayiṣyati māṃ prabho ..24..
16.33.d:
प्राप्तं कलियुगं रौद्रं सांप्रतं पृथिवीतले ..
लोकः पापसमाचारः स्पर्शयिष्यति मां प्रभो ..24..
16.33.m: The terrifying Kali age has now arrived upon the surface of the earth. / People whose conduct is sinful will touch me, O Lord;

16.33.s: tato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ syādyatpāpaiḥ saha saṃgamaḥ..25..
16.33.d: ततो दुःखतरं किं स्याद्यत्पापैः सह संगमः..25..
16.33.m: what could be more sorrowful than union with sinners?"

16.33.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
yadi pāpajanākīrṇaṃ na vāṃchasi dharātalam ..
pātālatalasaṃsthā tvaṃ naya vahniṃ mahodadhau..26..
16.33.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
यदि पापजनाकीर्णं न वांछसि धरातलम् ..
पातालतलसंस्था त्वं नय वह्निं महोदधौ..26..
16.33.m:
Brahmā said:
"If you do not desire the surface of the earth crowded with sinful people, / dwell in the realm of Pātāla and carry the fire to the great ocean.

16.33.s:
yadātiśramasaṃyuktā vahninā dahyase bhṛśam..
tadā vibhidya vasudhāṃ pratyakṣā bhava putrike..27..
16.33.d:
यदातिश्रमसंयुक्ता वह्निना दह्यसे भृशम्..
तदा विभिद्य वसुधां प्रत्यक्षा भव पुत्रिके..27..
16.33.m: When, exhausted by excessive exertion, you are burned intensely by the fire, / then, having broken through the earth, become visible, O little daughter.

16.33.s:
kṛtvā vaktraṃ viśālākṣi prācī bhava sumadhyame..
tato yāsyaṃti tīrthāni tvāṃ śrāṃtāṃ cāruhāsinīm..28..
16.33.d:
कृत्वा वक्त्रं विशालाक्षि प्राची भव सुमध्यमे..
ततो यास्यंति तीर्थानि त्वां श्रांतां चारुहासिनीम्..28..
16.33.m: Having turned your mouth [toward it], O wide-eyed one, flow eastwards, O slender-waisted lady. / Then the sacred fords will go to you who are weary, O woman of charming smiles;

16.33.s:
tāni sarvāṇi cāgatya sāhāyyaṃ te varānane..
kariṣyaṃti trayastriṃśatkoṭyo vai mama śāsanāt..29..
16.33.d:
तानि सर्वाणि चागत्य साहाय्यं ते वरानने..
करिष्यंति त्रयस्त्रिंशत्कोट्यो वै मम शासनात्..29..
16.33.m: and having arrived, all those thirty-three crores [of sacred fords] / will assist you by my command, O lovely-faced one.

16.33.s:
gaccha putri na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana..
ariṣṭaṃ vraja paṃthānaṃ mā santu paripaṃthinaḥ..7.1.33.30.
.. īśvara uvāca..
evamuktā tadā tena brahmaṇātha sarasvatī..
tyaktvā bhayaṃ hṛṣṭamanāḥ prayātuṃ samupasthitā..31..
16.33.d:
गच्छ पुत्रि न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः कथंचन..
अरिष्टं व्रज पंथानं मा सन्तु परिपंथिनः..7.1.33.30.
.. ईश्वर उवाच..
एवमुक्ता तदा तेन ब्रह्मणाथ सरस्वती..
त्यक्त्वा भयं हृष्टमनाः प्रयातुं समुपस्थिता..31..
16.33.m:
Go, daughter! No sorrow at all should be felt by you. / Tread an unhindered path; may there be no adversaries!" / Īśvara said:
Being thus addressed then by Brahmā, Sarasvatī / cast aside fear, and with a glad mind prepared to depart.

16.33.s:
tasyāḥ prayāṇasamaye śaṃkhaduṃdubhiniḥsvanaiḥ ..
maṃgalānāṃ ca nirghoṣairjagadāpūritaṃ śubhaiḥ .. 32 ..
16.33.d:
तस्याः प्रयाणसमये शंखदुंदुभिनिःस्वनैः ..
मंगलानां च निर्घोषैर्जगदापूरितं शुभैः .. 32 ..
16.33.m: At the time of her departure, the world was filled with the auspicious sounds / of conch shells and kettle-drums, and the loud reverberations of auspicious cries.

16.33.s:
sitāṃbaradharā devī sitacaṃdanaguṃṭhitā ..
śāradāṃbudasaṃkāśā tārahāravibhūṣitā .. 33 ..
16.33.d:
सितांबरधरा देवी सितचंदनगुंठिता ..
शारदांबुदसंकाशा तारहारविभूषिता .. 33 ..
16.33.m: The goddess, dressed in white garments and smeared with white sandalwood paste, / resembled an autumn cloud and was adorned with pearl necklaces.

16.33.s:
saṃpūrṇacaṃdravadanā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā ..
kīrtiryathā maheṃdrasya pūrayantī diśo daśa .. 34 ..
16.33.d:
संपूर्णचंद्रवदना पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणा ..
कीर्तिर्यथा महेंद्रस्य पूरयन्ती दिशो दश .. 34 ..
16.33.m: With a face like the full moon and eyes as wide as lotus petals, / like the renown of mighty Indra, she filled the ten directions.

16.33.s:
svatejasā dyotayaṃtī sarvamābhāsayajjagat ..
anuvrajaṃtī gaṃgā vai tayoktā varavarṇini .. 35 ..
16.33.d:
स्वतेजसा द्योतयंती सर्वमाभासयज्जगत् ..
अनुव्रजंती गंगा वै तयोक्ता वरवर्णिनि .. 35 ..
16.33.m: Illumining everything with her own splendor, she brightened the world. / Following her, Gaṅgā was addressed by her, O woman of excellent complexion:

16.33.s:
drakṣyāmi tvāṃ punarahaṃ kutra vai vasatīṃ sakhi ..
evamuktā tayā gaṃgā provāca snigdhayā girā .. 36 ..
16.33.d:
द्रक्ष्यामि त्वां पुनरहं कुत्र वै वसतीं सखि ..
एवमुक्ता तया गंगा प्रोवाच स्निग्धया गिरा .. 36 ..
16.33.m: "Where indeed shall I see you dwelling again, my friend?" / Being addressed thus by her, Gaṅgā replied in an affectionate voice:

16.33.s:
yadaiva vīkṣase prācīdiśi prāpsyasi māṃ tadā ..
suraiḥ parivṛtā sarvaistatrāhaṃ tava suvṛte .. 37 ..
16.33.d:
यदैव वीक्षसे प्राचीदिशि प्राप्स्यसि मां तदा ..
सुरैः परिवृता सर्वैस्तत्राहं तव सुवृते .. 37 ..
16.33.m: "Whenever you look toward the eastern direction, you will then reach me. / Surrounded there by all the gods, O lady of virtuous vows,

16.33.s:
darśanaṃ saṃpradāsyāmi tyaja śokaṃ śucismite ..
tāmāpṛcchya tato gaṃgāṃ punardarśanamastu te .. 38 ..
16.33.d:
दर्शनं संप्रदास्यामि त्यज शोकं शुचिस्मिते ..
तामापृच्छ्य ततो गंगां पुनर्दर्शनमस्तु ते .. 38 ..
16.33.m: I shall grant you a darśana; cast off sorrow, O woman of pure smiles!" / Having taken leave of that Gaṅgā [saying], "May you be seen again!

16.33.s:
gaccha svamālayaṃ bhadre smarttavyā'haṃ tvayā'naghe ..
yamunāpi tathā caivaṃ gāyatrī sumanoramā .. 39 ..
16.33.d:
गच्छ स्वमालयं भद्रे स्मर्त्तव्याऽहं त्वयाऽनघे ..
यमुनापि तथा चैवं गायत्री सुमनोरमा .. 39 ..
16.33.m: Go to your own abode, auspicious one; I should be remembered by you, sinless one!" / Likewise Yamunā and the delightful Gāyatrī,

16.33.s:
sāvitrīsahitāḥ sarvāḥ sakhyaḥ saṃpreṣitāstadā ..
tato visṛjya tāṃ devī nadī bhūtvā sarasvatī .. 7.1.33.40 ..
16.33.d:
सावित्रीसहिताः सर्वाः सख्यः संप्रेषितास्तदा ..
ततो विसृज्य तां देवी नदी भूत्वा सरस्वती .. 7.1.33.40 ..
16.33.m: along with Sāvitrī—all her female companions were then sent away. / Then, bidding farewell to that goddess, Sarasvatī, having become a river,

16.33.s:
himavaṃtaṃ giriṃ prāpya plakṣāttatra vinirgatā ..
avatīrṇā dharāpṛṣṭhe matsyakacchapasaṃkulā .. 41 ..
16.33.d:
हिमवंतं गिरिं प्राप्य प्लक्षात्तत्र विनिर्गता ..
अवतीर्णा धरापृष्ठे मत्स्यकच्छपसंकुला .. 41 ..
16.33.m: Having reached the mountain Himavat, she emerged from the Plakṣa tree, / and descended upon the surface of the earth, teeming with fish and turtles.

16.33.s:
grāhaḍiṃḍimasaṃpūrṇā timinakragaṇairyutā ..
hasaṃtī ca mahādevī phenaughaiḥ sarvato diśam..42..
16.33.d:
ग्राहडिंडिमसंपूर्णा तिमिनक्रगणैर्युता ..
हसंती च महादेवी फेनौघैः सर्वतो दिशम्..42..
16.33.m: Filled with crocodiles and diṇḍima fish, accompanied by shoals of timis and alligators, / the great goddess laughed in every direction with floods of foam.

16.33.s:
puṇyato yavahā devīstūyamānā dvijātibhiḥ ..
vāḍavaṃ vahnimādāya hayavegena niḥsṛtā .. 43 ..
16.33.d:
पुण्यतो यवहा देवीस्तूयमाना द्विजातिभिः ..
वाडवं वह्निमादाय हयवेगेन निःसृता .. 43 ..
16.33.m: Flowing with sacred waters, praised by the twice-born, / carrying the submarine fire, she rushed out with the speed of a horse.

16.33.s:
bhittvā vegāddharāpṛṣṭhaṃ praviṣṭātha mahītalam..
yadāyadābhavacchrāṃtā dahyate vāḍavāgninā ..
tadātadā martyaloke yāti pratyakṣatāṃ nadī .. 44 ..
16.33.d:
भित्त्वा वेगाद्धरापृष्ठं प्रविष्टाथ महीतलम्..
यदायदाभवच्छ्रांता दह्यते वाडवाग्निना ..
तदातदा मर्त्यलोके याति प्रत्यक्षतां नदी .. 44 ..
16.33.m: Splitting the surface of the earth through her speed, she then entered into the underworld; / whenever she became weary and was burnt by the submarine fire, / then the river became visible in the mortal world.

16.33.s:
tatastu jāyate prācī saṃtaptā vāḍavena tu ..
tato vai yāni tīrthāni kīrttitāni purātanaiḥ .. 45 ..
16.33.d:
ततस्तु जायते प्राची संतप्ता वाडवेन तु ..
ततो वै यानि तीर्थानि कीर्त्तितानि पुरातनैः .. 45 ..
16.33.m: Then she flowed eastward, scorched indeed by the submarine [fire]; / thereupon the sacred fords celebrated by the ancients,

16.33.s:
divyāṃtarikṣabhaumāni sāṃnidhyaṃ yāṃti bhāmini ..
tataścāśvāsitā taiḥ sā sarasvatī punarnadī ..
pātālatalamā sādya jagāma makarālayam .. 46 ..
16.33.d:
दिव्यांतरिक्षभौमानि सांनिध्यं यांति भामिनि ..
ततश्चाश्वासिता तैः सा सरस्वती पुनर्नदी ..
पातालतलमा साद्य जगाम मकरालयम् .. 46 ..
16.33.m: celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial, entered her presence, O lovely lady. / Then, consoled by them, the river Sarasvatī / reached the underworld and went towards the ocean.

16.33.s:
khadirāmodamāsādya tatra sā vīkṣya sāgaram ..
gaṃtuṃ pravṛttā taṃ vahnimādāya surasuṃdari ..47..
16.33.d:
खदिरामोदमासाद्य तत्र सा वीक्ष्य सागरम् ..
गंतुं प्रवृत्ता तं वह्निमादाय सुरसुंदरि ..47..
16.33.m: Reaching Khadirāmoda, seeing the ocean there, / she proceeded to go, carrying that fire, O divine beauty.

16.33.s:
nirūḍhabhāramātmānaṃ devādeśādviciṃtya sā ..
prahṛṣṭā sumanāstasmātpravṛttā dakṣiṇāmukhī .. 48 ..
16.33.d:
निरूढभारमात्मानं देवादेशाद्विचिंत्य सा ..
प्रहृष्टा सुमनास्तस्मात्प्रवृत्ता दक्षिणामुखी .. 48 ..
16.33.m: Considering her burden carried out by the command of the gods, / delighted and joyous in mind, she set forth facing southwards.

16.33.s:
etasminneva kāle tu ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ ..
catvāraśca mahādevi prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāśritāḥ .. 49 ..
16.33.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु ऋषयो वेदपारगाः ..
चत्वारश्च महादेवि प्रभासं क्षेत्रमाश्रिताः .. 49 ..
16.33.m: At that very time, four seers who had mastered the Vedas, / O great goddess, were residing in the sacred field Prabhāsa:

16.33.s:
hariṇaścātha vajraśca nyaṃkuḥ kapila eva ca ..
tapastapyaṃti tatrasthāḥ svādhyāyāsaktamānasāḥ .. 7.1.33.50 ..
16.33.d:
हरिणश्चाथ वज्रश्च न्यंकुः कपिल एव च ..
तपस्तप्यंति तत्रस्थाः स्वाध्यायासक्तमानसाः .. 7.1.33.50 ..
16.33.m: Hariṇa, Vajra, Nyaṅku, and Kapila; / dwelling there, their minds devoted to Vedic recitation, they practiced austerity.

16.33.s:
pṛthakpṛthaksamāhūtāḥ snānārthaṃ taiḥ sarasvatī ..
sāgaraḥ sammukhastasyāḥ sahasā sammupasthitaḥ .. 51 ..
16.33.d:
पृथक्पृथक्समाहूताः स्नानार्थं तैः सरस्वती ..
सागरः सम्मुखस्तस्याः सहसा सम्मुपस्थितः .. 51 ..
16.33.m: Sarasvatī was summoned by them individually for the sake of ritual ablution, / while the ocean suddenly stood right before her.

16.33.s:
tataḥ sā cintayāmāsa kathaṃ me sukṛtaṃ bhavet ..
śāpabhītā ca sā sādhvī paṃcasrotāstadā'bhavat .. 52 ..
16.33.d:
ततः सा चिन्तयामास कथं मे सुकृतं भवेत् ..
शापभीता च सा साध्वी पंचस्रोतास्तदाऽभवत् .. 52 ..
16.33.m: Then she reflected: 'How can my meritorious deed come to be?' / And fearing their curse, that virtuous one became divided into five streams.

16.33.s:
ekaikaṃ toṣayāmāsa tamṛṣiṃ varavarṇini ..
tato'syāḥ paṃca nāmāni jātāni pṛthivītale .. 53 ..
16.33.d:
एकैकं तोषयामास तमृषिं वरवर्णिनि ..
ततोऽस्याः पंच नामानि जातानि पृथिवीतले .. 53 ..
16.33.m: She gratified each seer, one by one, O fair-complexioned lady; / then five names of hers arose upon the surface of the earth:

16.33.s:
hariṇī vajriṇī nyaṃkuḥ kapilā ca sarasvatī ..
pānāvagāhanānnṛṇāṃ paṃcasrotāḥ sarasvatī .. 54 ..
16.33.d:
हरिणी वज्रिणी न्यंकुः कपिला च सरस्वती ..
पानावगाहनान्नृणां पंचस्रोताः सरस्वती .. 54 ..
16.33.m: Hariṇī, Vajriṇī, Nyaṅku, Kapilā, and Sarasvatī; / by drinking and bathing [in her], Sarasvatī is of five streams for mortals.

16.33.s:
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ ..
eṣāṃ saṃyogajaṃ cānyannarāṇāṃ paṃcamaṃ hi yat .. 55 ..
16.33.d:
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वंगनागमः ..
एषां संयोगजं चान्यन्नराणां पंचमं हि यत् .. 55 ..
16.33.m: The slaying of a brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and union with the guru's wife, / and that fifth [sin] of mortals arising from association with these—

16.33.s:
etatpaṃcavidhaṃ puṃsāṃ paṃcadhā'vasthitā satī ..
nāśayetpātakaṃ ghoraṃ sakhībhiḥ sahitā nadī..56..
16.33.d:
एतत्पंचविधं पुंसां पंचधाऽवस्थिता सती ..
नाशयेत्पातकं घोरं सखीभिः सहिता नदी..56..
16.33.m: abiding in five ways, the virtuous river, together with her companions, / destroys these five kinds of dreadful sin in men.

16.33.s:
brahmahatyāṃ mahāghorāṃ pratilomā sarasvatī ..
pānāvagāhanānnṛṇāṃ nāśayatyakhilaṃ hi sā .. 57 ..
16.33.d:
ब्रह्महत्यां महाघोरां प्रतिलोमा सरस्वती ..
पानावगाहनान्नृणां नाशयत्यखिलं हि सा .. 57 ..
16.33.m: Flowing backwards, Sarasvatī / destroys through men's drinking and bathing all of the most dreadful sin of killing a brahmin.

16.33.s:
pramādānmadirāpānadoṣeṇopahatātmanām ..
tadvyapohāya kapilā dvijānāṃ vahate nadī .. 58 ..
16.33.d:
प्रमादान्मदिरापानदोषेणोपहतात्मनाम् ..
तद्व्यपोहाय कपिला द्विजानां वहते नदी .. 58 ..
16.33.m: For twice-born men whose minds are ruined through negligent fault of drinking liquor, / the river Kapilā flows to remove that [sin].

16.33.s:
upavāsājjapāddhomātsnānātpānāddvijanmanām ..
saptāhānnāśayetpāpaṃ tattadbhāvena cetasā..59..
16.33.d:
उपवासाज्जपाद्धोमात्स्नानात्पानाद्द्विजन्मनाम् ..
सप्ताहान्नाशयेत्पापं तत्तद्भावेन चेतसा..59..
16.33.m: Through fasting, silent recitation, oblation, ritual ablution, and drinking, with that disposition of mind, / she destroys the sin of the twice-born within seven days.

16.33.s:
svayaṃ te'pi viśudhyaṃti yathoktavidhikāriṇaḥ ..
nyaṃkuṃ nadīṃ samāsādya mahataḥ pātakātkṛtāt .. 7.1.33.60 ..
16.33.d:
स्वयं तेऽपि विशुध्यंति यथोक्तविधिकारिणः ..
न्यंकुं नदीं समासाद्य महतः पातकात्कृतात् .. 7.1.33.60 ..
16.33.m: Having reached the river Nyaṅku, even those who have committed great sin / are purified by themselves if they perform the rites as prescribed.

16.33.s:
snānopāsanapānena vajriṇī gurutalpagam ..
nāśayatyakhilaṃ puṃsāṃ pāpaṃ bhūribhayaṃkaram .. 61 ..
16.33.d:
स्नानोपासनपानेन वज्रिणी गुरुतल्पगम् ..
नाशयत्यखिलं पुंसां पापं भूरिभयंकरम् .. 61 ..
16.33.m: By ritual ablution, worship, and drinking, Vajriṇī destroys entirely / the terribly frightening sin of men who violate the guru's bed.

16.33.s:
saṃyogajasya pāpasya haraṇāddhariṇī smṛtā ..
nadī puṇyajalopetā saptāhamavagāhanāt .. 62 ..
16.33.d:
संयोगजस्य पापस्य हरणाद्धरिणी स्मृता ..
नदी पुण्यजलोपेता सप्ताहमवगाहनात् .. 62 ..
16.33.m: Because of taking away the sin arising from association, it is called Hariṇī, / a river endowed with sacred waters, by bathing in it for seven days.

16.33.s:
evametāni pāpāni sarvāṇi surasuṃdari ..
nadī nāśayate tathyaṃ paṃcasrotā sarasvatī .. 63 ..
16.33.d:
एवमेतानि पापानि सर्वाणि सुरसुंदरि ..
नदी नाशयते तथ्यं पंचस्रोता सरस्वती .. 63 ..
16.33.m: Thus the river Sarasvatī of five streams, O divine beauty, / truly destroys all these sins.

16.33.s:
tato'paśyatpunaścāru sā devī pathi saṃsthitam ..
parvataṃ sāgarasyāṃte roddhuṃ mārgamiva sthitam .. 64 ..
16.33.d:
ततोऽपश्यत्पुनश्चारु सा देवी पथि संस्थितम् ..
पर्वतं सागरस्यांते रोद्धुं मार्गमिव स्थितम् .. 64 ..
16.33.m: Then again that beautiful goddess saw standing in her path / a mountain at the edge of the ocean, stationed as if to block the way.

16.33.s:
brahmāṇḍamānadaṇḍo'yaṃ purato girisattamaḥ ..
vrajantyāḥ surakāryeṇa mama vighnakaraḥ sthitaḥ .. .. 65 ..
16.33.d:
ब्रह्माण्डमानदण्डोऽयं पुरतो गिरिसत्तमः ..
व्रजन्त्याः सुरकार्येण मम विघ्नकरः स्थितः .. .. 65 ..
16.33.m: [She thought:] 'This excellent mountain, like a measuring rod of the universe, / stands before me, creating an obstacle as I travel on the mission of the gods.'

16.33.s:
uccaistaraṃ mahāśailamavalokya sarasvatī ..
atha vegena ruddhena giriṇā vismitā satī .. 66 ..
16.33.d:
उच्चैस्तरं महाशैलमवलोक्य सरस्वती ..
अथ वेगेन रुद्धेन गिरिणा विस्मिता सती .. 66 ..
16.33.m: Beholding that exceedingly high, great mountain, Sarasvatī, / with her swift course now obstructed by the mountain, was astonished.

16.33.s:
evaṃ saṃcintayedyāvanmanasā tanma hādbhutam ..
tāvanmaṃgalaśabdena pratibuddhaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ .. 67 ..
16.33.d:
एवं संचिन्तयेद्यावन्मनसा तन्म हाद्भुतम् ..
तावन्मंगलशब्देन प्रतिबुद्धः कृतस्मरः .. 67 ..
16.33.m: While she was thus reflecting in her mind upon that great wonder, / awakened by the auspicious sound, [the mountain] Kṛtasmara,

16.33.s:
giriśṛṃgadvaṃdvacaraṃ dadarśa puruṣaṃ ca sā ..
tāmāha devīṃ sa nago mārgo nāstīha suvrate .. 68 ..
16.33.d:
गिरिशृंगद्वंद्वचरं ददर्श पुरुषं च सा ..
तामाह देवीं स नगो मार्गो नास्तीह सुव्रते .. 68 ..
16.33.m: moving between both peaks of the mountain, appeared as a man to her sight; / that mountain spoke to the goddess: 'There is no way here, O lady of good vows!

16.33.s:
anyatra kvāpi gaccha tvaṃ yatra te'bhimataṃ śubhe ..
āhaivamukte sā devī naraṃ nagaśiraḥsthitam .. 69 ..
16.33.d:
अन्यत्र क्वापि गच्छ त्वं यत्र तेऽभिमतं शुभे ..
आहैवमुक्ते सा देवी नरं नगशिरःस्थितम् .. 69 ..
16.33.m: Go somewhere else, wherever you desire, O auspicious lady.' / When he had spoken thus, that goddess addressed the man standing atop the mountain:

16.33.s:
devādeśātsamāyātā na nirodhyā gire tvayā ..
evamukte giriḥ prāha tāṃ devīṃ sumanoramām .. 7.1.33.70 ..
16.33.d:
देवादेशात्समायाता न निरोध्या गिरे त्वया ..
एवमुक्ते गिरिः प्राह तां देवीं सुमनोरमाम् .. 7.1.33.70 ..
16.33.m: 'I have arrived by the command of the gods; I must not be obstructed by you, O mountain!' / When she had spoken thus, the mountain said to that most delightful goddess:

16.33.s:
parvato'haṃ tvayā bhadre kiṃ na jñātaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ ..
tvatsparśanānna doṣosti kumārī tvaṃ yato'naghe .. 71 ..
16.33.d:
पर्वतोऽहं त्वया भद्रे किं न ज्ञातः कृतस्मरः ..
त्वत्स्पर्शनान्न दोषोस्ति कुमारी त्वं यतोऽनघे .. 71 ..
16.33.m: 'I am the mountain Kṛtasmara, O good lady; do you not know me? / Because you are a maiden, O faultless one, there is no fault in your touching [me].

16.33.s: atastvāṃ varaye devi bhāryā me bhava suvrate .. 72 ..
16.33.d: अतस्त्वां वरये देवि भार्या मे भव सुव्रते .. 72 ..
16.33.m: Therefore I choose you, O goddess; become my wife, O lady of good vows!'

16.33.s:
.. sarasvatyuvāca .. ..
pitā me dhriyate yasmāttena nāhaṃ svayaṃvarā ..
tava bhāryā bhaviṣyāmi mārgaṃ yaccha mamādhunā .. 73 ..
16.33.d:
.. सरस्वत्युवाच .. ..
पिता मे ध्रियते यस्मात्तेन नाहं स्वयंवरा ..
तव भार्या भविष्यामि मार्गं यच्छ ममाधुना .. 73 ..
16.33.m: Sarasvatī said: / 'Because my father lives, I am not free to choose my own husband; / I cannot become your wife; grant me passage now.'

16.33.s:
evamukto giriḥ prāha anicchaṃtīṃ mahābalāt ..
udvāhayiṣye tvāṃ bhadre kastrātā sti tavādhunā .. 74 ..
16.33.d:
एवमुक्तो गिरिः प्राह अनिच्छंतीं महाबलात् ..
उद्वाहयिष्ये त्वां भद्रे कस्त्राता स्ति तवाधुना .. 74 ..
16.33.m: Addressed thus, the mountain said: 'Against your will, by my great might, / I shall marry you, O good lady! Who is your protector now?'

16.33.s:
sā taṃ manobhavākrāntaṃ matvā divyena cakṣuṣā ..
āha nāsti mama trātā tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatā .. 75 ..
16.33.d:
सा तं मनोभवाक्रान्तं मत्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा ..
आह नास्ति मम त्राता त्वामेव शरणं गता .. 75 ..
16.33.m: Knowing through divine sight that he was overpowered by desire, / she said: 'I have no protector; I have come to you alone for refuge.

16.33.s:
tvayodvāhyā yadya vaśyamahamevaṃ mahābala ..
asnātāṃ nodvaha vibho snānaṃ karttuṃ ca dehi me .. 76 ..
16.33.d:
त्वयोद्वाह्या यद्य वश्यमहमेवं महाबल ..
अस्नातां नोद्वह विभो स्नानं कर्त्तुं च देहि मे .. 76 ..
16.33.m: If I must indeed be married by you, O mighty one, / do not marry me unbathed, O lord, and grant me permission to bathe.'

16.33.s:
tāmuvāca tataḥ śailaḥ svasaṃpadabhimānavān ..
saukhyadaṃ paśya subhage mayi saṃpūrṇavaibhavam .. 77 ..
16.33.d:
तामुवाच ततः शैलः स्वसंपदभिमानवान् ..
सौख्यदं पश्य सुभगे मयि संपूर्णवैभवम् .. 77 ..
16.33.m: Then the mountain, proud of his own wealth, spoke to her: / 'Behold in me, O fortunate lady, all my majesty which brings happiness!

16.33.s:
dvaṃdvāni yatra gāyaṃti kiṃnarāṇāṃ manoramam ..
śrūyate ca sunidhvānaṃ taṃtrīvādyamathāparam .. 78 ..
16.33.d:
द्वंद्वानि यत्र गायंति किंनराणां मनोरमम् ..
श्रूयते च सुनिध्वानं तंत्रीवाद्यमथापरम् .. 78 ..
16.33.m: Where pairs of kiṃnaras sing delightfully, / and the pleasant sound of lutes and other instruments is heard;

16.33.s:
tatra tālāstamālāśca pippalāḥ panasāstathā ..
sadaiva phalapuṣpāścā dṛśyaṃte sumanoramāḥ ..79..
16.33.d:
तत्र तालास्तमालाश्च पिप्पलाः पनसास्तथा ..
सदैव फलपुष्पाश्चा दृश्यंते सुमनोरमाः ..79..
16.33.m: where palmyras, tamālas, pippalas, and jackfruit trees / are always seen, most lovely, laden with fruit and flowers;

16.33.s:
kuṭajaiḥ kovidāraiśca kadaṃbaiḥ kurabaistathā ..
mattālikulaghuṣṭaiśca bhūdharo bhāti sarvataḥ .. 7.1.33.80 ..
16.33.d:
कुटजैः कोविदारैश्च कदंबैः कुरबैस्तथा ..
मत्तालिकुलघुष्टैश्च भूधरो भाति सर्वतः .. 7.1.33.80 ..
16.33.m: with kuṭajas, kovidāras, kadambas, and kurabas, / resplendent with swarms of intoxicated bees, the mountain shines on all sides.

16.33.s:
harāṃgarāgavadbhāti kvacitkuṭajakuḍmalaiḥ ..
kvacittu karṇikāraiśca viṣṇorvāsaḥsamaprabhaḥ .. 81 ..
16.33.d:
हरांगरागवद्भाति क्वचित्कुटजकुड्मलैः ..
क्वचित्तु कर्णिकारैश्च विष्णोर्वासःसमप्रभः .. 81 ..
16.33.m: In some places, with buds of kuṭaja, it shines like Hara's bodily cosmetic; / in others, with karṇikāras, it has the luster of Viṣṇu's garment;

16.33.s:
tamāladalasaṃchannaḥ kvacidvaivasvatadyutiḥ..
kvaciddhātuviliptāṃgo gaṇādhyakṣavapurnagaḥ .. 82 ..
16.33.d:
तमालदलसंछन्नः क्वचिद्वैवस्वतद्युतिः..
क्वचिद्धातुविलिप्तांगो गणाध्यक्षवपुर्नगः .. 82 ..
16.33.m: covered with tamāla leaves, in some places it has the splendor of Yama; / in others, its limbs smeared with mineral dyes, the mountain resembles the form of the chief of the gaṇas;

16.33.s:
caturmukha ivābhāti haritālavapuḥ kvacit ..
kvacitsaptacchadairviṣṇorvapuṣā bhātyayaṃ giriḥ.. 83 ..
16.33.d:
चतुर्मुख इवाभाति हरितालवपुः क्वचित् ..
क्वचित्सप्तच्छदैर्विष्णोर्वपुषा भात्ययं गिरिः.. 83 ..
16.33.m: in some places, with a body of yellow orpiment, it shines like the four-faced [Brahmā]; / in others, with saptacchada trees, this mountain shines like the body of Viṣṇu;

16.33.s:
kvacitkātyāyanīprakhyaḥ priyaṃgususamākulaḥ ..
kvacitkesarasaṃyuktairanalābho vibhātyasau .. 84 ..
16.33.d:
क्वचित्कात्यायनीप्रख्यः प्रियंगुसुसमाकुलः ..
क्वचित्केसरसंयुक्तैरनलाभो विभात्यसौ .. 84 ..
16.33.m: in some places, filled with priyaṅgu blossoms, it resembles Kātyāyanī; / in others, with kesara flowers, it shines with the appearance of fire.'

16.33.s:
vṛttaiḥ sapulakaiḥ snigdhaiḥ strīṇāmiva payodharaiḥ ..
duṣprāpyairalpapuṇyānāṃ kvacidābhāti bilvakaiḥ .. 85 ..
16.33.d:
वृत्तैः सपुलकैः स्निग्धैः स्त्रीणामिव पयोधरैः ..
दुष्प्राप्यैरल्पपुण्यानां क्वचिदाभाति बिल्वकैः .. 85 ..
16.33.m: In some places it shines with bilva fruits, round, bristling, and smooth / like women’s breasts, hard to obtain for those of little merit.

16.33.s:
siṃhairvyāghrairmṛgairnāgairvarāhairvānaraistathā ..
kvacitkvacidasau bhāti parasparamanuvrataiḥ .. 86 ..
16.33.d:
सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्मृगैर्नागैर्वराहैर्वानरैस्तथा ..
क्वचित्क्वचिदसौ भाति परस्परमनुव्रतैः .. 86 ..
16.33.m: In various places it shines with lions, tigers, deer, elephants, / boars, and monkeys devoted to one another,

16.33.s:
śūlikodbhinnamākāśamiva kurvadbhiruccakaiḥ ..
evamukte pratyuvāca śāradā taṃ nagottamam .. 87 ..
16.33.d:
शूलिकोद्भिन्नमाकाशमिव कुर्वद्भिरुच्चकैः ..
एवमुक्ते प्रत्युवाच शारदा तं नगोत्तमम् .. 87 ..
16.33.m:
rising high as if piercing the sky with their peaks.
When this was said, Śāradā replied to that best of mountains:

16.33.s:
yadi māṃ tvaṃ pariṇaye rudaṃtīmekikāṃ tathā ..
gṛhāṇa vāḍavaṃ haste yāvatsnānaṃ karomyaham .. 88 ..
16.33.d:
यदि मां त्वं परिणये रुदंतीमेकिकां तथा ..
गृहाण वाडवं हस्ते यावत्स्नानं करोम्यहम् .. 88 ..
16.33.m: “If you would marry me as I weep thus alone, / hold the submarine fire in your hand while I perform my ritual ablution.”

16.33.s:
evamukte sa jagrāha ta nagedro'pavarjim ..
kṛtasmarastatsaṃsparśātkṣaṇādbhasmatvamāgataḥ .. 89 ..
16.33.d:
एवमुक्ते स जग्राह त नगेद्रोऽपवर्जिम् ..
कृतस्मरस्तत्संस्पर्शात्क्षणाद्भस्मत्वमागतः .. 89 ..
16.33.m:
When this was said, the lord of mountains took the fire.
Kṛtasmara, from its touch, turned to ash in an instant.

16.33.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti te tasya pāṣāṇā mṛdutāṃ gatāḥ ..
gṛhadevakulārthāya gṛhyaṃte śilpibhiḥ saha .. 7.1.33.90 ..
16.33.d:
ततः प्रभृति ते तस्य पाषाणा मृदुतां गताः ..
गृहदेवकुलार्थाय गृह्यंते शिल्पिभिः सह .. 7.1.33.90 ..
16.33.m:
From then on, his stones became soft;
they are quarried together with artisans for houses and temples.

16.33.s:
dagdhvā kṛtasmaraṃ devī punarādāya vāḍavam ..
samudrasya samīpe sā sthitā hṛṣṭatanūruhā .. 91 ..
16.33.d:
दग्ध्वा कृतस्मरं देवी पुनरादाय वाडवम् ..
समुद्रस्य समीपे सा स्थिता हृष्टतनूरुहा .. 91 ..
16.33.m:
Having burned Kṛtasmara, the goddess took up the submarine fire once more
and stood near the sea, her bodily hair bristling with joy.

16.33.s:
tatrasthā sā mahādevī tamāha vaḍavānalam ..
paśya vāḍava garjantaṃ sāgaraṃ purataḥ sthitam .. 92 ..
16.33.d:
तत्रस्था सा महादेवी तमाह वडवानलम् ..
पश्य वाडव गर्जन्तं सागरं पुरतः स्थितम् .. 92 ..
16.33.m:
Standing there, that great goddess said to the submarine fire:
“Look, O submarine fire, at the ocean standing roaring before us!”

16.33.s:
garjaṃtaṃ so'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā prasarpaṃtaṃ ca vīcibhiḥ ..
tāmāha kimidaṃ bhadre bhīto me lavaṇodadhiḥ .. 93 ..
16.33.d:
गर्जंतं सोऽपि तं दृष्ट्वा प्रसर्पंतं च वीचिभिः ..
तामाह किमिदं भद्रे भीतो मे लवणोदधिः .. 93 ..
16.33.m:
Seeing it roaring and creeping forward with waves,
he also said to her: “What is this, fair one? Is the salt ocean afraid of me?”

16.33.s:
prahasyovāca sā bālā ko na bhītastavānala ..
bhakṣyaste vihito yasmāttava devairmahābala .. 94 ..
16.33.d:
प्रहस्योवाच सा बाला को न भीतस्तवानल ..
भक्ष्यस्ते विहितो यस्मात्तव देवैर्महाबल .. 94 ..
16.33.m:
Laughing, the maiden said: “Who would not fear you, O fire?
For it has been ordained as your food by the gods, O mighty one!”

16.33.s:
sa tasyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭastu pāvakaḥ ..
dāsyāmi te varaṃ bhadre yatheṣṭaṃ prārthayasva naḥ ..95..
16.33.d:
स तस्यास्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा संप्रहृष्टस्तु पावकः ..
दास्यामि ते वरं भद्रे यथेष्टं प्रार्थयस्व नः ..95..
16.33.m:
Hearing that speech of hers, the fire became exceedingly glad:
“I shall grant you a boon, fair one; ask of me whatever you desire.”

16.33.s:
tenaivamuktā sā devī vāḍavenāgninā tadā ..
sasmāra kāraṇātmānaṃ viṣṇuṃ kamalalocanam .. 96 ..
16.33.d:
तेनैवमुक्ता सा देवी वाडवेनाग्निना तदा ..
सस्मार कारणात्मानं विष्णुं कमललोचनम् .. 96 ..
16.33.m:
Thus addressed at that time by the submarine fire, the goddess
remembered the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu, the causal self.

16.33.s:
dṛṣṭosāvātmahṛtsaṃsthastayā devo janārddanaḥ ..
smṛtamātraḥ sarasvatyā parastribhuvaneśvaraḥ ..97..
16.33.d:
दृष्टोसावात्महृत्संस्थस्तया देवो जनार्द्दनः ..
स्मृतमात्रः सरस्वत्या परस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ..97..
16.33.m:
As soon as he was remembered by Sarasvatī, the transcendent lord of the three worlds,
the god Janārdana, was seen by her residing within her own heart.

16.33.s:
manodṛṣṭyā vilokyāha sā tamaṃtaḥsthamacyutam ..
vāḍavo yacchati varamahaṃ taṃ prārthayāmi kim..98..
16.33.d:
मनोदृष्ट्या विलोक्याह सा तमंतःस्थमच्युतम् ..
वाडवो यच्छति वरमहं तं प्रार्थयामि किम्..98..
16.33.m:
Beholding the imperishable one dwelling within her by her mind’s vision, she said:
“The submarine fire is offering a boon. What should I ask of him?”

16.33.s:
tatastena hṛdisthena proktā devī sarasvatī ..
prārthanīyo varo bhadre sūcīvaktratvamādarāt .. 99 ..
16.33.d:
ततस्तेन हृदिस्थेन प्रोक्ता देवी सरस्वती ..
प्रार्थनीयो वरो भद्रे सूचीवक्त्रत्वमादरात् .. 99 ..
16.33.m:
Then the goddess Sarasvatī was told by him who was in her heart:
“The boon to be requested with care, fair one, is that his mouth become like a needle.”

16.33.s:
tatastvabhihito devyā yadi me tvaṃ varapradaḥ ..
tataḥ sūcīmukho bhūtvā tvaṃ pibāpo mahābala .. 7.1.33.100 ..
16.33.d:
ततस्त्वभिहितो देव्या यदि मे त्वं वरप्रदः ..
ततः सूचीमुखो भूत्वा त्वं पिबापो महाबल .. 7.1.33.100 ..
16.33.m:
Then he was addressed by the goddess: “If you grant me a boon,
then, having become needle-mouthed, drink the waters, O mighty one!”

16.33.s:
evamuktena tattena sūcīvedhasamaṃ kṛtam ..
ghaṭikāpūraṇaṃ yadvatpapau tadvadanaṃ jalam .. 101 ..
16.33.d:
एवमुक्तेन तत्तेन सूचीवेधसमं कृतम् ..
घटिकापूरणं यद्वत्पपौ तद्वदनं जलम् .. 101 ..
16.33.m:
When he was thus addressed, it was made equal to a needle's bore by him;
like the filling of a water-clock, that mouth drank the water.

16.33.s:
evaṃ sa vāḍavo vahniḥ surāṇāṃ bhakṣaṇodyataḥ ..
vaṃcito viṣṇunā yāti medhāmādhāya yatnataḥ .. 102 ..
16.33.d:
एवं स वाडवो वह्निः सुराणां भक्षणोद्यतः ..
वंचितो विष्णुना याति मेधामाधाय यत्नतः .. 102 ..
16.33.m:
Thus that submarine fire, ready to devour the gods,
went forth, deceived by Viṣṇu who carefully used his intellect.

16.33.s:
sargametaṃ naraḥ puṇyaṃ vācyamānaṃ śṛṇoti yaḥ ..
sa viṣṇu lokamāsādya tenaiva saha modate ..103..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye sara svatīvṛttāṃtavaḍavānalavacanavarṇanaṃnāma trayastriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 33 .. cha ..
16.33.d:
सर्गमेतं नरः पुण्यं वाच्यमानं शृणोति यः ..
स विष्णु लोकमासाद्य तेनैव सह मोदते ..103..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सर स्वतीवृत्तांतवडवानलवचनवर्णनंनाम त्रयस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 33 .. छ ..
16.33.m:
The man who hears this holy creation recited
attains the realm of Viṣṇu and rejoices with him.
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Sarasvatī Account and the Speech of the Submarine Fire,' in the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, the first [sub-section] of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, the seventh [section] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

16.34.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
sarasvatī varaṃ prāpya variṣṭhaṃ vaḍavānalāt ..
punastaṃ sāgare kṣeptumudyatā sā manasvinī .. 1 ..
16.34.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
सरस्वती वरं प्राप्य वरिष्ठं वडवानलात् ..
पुनस्तं सागरे क्षेप्तुमुद्यता सा मनस्विनी .. 1 ..
16.34.m:
Īśvara said:
Having obtained the supreme boon from the submarine fire,
that high-minded goddess prepared again to cast it into the ocean.

16.34.s:
devādeśātprabhāsasya purataḥ saṃsthitā tadā ..
samudramāhūya tadā vāḍavārpaṇakāṃkṣiṇī .. 2 ..
16.34.d:
देवादेशात्प्रभासस्य पुरतः संस्थिता तदा ..
समुद्रमाहूय तदा वाडवार्पणकांक्षिणी .. 2 ..
16.34.m:
By command of the gods, she stood then before Prabhāsa,
calling the ocean, desiring to deliver the submarine fire.

16.34.s:
tvamādiḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ prāṇaḥ prāṇināṃ sadā ..
devādeśādgṛhāṇa tvamāgatyārṇava vāḍavam .. 3 ..
16.34.d:
त्वमादिः सर्वदेवानां त्वं प्राणः प्राणिनां सदा ..
देवादेशाद्गृहाण त्वमागत्यार्णव वाडवम् .. 3 ..
16.34.m:
“You are the beginning of all the gods; you are always the life-breath of living beings.
By command of the gods, come and receive the submarine fire, O ocean!”

16.34.s:
evaṃ saṃciṃtito devyā yadāsāvaṃbhasāṃpatiḥ ..
tathā jalātsamuttīrya samāyāto mahādyutiḥ .. 4 ..
16.34.d:
एवं संचिंतितो देव्या यदासावंभसांपतिः ..
तथा जलात्समुत्तीर्य समायातो महाद्युतिः .. 4 ..
16.34.m:
When that lord of waters was thus contemplated by the goddess,
he, of great splendor, emerged from the water and approached.

16.34.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitā devī divyaṃ viṣṇumivāparam ..
śyāmaṃ kamalapatrākṣaṃ sāgaraṃ sumanoramam .. 5 ..
16.34.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिता देवी दिव्यं विष्णुमिवापरम् ..
श्यामं कमलपत्राक्षं सागरं सुमनोरमम् .. 5 ..
16.34.m:
Seeing him, the goddess was amazed: he was like another celestial Viṣṇu,
dark, lotus-petal-eyed, the exceedingly charming ocean,

16.34.s:
vicitramālyābharaṇaṃ citravastrānulepanam..
āpagābhiḥ sarūpābhiḥ strīrūpābhiḥ samāvṛtam .. 6 ..
16.34.d:
विचित्रमाल्याभरणं चित्रवस्त्रानुलेपनम्..
आपगाभिः सरूपाभिः स्त्रीरूपाभिः समावृतम् .. 6 ..
16.34.m:
with diverse garlands and ornaments, diverse garments and unguents,
surrounded by rivers in women's forms of like appearance.

16.34.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ samālokya sā devī brahmaṇaḥ sutā ..
sarasvatī jalanidhimuvācedaṃ śucismitā .. 7 ..
16.34.d:
एवंविधं समालोक्य सा देवी ब्रह्मणः सुता ..
सरस्वती जलनिधिमुवाचेदं शुचिस्मिता .. 7 ..
16.34.m:
Seeing him of such a form, the goddess Sarasvatī,
the daughter of Brahmā, smiling purely, said this to the ocean:

16.34.s:
tvamagrajaḥ sarvabhavodbhavānāṃ tvaṃ jīvitaṃ janmavatāṃ narāṇām ..
tasmātsurāṇāṃ kuru kāryamiṣṭaṃ vahniṃ gṛhāṇa tvamihopanītam .. 8 ..
16.34.d:
त्वमग्रजः सर्वभवोद्भवानां त्वं जीवितं जन्मवतां नराणाम् ..
तस्मात्सुराणां कुरु कार्यमिष्टं वह्निं गृहाण त्वमिहोपनीतम् .. 8 ..
16.34.m:
“You are the firstborn among all that arises in existence; you are the life of mortal beings.
Therefore, perform the desired task of the gods: receive the fire brought here.”

16.34.s:
atrāṃtare so'pi vimṛśya sarvaṃ kāryaṃ svabuddhyā kimihopapannam ..
kṛtvā'nalasya grahaṇaṃ mayedaṃ kāryaṃ surāṇāṃ vihitaṃ bhavecca .. 9 ..
16.34.d:
अत्रांतरे सोऽपि विमृश्य सर्वं कार्यं स्वबुद्ध्या किमिहोपपन्नम् ..
कृत्वाऽनलस्य ग्रहणं मयेदं कार्यं सुराणां विहितं भवेच्च .. 9 ..
16.34.m:
In the meantime, he too, considering the whole matter with his intellect as to what was fitting here, [thought]:
“By receiving this fire, the purpose of the gods will be accomplished by me.”

16.34.s:
evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya grahaṇaṃ rucitaṃ tataḥ ..
vāḍavāgneḥ samudrasya surapīḍākṛte yadā .. 7.1.34.10 ..
16.34.d:
एवं चिंतयतस्तस्य ग्रहणं रुचितं ततः ..
वाडवाग्नेः समुद्रस्य सुरपीडाकृते यदा .. 7.1.34.10 ..
16.34.m:
As he was thus thinking, the receiving of the submarine fire
became pleasing to the ocean, when it was for the relief of the gods' distress.

16.34.s:
tadā tena puraḥsthena devī sābhihitā bhṛśam ..
vāḍavaṃ saṃprayacchainaṃ suraśatruṃ sarasvati .. 11 ..
16.34.d:
तदा तेन पुरःस्थेन देवी साभिहिता भृशम् ..
वाडवं संप्रयच्छैनं सुरशत्रुं सरस्वति .. 11 ..
16.34.m:
Then that goddess was earnestly addressed by him who stood before her:
“Hand over this submarine fire, the enemy of the gods, O Sarasvatī!”

16.34.s:
tatastayā praṇamyāśu pitāmahapuraḥsarān ..
cāraṇāṃścārucitrāṃgyā sarasvatyā divi sthitān .. 12 ..
16.34.d:
ततस्तया प्रणम्याशु पितामहपुरःसरान् ..
चारणांश्चारुचित्रांग्या सरस्वत्या दिवि स्थितान् .. 12 ..
16.34.m:
Then, having quickly bowed to those headed by the Grandfather [Brahmā]
and to the cāraṇas stationed in heaven, Sarasvatī of beautiful and variegated limbs,

16.34.s:
punaśca karasaṃstho'sau vāḍavo'bhihitastayā ..
tvamapo bhakṣayasveti surairukta imā iti .. 13 ..
16.34.d:
पुनश्च करसंस्थोऽसौ वाडवोऽभिहितस्तया ..
त्वमपो भक्षयस्वेति सुरैरुक्त इमा इति .. 13 ..
16.34.m:
addressed the submarine fire resting in her hand once again:
“The gods have said, ‘Devour these waters!’”

16.34.s:
evamuktvā samudrasya tadā devyā samarppitaḥ ..
vāḍavo'gniḥ sarasvatyā surādeśānmahābalaḥ .. 14 ..
16.34.d:
एवमुक्त्वा समुद्रस्य तदा देव्या समर्प्पितः ..
वाडवोऽग्निः सरस्वत्या सुरादेशान्महाबलः .. 14 ..
16.34.m:
Having spoken thus, the mighty submarine fire was then delivered
to the ocean by the goddess Sarasvatī by order of the gods.

16.34.s:
taṃ samarpya tatastasmi nnadī bhūtvā sarasvatī ..
praviṣṭā sāgaraṃ devī nāradeśvaramārgataḥ .. 15 ..
16.34.d:
तं समर्प्य ततस्तस्मि न्नदी भूत्वा सरस्वती ..
प्रविष्टा सागरं देवी नारदेश्वरमार्गतः .. 15 ..
16.34.m:
Having delivered it, the goddess Sarasvatī then became a river,
and entered the ocean by the path of Nāradeśvara.

16.34.s:
daityasūdanasāṃnidhye dattvārghyaṃ lavaṇāṃbhasi ..
arghyeśvaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya daityasūdana paścime .. 16 ..
16.34.d:
दैत्यसूदनसांनिध्ये दत्त्वार्घ्यं लवणांभसि ..
अर्घ्येश्वरं प्रतिष्ठाप्य दैत्यसूदन पश्चिमे .. 16 ..
16.34.m:
Offering an arghya into the salt waters in the presence of Daityasūdana,
and installing Arghyeśvara to the west of Daityasūdana,

16.34.s:
tato'bdhiṃ saṃpraviṣṭā sā paṃcasrotā mahānadī ..
svarūpeṇaiva sā puṇyā punaḥ puṇyatamā'bhavat .. 17 ..
16.34.d:
ततोऽब्धिं संप्रविष्टा सा पंचस्रोता महानदी ..
स्वरूपेणैव सा पुण्या पुनः पुण्यतमाऽभवत् .. 17 ..
16.34.m:
that great five-streamed river then entered the sea;
holy by her very nature, she became even holier

16.34.s:
prabhāsakṣetrasaṃparkātsamudrasya ca saṃgamāt ..
sāgaro'pi samāsādya sarasvatyāstu vāḍavam ..
nirdhano vai dhanaṃ prāpyācintayatkva kṣipāmyaham .. 18 ..
16.34.d:
प्रभासक्षेत्रसंपर्कात्समुद्रस्य च संगमात् ..
सागरोऽपि समासाद्य सरस्वत्यास्तु वाडवम् ..
निर्धनो वै धनं प्राप्याचिन्तयत्क्व क्षिपाम्यहम् .. 18 ..
16.34.m:
through contact with Prabhāsakṣetra and union with the ocean.
The ocean too, having received the submarine fire from Sarasvatī,
thought, like a pauper who has found wealth: “Where shall I place it?”

16.34.s:
sa tenaiva karasthena dīpya mānena sāgaraḥ ..
vahninā śikharasthena bhāti merurivāparaḥ .. 19 ..
16.34.d:
स तेनैव करस्थेन दीप्य मानेन सागरः ..
वह्निना शिखरस्थेन भाति मेरुरिवापरः .. 19 ..
16.34.m:
With that fire blazing in his hand, placed upon his peak,
the ocean shone like another Mount Meru.

16.34.s:
taṃ tathāvidhamālokya tatra ye jalacāriṇaḥ ..
yādogaṇāste mumucurdāhabhītā mahāsvanam .. 7.1.34.20 ..
16.34.d:
तं तथाविधमालोक्य तत्र ये जलचारिणः ..
यादोगणास्ते मुमुचुर्दाहभीता महास्वनम् .. 7.1.34.20 ..
16.34.m:
Seeing him in that condition, the aquatic creatures that lived there,
the hosts of sea monsters, terrified of burning, raised a great cry.

16.34.s:
taṃ śrutvā bhairavaṃ śabdamāyāto daityasūdanaḥ ..
āha yādogaṇānsarvānmā bhaiṣṭa sumahābalāḥ .. 21 ..
16.34.d:
तं श्रुत्वा भैरवं शब्दमायातो दैत्यसूदनः ..
आह यादोगणान्सर्वान्मा भैष्ट सुमहाबलाः .. 21 ..
16.34.m:
Hearing that dreadful cry, Daityasūdana arrived
and said to all the hosts of sea monsters: “Do not fear, O very mighty ones!

16.34.s:
yasmādanena prathamā āpo bhakṣyā na tatragāḥ ..
prāṇinastanna bhetavyaṃ bhavadbhistu mamājñayā .. 22 ..
16.34.d:
यस्मादनेन प्रथमा आपो भक्ष्या न तत्रगाः ..
प्राणिनस्तन्न भेतव्यं भवद्भिस्तु ममाज्ञया .. 22 ..
16.34.m:
Since the waters are first to be devoured by him, not the creatures
dwelling in them, therefore you must not fear, by my command.”

16.34.s: evamuktastu kṛṣṇena tūṣṇīṃbhūtā jalecarāḥ .. 23 ..
16.34.d: एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन तूष्णींभूता जलेचराः .. 23 ..
16.34.m: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the aquatic creatures fell silent.

16.34.s:
tūṣṇīṃbhūteṣu sarveṣu jalajeṣu jaleśvaram ..
prāhācyutaḥ prakṣipa tvamapāṃ madhye tu vāḍavam .. 24 ..
16.34.d:
तूष्णींभूतेषु सर्वेषु जलजेषु जलेश्वरम् ..
प्राहाच्युतः प्रक्षिप त्वमपां मध्ये तु वाडवम् .. 24 ..
16.34.m: When all the aquatic creatures fell silent, Acyuta said to the lord of the waters: / "Cast the submarine fire into the midst of the waters."

16.34.s:
agādhembhasi tenāsau nikṣipto vāḍavo'nalaḥ ..
varuṇena pibannāste tajjalaṃ sumahābalaḥ .. 25 ..
16.34.d:
अगाधेम्भसि तेनासौ निक्षिप्तो वाडवोऽनलः ..
वरुणेन पिबन्नास्ते तज्जलं सुमहाबलः .. 25 ..
16.34.m: Then that submarine fire was cast into the deep water by Varuṇa; / drinking that water, he abides there, possessing exceedingly great power.

16.34.s:
tasyocchvāsāniloddhūtaṃ tattoyaṃ sāgarādbahiḥ ..
nirmaryādeva yuvatiritaścetaścadhāvati .. 26 ..
16.34.d:
तस्योच्छ्वासानिलोद्धूतं तत्तोयं सागराद्बहिः ..
निर्मर्यादेव युवतिरितश्चेतश्चधावति .. 26 ..
16.34.m: Agitated by the breath-wind from his exhale, that water beyond the ocean / runs hither and thither, like an unruly young woman.

16.34.s:
atha kāle gate devi śuṣyatyaṃbu śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
viditvā kṣīyamāṇāstā apo jalanidhistataḥ .. 27 ..
16.34.d:
अथ काले गते देवि शुष्यत्यंबु शनैःशनैः ..
विदित्वा क्षीयमाणास्ता अपो जलनिधिस्ततः .. 27 ..
16.34.m: Then, as time passed, O goddess, the water slowly dried up; / perceiving that those waters were being depleted, the ocean thereupon

16.34.s:
āhaivaṃ puṃḍarīkākṣamapaḥ kuru tvamakṣayāḥ ..
anyathā sarvanāśena jalānāṃ māmihāgrataḥ ..
bhakṣayiṣyatyasau vahnirvāḍavo hi janārddana .. 28 ..
16.34.d:
आहैवं पुंडरीकाक्षमपः कुरु त्वमक्षयाः ..
अन्यथा सर्वनाशेन जलानां मामिहाग्रतः ..
भक्षयिष्यत्यसौ वह्निर्वाडवो हि जनार्द्दन .. 28 ..
16.34.m: spoke thus to the lotus-eyed one: "Make the waters inexhaustible; / otherwise, upon the complete destruction of the waters, Janārdana, this submarine fire will devour me next!"

16.34.s:
etacchrutvā vacastasya samudrasya tu bhīṣaṇam ..
kṛtaṃ tadakṣayaṃ toyamā tmano bhayanāśanam .. 29 ..
16.34.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य समुद्रस्य तु भीषणम् ..
कृतं तदक्षयं तोयमा त्मनो भयनाशनम् .. 29 ..
16.34.m: Hearing this terrifying statement from the ocean, / he made that water inexhaustible, destroying his fear.

16.34.s:
jñātvā surāḥ sarvamidaṃ viceṣṭitaṃ kṛtyānalasyāsya nibaṃdhanaṃ tathā ..
pralobhanaṃ toyapuraḥsarā dviṣaḥ pupūjire keśavamatra cāriṇam.. 7.1.34.30 ..
16.34.d:
ज्ञात्वा सुराः सर्वमिदं विचेष्टितं कृत्यानलस्यास्य निबंधनं तथा ..
प्रलोभनं तोयपुरःसरा द्विषः पुपूजिरे केशवमत्र चारिणम्.. 7.1.34.30 ..
16.34.m: Knowing this entire deed, the restraint of this fire, / and the enticement accompanied by water, the gods worshipped Keśava as he moved there.

16.34.s:
evaṃ sarasvatī prāptā prabhāsaṃ kṣetramuttamam ..
brahmalokānmahādevi sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .. 31 ..
16.34.d:
एवं सरस्वती प्राप्ता प्रभासं क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..
ब्रह्मलोकान्महादेवि सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .. 31 ..
16.34.m: Thus Sarasvatī, destroyer of all sins, / arrived at the excellent sacred field of Prabhāsa from the world of Brahmā, O great goddess.

16.34.s:
someśāddakṣiṇāgneye sāgarasya samī pataḥ ..
saṃsthitā tu mahādevī vaḍavānaladhāriṇī .. 32 ..
16.34.d:
सोमेशाद्दक्षिणाग्नेये सागरस्य समी पतः ..
संस्थिता तु महादेवी वडवानलधारिणी .. 32 ..
16.34.m: South-east of Someśa, near the ocean, / the great goddess stays, bearing the submarine fire.

16.34.s:
snātvā'gnitīrthe pūrvaṃ tāṃ pūjayedvidhinā naraḥ ..
daṃpatyorbhojanaṃ tatra paridhānaṃ sakañcu kam .. 33 ..
16.34.d:
स्नात्वाऽग्नितीर्थे पूर्वं तां पूजयेद्विधिना नरः ..
दंपत्योर्भोजनं तत्र परिधानं सकञ्चु कम् .. 33 ..
16.34.m: Having first bathed at Agnitīrtha, a man should worship her according to rule; / there [should be offered] food to a married couple, and garments with bodices.

16.34.s:
dattvā tato mahādevaṃ pūjayecca kaparddinam ..
iti vṛttaṃ purā devi cākṣuṣasyāṃtare'bhavat .. 34 ..
16.34.d:
दत्त्वा ततो महादेवं पूजयेच्च कपर्द्दिनम् ..
इति वृत्तं पुरा देवि चाक्षुषस्यांतरेऽभवत् .. 34 ..
16.34.m: Having given [these], he should then worship Mahādeva Kapardin. / Such was the event, O goddess, that occurred formerly in the Cākṣuṣa manvantara,

16.34.s:
dadhīcyanvayajātasya vāḍavasya mahā tmanaḥ ..
asminpunarmahādevi prāpte vaivasvateṃ'tare ..
aurvastu bhārgave vaṃśe samutpanno mahādvijaḥ .. 35..
16.34.d:
दधीच्यन्वयजातस्य वाडवस्य महा त्मनः ..
अस्मिन्पुनर्महादेवि प्राप्ते वैवस्वतेंऽतरे ..
और्वस्तु भार्गवे वंशे समुत्पन्नो महाद्विजः .. 35..
16.34.m: concerning the great-souled submarine fire born in the lineage of Dadhīci. / When, O great goddess, this present Vaivasvata manvantara arrived, / Aurva, the great twice-born, was born in the lineage of Bhṛgu.

16.34.s:
saṃkṣipto'sau sarasvatyā devamātrā mahāprabhaḥ..
tāvatsthāsyatyapāṃ garbhe yāvanmanvatarāvadhiḥ .. 36 ..
16.34.d:
संक्षिप्तोऽसौ सरस्वत्या देवमात्रा महाप्रभः..
तावत्स्थास्यत्यपां गर्भे यावन्मन्वतरावधिः .. 36 ..
16.34.m: Restrained by Sarasvatī, the mother of the gods, he of great radiance / will remain within the waters until the end of the manvantara.

16.34.s:
iti te kathitaṃ devi sarasvatyāḥ samudbhavam ..
śrutaṃ pāpaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ kīrttidaṃ puṇyavarddhanam.. 37 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye sarasvatyavatāramahimavarṇanaṃnāma catustriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 34 .. .. cha ..
16.34.d:
इति ते कथितं देवि सरस्वत्याः समुद्भवम् ..
श्रुतं पापहरं नृणां कीर्त्तिदं पुण्यवर्द्धनम्.. 37 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सरस्वत्यवतारमहिमवर्णनंनाम चतुस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 34 .. .. छ ..
16.34.m:
Thus the origin of Sarasvatī has been told to you, O goddess; / when heard, it removes the sins of mortals, grants renown, and increases merit.
Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled 'Description of the Greatness of the Descent of Sarasvatī', in the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, the first [subdivision] of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, the seventh [book] of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

16.35.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
bhagavanbhārgave vaṃśe yastvaurvaḥ kathitastvayā ..
vaivasvateṃ'tare cāsmiṃstasyotpattiṃ vada prabho .. 1 ..
16.35.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
भगवन्भार्गवे वंशे यस्त्वौर्वः कथितस्त्वया ..
वैवस्वतेंऽतरे चास्मिंस्तस्योत्पत्तिं वद प्रभो .. 1 ..
16.35.m: The goddess said: / "O Lord, tell of the birth of Aurva, whom you mentioned / as born in the Bhārgava lineage during this Vaivasvata manvantara, O master."

16.35.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
brāhmaṇā nihatā ye tu kṣatriyairvittakāraṇāt ..
kṣayaṃ nītāstu te sarve saputrāśca sagarbhataḥ .. 2 ..
16.35.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ब्राह्मणा निहता ये तु क्षत्रियैर्वित्तकारणात् ..
क्षयं नीतास्तु ते सर्वे सपुत्राश्च सगर्भतः .. 2 ..
16.35.m: Īśvara said: / "The brahmins who were slaughtered by the kṣatriyas for the sake of wealth— / they were all brought to destruction, along with their sons and the unborn in the womb.

16.35.s:
mriyamāṇeṣu sarveṣu ekā strī samatiṣṭhata ..
tayā tu rakṣito garbha ūrvordeśe nidhāya ca .. 3 ..
16.35.d:
म्रियमाणेषु सर्वेषु एका स्त्री समतिष्ठत ..
तया तु रक्षितो गर्भ ऊर्वोर्देशे निधाय च .. 3 ..
16.35.m: When all were being killed, one woman remained; / by her the embryo was preserved, placed in her thigh.

16.35.s:
anyāsāṃ caiva nārīṇāṃ sarvāsāmapi bhāmini ..
garbhāni pātitāstaistu dravyārthaṃ kṣatriyādhamaiḥ .. 4 ..
16.35.d:
अन्यासां चैव नारीणां सर्वासामपि भामिनि ..
गर्भानि पातितास्तैस्तु द्रव्यार्थं क्षत्रियाधमैः .. 4 ..
16.35.m: And in the case of all other women, O lovely woman, / the embryos were aborted by those vile kṣatriyas for the sake of wealth.

16.35.s:
kālāṃtare tato bhittvā kurudeśaṃ mahāprabhaḥ ..
nirgatottaṃbhitaśirā jvaladāsyotibhīṣaṇaḥ .. 5 ..
16.35.d:
कालांतरे ततो भित्त्वा कुरुदेशं महाप्रभः ..
निर्गतोत्तंभितशिरा ज्वलदास्योतिभीषणः .. 5 ..
16.35.m: Then, in the course of time, bursting forth from the thigh, the exceedingly radiant one / emerged with raised head, a blazing face, and terrifying aspect.

16.35.s:
tadvairaṃ hṛdi cādhāya dadāha vasudhātalam ..
utpādya vahniṃ tapasā raudramaurvaṃ jalāśanam .. 6 ..
16.35.d:
तद्वैरं हृदि चाधाय ददाह वसुधातलम् ..
उत्पाद्य वह्निं तपसा रौद्रमौर्वं जलाशनम् .. 6 ..
16.35.m: Holding that enmity in his heart, he burned the surface of the earth, / having generated through austerity the dreadful fire Aurva, whose food is water.

16.35.s:
tamindraḥ plāvayāmāsa vṛṣṭyaughairvaravarṇini ..
na śaśāka yadā netuṃ tadā sa yatavāksthitaḥ .. 7 ..
16.35.d:
तमिन्द्रः प्लावयामास वृष्ट्यौघैर्वरवर्णिनि ..
न शशाक यदा नेतुं तदा स यतवाक्स्थितः .. 7 ..
16.35.m: Indra inundated him with torrential rains, O lady of fair complexion; / when he could not subdue him, he then remained keeping silence.

16.35.s:
tato devāḥ sagaṃdharvā brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ..
abhavanbhayasaṃtrastāḥ sarve prāṃjalayaḥ sthitāḥ .. 8 ..
16.35.d:
ततो देवाः सगंधर्वा ब्रह्माणं शरणं गताः ..
अभवन्भयसंत्रस्ताः सर्वे प्रांजलयः स्थिताः .. 8 ..
16.35.m: Then the gods, along with the gandharvas, took refuge with Brahmā; / terrified with fear, they all stood with folded hands.

16.35.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
bhagavanbhārgave vaṃśe jātaḥ ko'pi mahādyutiḥ ..
agnirūpeṇa sarvaṃ sa dadāha vasudhātalam .. ..
kṛto yatnaḥ purā'smābhistadvināśāya sattama ..
jalena vṛddhimāyāti tato no bhayamāgatam .. 7.1.35.10 ..
16.35.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
भगवन्भार्गवे वंशे जातः कोऽपि महाद्युतिः ..
अग्निरूपेण सर्वं स ददाह वसुधातलम् .. ..
कृतो यत्नः पुराऽस्माभिस्तद्विनाशाय सत्तम ..
जलेन वृद्धिमायाति ततो नो भयमागतम् .. 7.1.35.10 ..
16.35.m: The gods said: / "O Lord, someone of great splendour has been born in the lineage of Bhṛgu; / in the form of fire, he has burned the entire surface of the earth. / An effort was made previously by us to destroy him, O best of beings, / [yet] through water he increases, and so fear has come upon us.

16.35.s:
vinaṣṭe bhūtale deva agniṣṭomādikāḥ kriyāḥ..
ucchidyate tato'smākaṃ nāśo nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 11 ..
16.35.d:
विनष्टे भूतले देव अग्निष्टोमादिकाः क्रियाः..
उच्छिद्यते ततोऽस्माकं नाशो नूनं भविष्यति .. 11 ..
16.35.m: When the surface of the earth is destroyed, O god, rites such as the Agniṣṭoma / will be broken off; from that, our destruction will surely come about.

16.35.s: tasmādyatnaṃ kuru vibho trailokyahitakāmyayā .. 12 ..
16.35.d: तस्माद्यत्नं कुरु विभो त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया .. 12 ..
16.35.m: Therefore, O all-pervading one, make an effort out of a desire for the welfare of the three worlds."

16.35.s:
tato brahmā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ bhārgavaiśca maharṣibhiḥ ..
āgatya cābravīdaurvaṃ kimarthaṃ dahasi kṣitim .. 13 ..
16.35.d:
ततो ब्रह्मा सुरैः सार्द्धं भार्गवैश्च महर्षिभिः ..
आगत्य चाब्रवीदौर्वं किमर्थं दहसि क्षितिम् .. 13 ..
16.35.m: Then Brahmā, having come together with the gods and the great seers of the Bhārgava lineage, / said to Aurva: "Why are you burning the earth?

16.35.s: virāmaḥ kriyatāṃ sadyo mamārthaṃ ca dvijottama.. 14 ..
16.35.d: विरामः क्रियतां सद्यो ममार्थं च द्विजोत्तम.. 14 ..
16.35.m: Let a cessation be made immediately for my sake, O best of the twice-born."

16.35.s:
.. aurva uvāca .. ..
eṣa eva nivṛtto'haṃ tava vākyena sattama ..
eṣa vahnirmayotsṛṣṭaḥ sa vibho tava śāsanāt .. 15 ..
16.35.d:
.. और्व उवाच .. ..
एष एव निवृत्तोऽहं तव वाक्येन सत्तम ..
एष वह्निर्मयोत्सृष्टः स विभो तव शासनात् .. 15 ..
16.35.m: Aurva said: / "I have indeed desisted at your word, O best of beings; / this fire was emitted by me, O all-pervading one, by your command.

16.35.s: yathā gacchetsamudrāṃtaṃ tathā nītirvidhīya tām .. 16 ..
16.35.d: यथा गच्छेत्समुद्रांतं तथा नीतिर्विधीय ताम् .. 16 ..
16.35.m: Let a strategy be devised so that it may reach the ocean."

16.35.s:
samāhūya tato devīṃ svāṃ sutāṃ padmasaṃbhavaḥ ..
uvāca putri gaccha tvaṃ gṛhītvāgniṃ mahodadhim ..
madvākyaṃ nānyathā kāryaṃ gaccha śīghraṃ mahāprabhe .. 17 ..
16.35.d:
समाहूय ततो देवीं स्वां सुतां पद्मसंभवः ..
उवाच पुत्रि गच्छ त्वं गृहीत्वाग्निं महोदधिम् ..
मद्वाक्यं नान्यथा कार्यं गच्छ शीघ्रं महाप्रभे .. 17 ..
16.35.m: Then the lotus-born, having summoned his own daughter, the goddess, / said: 'Daughter, taking the fire, go to the great ocean; / my command must not be neglected; go quickly, O exceedingly radiant one!'"

16.35.s:
.. sarasvatyuvāca .. ..
eṣāsmi prasthitā deva tava vākyādasaṃśayam ..
ityukte sādhu sādhvīti brahmaṇā samudāhṛtā .. .. 18 ..
16.35.d:
.. सरस्वत्युवाच .. ..
एषास्मि प्रस्थिता देव तव वाक्यादसंशयम् ..
इत्युक्ते साधु साध्वीति ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृता .. .. 18 ..
16.35.m: Sarasvatī said: / "Here I set forth, O god, at your word, without doubt." / When she had said this, she was commended by Brahmā: 'Well done, virtuous lady!'

16.35.s:
tatobhimaṃtritaṃ vahniṃ kṣiptvā kuṃbhe hiraṇmaye ..
prāyacchata sarasvatyai svayaṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ ..
āśiṣo vividhā dattvā provācedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ .. 19 ..
16.35.d:
ततोभिमंत्रितं वह्निं क्षिप्त्वा कुंभे हिरण्मये ..
प्रायच्छत सरस्वत्यै स्वयं ब्रह्मा पितामहः ..
आशिषो विविधा दत्त्वा प्रोवाचेदं पुनः पुनः .. 19 ..
16.35.m: Then, having placed the consecrated fire in a golden pot, / Grandfather Brahmā himself handed it to Sarasvatī; / bestowing various blessings, he spoke thus again and again:

16.35.s:
gaccha putri na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃcana ..
ariṣṭaṃ vraja paṃthānaṃ mā saṃtu paripanthinaḥ .. 7.1.35.20 ..
16.35.d:
गच्छ पुत्रि न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः कथंचन ..
अरिष्टं व्रज पंथानं मा संतु परिपन्थिनः .. 7.1.35.20 ..
16.35.m: "Go, daughter! No sorrow should be felt by you in any way; / proceed along a path free from misfortune; let there be no adversaries!"

16.35.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
evamuktā tadā tena brahmaṇā ca sarasvatī ..
himavaṃtaṃ giriṃ prāpya pippalādāśramāttadā .. 21 ..
16.35.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्ता तदा तेन ब्रह्मणा च सरस्वती ..
हिमवंतं गिरिं प्राप्य पिप्पलादाश्रमात्तदा .. 21 ..
16.35.m: Īśvara said: / "Thus addressed at that time by Brahmā, Sarasvatī / reached Mount Himavat from the hermitage of Pippalāda at that time.

16.35.s:
udbhūtā sā tadā devī adhastādvṛkṣamūlataḥ ..
tatkoṭara kuṭīkoṭipraviṣṭānāṃ dvijanmanām .. 22 ..
16.35.d:
उद्भूता सा तदा देवी अधस्ताद्वृक्षमूलतः ..
तत्कोटर कुटीकोटिप्रविष्टानां द्विजन्मनाम् .. 22 ..
16.35.m: The goddess then emerged beneath the root of a tree / where the sounds of the Vedas of the twice-born / who had entered crores of hollows and huts

16.35.s:
śrūyante vedanirghoṣā sarasāraktacetasām ..
viṣṇurāste tatra devo devānāṃ pravaro guruḥ .. 23 ..
16.35.d:
श्रूयन्ते वेदनिर्घोषा सरसारक्तचेतसाम् ..
विष्णुरास्ते तत्र देवो देवानां प्रवरो गुरुः .. 23 ..
16.35.m: were heard, their minds passionately delighting in [them]; / there stays God Viṣṇu, the foremost teacher of the gods.

16.35.s:
tasmātsthānāttato devī pratīcyabhimukhaṃ yayau ..
antarddhānena sā prāptā kedāraṃ himamadhyagam .. 24 ..
16.35.d:
तस्मात्स्थानात्ततो देवी प्रतीच्यभिमुखं ययौ ..
अन्तर्द्धानेन सा प्राप्ता केदारं हिममध्यगम् .. 24 ..
16.35.m: From that place the goddess then went westward; / through disappearance she reached Kedāra, situated in the midst of snow.

16.35.s:
tatsaṃplāvya gireḥ śṛṃgaṃ kedārasya puraḥ sthitā ..
tenāgninā karasthena dahyamānā sarasvatī .. 25 ..
16.35.d:
तत्संप्लाव्य गिरेः शृंगं केदारस्य पुरः स्थिता ..
तेनाग्निना करस्थेन दह्यमाना सरस्वती .. 25 ..
16.35.m: Having inundated that mountain peak, she stood before Kedāra; / burning with that fire held in her hand, Sarasvatī,

16.35.s:
bhūmiṃ vidārya tasyādhaḥ praviṣṭā gajagāminī ..
tadaṃtarddhānamārgeṇa pravṛttā paścimāmukhī .. 26 ..
16.35.d:
भूमिं विदार्य तस्याधः प्रविष्टा गजगामिनी ..
तदंतर्द्धानमार्गेण प्रवृत्ता पश्चिमामुखी .. 26 ..
16.35.m: she of elephant-like gait, cleaved the earth and entered beneath it; / then, by way of an invisible path, she proceeded facing west.

16.35.s:
pāpabhūmimatikramya bhūmiṃ bhittvā vini(?)gatā ..
tatra kūpaḥ samabhavannāmnā gandharvasaṃjñitaḥ .. 27 ..
16.35.d:
पापभूमिमतिक्रम्य भूमिं भित्त्वा विनि(?)गता ..
तत्र कूपः समभवन्नाम्ना गन्धर्वसंज्ञितः .. 27 ..
16.35.m: Having passed beyond the sinful land, she split the ground and came out. / A well formed there, known by the name Gandharva.

16.35.s:
tasmātkūpātpunardṛśyā sā babhūva mahānadī ..
matiḥ smṛtistathā prajñā medhā buddhirgirādharā .. 28 ..
16.35.d:
तस्मात्कूपात्पुनर्दृश्या सा बभूव महानदी ..
मतिः स्मृतिस्तथा प्रज्ञा मेधा बुद्धिर्गिराधरा .. 28 ..
16.35.m: From that well the great river became visible once more: / Mati, Smṛti, Prajñā, Medhā, Buddhi, and Girādharā—

16.35.s:
upāsikāḥ sarasvatyāḥ ṣaḍetāḥ prasthitāstadā ..
punaḥ pravṛttā sā tasmādudbhedātpaścimāmukhī ..29..
16.35.d:
उपासिकाः सरस्वत्याः षडेताः प्रस्थितास्तदा ..
पुनः प्रवृत्ता सा तस्मादुद्भेदात्पश्चिमामुखी ..29..
16.35.m: these six attendants of Sarasvatī set forth then. / From that fissure she proceeded again, facing westward,

16.35.s:
bhūtīśvaraṃ samāyātā siddho yatra mahāmuniḥ ..
bhūtīśvare samīpasthaṃ tatra prāptā manoramam ..7.1.35.30..
16.35.d:
भूतीश्वरं समायाता सिद्धो यत्र महामुनिः ..
भूतीश्वरे समीपस्थं तत्र प्राप्ता मनोरमम् ..7.1.35.30..
16.35.m: and reached Bhūtīśvara, where the great sage attained perfection. / Close to Bhūtīśvara, she arrived at that delightful spot.

16.35.s:
tasya dakṣiṇadiksaṃsthaṃ rudrakoṭyupalakṣitam ..
śrīkaṃṭha deśaṃ vikhyātaṃ gatā sarvauṣadhīyutam .. 31 ..
16.35.d:
तस्य दक्षिणदिक्संस्थं रुद्रकोट्युपलक्षितम् ..
श्रीकंठ देशं विख्यातं गता सर्वौषधीयुतम् .. 31 ..
16.35.m: Situated to its south, distinguished by Rudrakoṭi, / she went to the celebrated region of Śrīkaṇṭha, endowed with all medicinal herbs.

16.35.s:
tasmātpuṇyatamāddeśācchrīkaṇṭhātsā manasvinī ..
saṃprāptā vahninā sārddhaṃ kurukṣetraṃ sarasvatī .. 32 ..
16.35.d:
तस्मात्पुण्यतमाद्देशाच्छ्रीकण्ठात्सा मनस्विनी ..
संप्राप्ता वह्निना सार्द्धं कुरुक्षेत्रं सरस्वती .. 32 ..
16.35.m: From that most holy region of Śrīkaṇṭha, the noble-minded river, / Sarasvatī, along with the fire, arrived at Kurukṣetra.

16.35.s:
punastasmātkurukṣetrādvirāṭanagarasya sā ..
samudbhūtā samīpasthā antarddhānānmanoramā ..
gopāyano giriryatra tatra sā punarudgatā .. 33 ..
16.35.d:
पुनस्तस्मात्कुरुक्षेत्राद्विराटनगरस्य सा ..
समुद्भूता समीपस्था अन्तर्द्धानान्मनोरमा ..
गोपायनो गिरिर्यत्र तत्र सा पुनरुद्गता .. 33 ..
16.35.m: Then, from that Kurukṣetra, emerging near the city of Virāṭa / out of her underground course, the delightful goddess / rose up again where Mount Gopāyana stands.

16.35.s:
gopāyitā keśavena yatra te pāṇḍunandanāḥ ..
kurvaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi na kaiścidupalakṣitā .. 34 ..
16.35.d:
गोपायिता केशवेन यत्र ते पाण्डुनन्दनाः ..
कुर्वंतः स्वानि कर्माणि न कैश्चिदुपलक्षिता .. 34 ..
16.35.m: It was there that those sons of Pāṇḍu were hidden by Keśava, / performing their appointed tasks without being noticed by anyone.

16.35.s:
tatra kuṃḍe sthitā devī mahāpātakanāśinī ..
puna rgopāyanāddevī kṣetraṃ prāptātiśobhanam .. 35 ..
16.35.d:
तत्र कुंडे स्थिता देवी महापातकनाशिनी ..
पुन र्गोपायनाद्देवी क्षेत्रं प्राप्तातिशोभनम् .. 35 ..
16.35.m: Remaining there in a pool, the goddess who destroys heinous sins, / the goddess went further from Gopāyana to an exceedingly beautiful sacred field.

16.35.s:
kharjurīvanamāpannā nandānāmnīti tatra sā ..
sarasvatī punastasmādvanātkharjūrasaṃjñitāt .. 36 ..
16.35.d:
खर्जुरीवनमापन्ना नन्दानाम्नीति तत्र सा ..
सरस्वती पुनस्तस्माद्वनात्खर्जूरसंज्ञितात् .. 36 ..
16.35.m: Reaching the Kharjūrī forest, she was known there as Nandā. / Then, from that forest named Kharjūra, the river Sarasvatī,

16.35.s:
merupādaṃ samāsādya mārkaṃḍāśramamāgatā ..
yatra mārkaṃḍakaṃ tīrthaṃ merupāde samāśritam .. 37 ..
16.35.d:
मेरुपादं समासाद्य मार्कंडाश्रममागता ..
यत्र मार्कंडकं तीर्थं मेरुपादे समाश्रितम् .. 37 ..
16.35.m: approaching the foot of Meru, arrived at the hermitage of Mārkaṇḍa, / where the sacred ford Mārkaṇḍaka is located at the foot of Meru.

16.35.s:
sarasvatī punastasmādarbudāraṇyamāśritā ..
gatā vaṭavanaṃ ramyaṃ mārkaṃḍeyāśramācchubhāt ..38..
16.35.d:
सरस्वती पुनस्तस्मादर्बुदारण्यमाश्रिता ..
गता वटवनं रम्यं मार्कंडेयाश्रमाच्छुभात् ..38..
16.35.m: From that auspicious hermitage of Mārkaṇḍeya, Sarasvatī then / entered the Arbuda forest and proceeded to the charming Vaṭa forest,

16.35.s:
tapastaptaṃ purā yatra vasiṣṭhena samāśritāt ..
tasmādvaṭavanātpuṇyādudumbaravanaṃ gatā ..
merupāde ca tatraiva taṇḍiryatrā tapattapaḥ .. 39 ..
16.35.d:
तपस्तप्तं पुरा यत्र वसिष्ठेन समाश्रितात् ..
तस्माद्वटवनात्पुण्यादुदुम्बरवनं गता ..
मेरुपादे च तत्रैव तण्डिर्यत्रा तपत्तपः .. 39 ..
16.35.m: where Vasiṣṭha formerly performed austerity. Having resorted to it, / she went from that holy Vaṭa forest to the Udumbara forest, / located right there at the foot of Meru, where Taṇḍi performed austerity.

16.35.s:
ūduṃbaravanāttasmātpunardevī sarasvatī ..
antarddhānena śikharamanyatprāptā mahānadī .. 7.1.35.40 ..
16.35.d:
ऊदुंबरवनात्तस्मात्पुनर्देवी सरस्वती ..
अन्तर्द्धानेन शिखरमन्यत्प्राप्ता महानदी .. 7.1.35.40 ..
16.35.m: From that Udumbara forest, the divine river Sarasvatī, / the great river, reaching another peak through underground flow,

16.35.s:
merupādaṃ tu sumahatsurasiddhaniṣevitam ..
bhinnāṃjanacayākāraṃ golāṃgūlamiti smṛtam .. 41 ..
16.35.d:
मेरुपादं तु सुमहत्सुरसिद्धनिषेवितम् ..
भिन्नांजनचयाकारं गोलांगूलमिति स्मृतम् .. 41 ..
16.35.m: came to the foot of Meru—vast, attended by gods and siddhas, / shaped like a mass of crushed collyrium, known as Golāṅgūla.

16.35.s:
sthānaṃ manoramaṃ tasmādudgatā sā sumadhyamā ..
vaṃśastaṃbātsuvipulā pravṛttā dakṣiṇāmukhī .. 42 ..
16.35.d:
स्थानं मनोरमं तस्मादुद्गता सा सुमध्यमा ..
वंशस्तंबात्सुविपुला प्रवृत्ता दक्षिणामुखी .. 42 ..
16.35.m: From that delightful place, she of slender waist emerged; / exceptionally broad, she proceeded southward from a clump of bamboo.

16.35.s:
tatrodgamavaṭastasyāstatsamākhyo vyavasthitaḥ ..
tataḥ prabhṛti sā devī suprabhaṃ prakaṭā sthitā .. 43 ..
16.35.d:
तत्रोद्गमवटस्तस्यास्तत्समाख्यो व्यवस्थितः ..
ततः प्रभृति सा देवी सुप्रभं प्रकटा स्थिता .. 43 ..
16.35.m: The banyan tree of her emergence, named after her, stands there. / From that time onward, that goddess remained visible and radiant,

16.35.s:
aṃtarddhānaṃ parityajya prāṇināmanukampayā ..
tasyāstaṭeṣu ramyeṣu saṃti tīrthāni koṭiśaḥ .. 44 ..
16.35.d:
अंतर्द्धानं परित्यज्य प्राणिनामनुकम्पया ..
तस्यास्तटेषु रम्येषु संति तीर्थानि कोटिशः .. 44 ..
16.35.m: abandoning her hidden course out of compassion for living beings. / On her delightful banks are sacred fords by the millions.

16.35.s:
teṣu tīrtheṣu sarveṣu dharmahetuḥ sarasvatī ..
rudrāvatāramārge'sminpravaraṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam .. 45 ..
16.35.d:
तेषु तीर्थेषु सर्वेषु धर्महेतुः सरस्वती ..
रुद्रावतारमार्गेऽस्मिन्प्रवरं प्रथमं स्मृतम् .. 45 ..
16.35.m: Among all those sacred fords, Sarasvatī is the cause of righteousness. / On this path of Rudra's descent, the first and foremost is remembered

16.35.s:
tarattaraṃganāmāḍhyaṃ kākatīrthaṃ mahāprabham ..
tatra tīrthaṃ punastvanyattīrthaṃ dhāreśvaraṃ smṛtam .. 46 ..
16.35.d:
तरत्तरंगनामाढ्यं काकतीर्थं महाप्रभम् ..
तत्र तीर्थं पुनस्त्वन्यत्तीर्थं धारेश्वरं स्मृतम् .. 46 ..
16.35.m: as Kākatīrtha of great splendor, abounding with the name Tarattaraṅga. / Further on is another sacred ford remembered as Dhāreśvara.

16.35.s:
dhāreśvarātpunaścānyadgaṃgodbhedamiti smṛtam ..
sārasvataṃ tathā gāṃgaṃ yatraikaṃ saṃsthitaṃ jalam ..
tasmādanyatparaṃ tīrthaṃ puṃḍarīkaṃ tataḥ param .. .. 47 ..
16.35.d:
धारेश्वरात्पुनश्चान्यद्गंगोद्भेदमिति स्मृतम् ..
सारस्वतं तथा गांगं यत्रैकं संस्थितं जलम् ..
तस्मादन्यत्परं तीर्थं पुंडरीकं ततः परम् .. .. 47 ..
16.35.m: Beyond Dhāreśvara is another remembered as Gaṅgodbheda, / where the water of Sarasvatī and that of the Gaṅgā unite as one. / Beyond that is another supreme sacred ford, Puṇḍarīka; then beyond that

16.35.s:
mātṛtīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvātaṃkaharaṃ param ..
mātṛtīrthātpunastasmānnātidūre vyavasthitam .. 48 ..
16.35.d:
मातृतीर्थं महापुण्यं सर्वातंकहरं परम् ..
मातृतीर्थात्पुनस्तस्मान्नातिदूरे व्यवस्थितम् .. 48 ..
16.35.m: is Mātṛtīrtha, most holy, dispelling all distress, supreme. / Further, not very far from that Mātṛtīrtha, is situated

16.35.s:
tīrthaṃ tvanarakaṃnāma narakārti bhayāpaham ..
tatastasmādanarakāttīrthamanyatpunaḥ sthitam .. 49 ..
16.35.d:
तीर्थं त्वनरकंनाम नरकार्ति भयापहम् ..
ततस्तस्मादनरकात्तीर्थमन्यत्पुनः स्थितम् .. 49 ..
16.35.m: the sacred ford named Anaraka, which removes the dread of the torment of hell. / Beyond that Anaraka stands yet another sacred ford,

16.35.s:
saṃgameśvaranāmāḍhyaṃ prasiddhaṃ tanmahītale ..
tatastasmātpunaścānyattīrthaṃ koṭīśvarāhvayam .. 7.1.35.50 ..
16.35.d:
संगमेश्वरनामाढ्यं प्रसिद्धं तन्महीतले ..
ततस्तस्मात्पुनश्चान्यत्तीर्थं कोटीश्वराह्वयम् .. 7.1.35.50 ..
16.35.m: renowned on the face of the earth by the name Saṅgameśvara. / Then from that is another sacred ford named Koṭīśvara.

16.35.s:
tatastasmānmahādevi śaṃbhukuṇḍeśvaraṃ smṛtam ..
tīrthe sarasvatītīre tasminsiddheśvaraṃ smṛtam .. 51 ..
16.35.d:
ततस्तस्मान्महादेवि शंभुकुण्डेश्वरं स्मृतम् ..
तीर्थे सरस्वतीतीरे तस्मिन्सिद्धेश्वरं स्मृतम् .. 51 ..
16.35.m: Beyond that, O great goddess, Śambhukuṇḍeśvara is remembered; / and at that sacred ford on the bank of the Sarasvatī, Siddheśvara is remembered.

16.35.s:
siddheśvarātpunastasmātpravṛttā paścimāmukhī ..
paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ gaṃtuṃ sakhīṃ smṛtvā ruroda sā ..52..
16.35.d:
सिद्धेश्वरात्पुनस्तस्मात्प्रवृत्ता पश्चिमामुखी ..
पश्चिमं सागरं गंतुं सखीं स्मृत्वा रुरोद सा ..52..
16.35.m: From that Siddheśvara, turning westward again / to go toward the western ocean, she wept, remembering her friend.

16.35.s:
sthitvā pūrvamukhā devī hā gaṃgeti vinā tvayā..
ekākinī maṃdabhāgyā kva gamiṣyāmyabāṃdhavā .. 53 ..
16.35.d:
स्थित्वा पूर्वमुखा देवी हा गंगेति विना त्वया..
एकाकिनी मंदभाग्या क्व गमिष्याम्यबांधवा .. 53 ..
16.35.m: Standing facing the east, the goddess cried: “Ah, Gaṅgā! Without you, / where shall I, alone, ill-fated, and without kin, go?”

16.35.s:
tāṃ vijñāya tato gaṃgā rudatīṃ śokakarśitām ..
śīghraṃ svargātsamāyātā tīrthānāṃ koṭibhiḥ saha .. 54 ..
16.35.d:
तां विज्ञाय ततो गंगा रुदतीं शोककर्शिताम् ..
शीघ्रं स्वर्गात्समायाता तीर्थानां कोटिभिः सह .. 54 ..
16.35.m: Perceiving her weeping, emaciated by grief, the Gaṅgā then / quickly arrived from heaven along with millions of sacred fords.

16.35.s:
tato duḥkhaṃ parityajya tatra prācī sarasvatī ..
sarvadevaguṇaiyuktā evaṃ tatra sthitā'bhavat .. 55 ..
16.35.d:
ततो दुःखं परित्यज्य तत्र प्राची सरस्वती ..
सर्वदेवगुणैयुक्ता एवं तत्र स्थिताऽभवत् .. 55 ..
16.35.m: Casting aside her sorrow, the east-flowing Sarasvatī, / endowed with all divine virtues, remained there in that manner.

16.35.s:
tatra siddhavaṭaṃnāma tīrthaṃ paitāmahaṃ smṛtam ..
vaṭeśvarasya purataḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .. 56 ..
16.35.d:
तत्र सिद्धवटंनाम तीर्थं पैतामहं स्मृतम् ..
वटेश्वरस्य पुरतः सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .. 56 ..
16.35.m: There is a sacred ford named Siddhavaṭa, belonging to the Grandfather, / situated before Vaṭeśvara, destroying all sins.

16.35.s:
trikālaṃ yatra rudrastu samāgatya vyavasthitaḥ ..
tanmahālayamityuktaṃ sthānaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ .. .. 57 ..
16.35.d:
त्रिकालं यत्र रुद्रस्तु समागत्य व्यवस्थितः ..
तन्महालयमित्युक्तं स्थानं तस्य महात्मनः .. .. 57 ..
16.35.m: Where Rudra arrives and stays at the three junctures of the day— / that place of the great-souled god is called Mahālaya.

16.35.s:
piṃḍatārakamityetatprācīnaṃ tīrthamuttamam ..
kumbhakukṣigiristhaṃ tatpitrye karmaṇi siddhidam .. 58 ..
16.35.d:
पिंडतारकमित्येतत्प्राचीनं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
कुम्भकुक्षिगिरिस्थं तत्पित्र्ये कर्मणि सिद्धिदम् .. 58 ..
16.35.m: The excellent ancient sacred ford called Piṇḍatāraka / situated on Mount Kumbhakukṣi grants success in ancestral rites.

16.35.s:
prācīneśvaradevasya purobhūtaṃ prati ṣṭhitam..
prācī sarasvatī yatra tatra kiṃ mṛgyate param .. 59 ..
16.35.d:
प्राचीनेश्वरदेवस्य पुरोभूतं प्रति ष्ठितम्..
प्राची सरस्वती यत्र तत्र किं मृग्यते परम् .. 59 ..
16.35.m: Established in front of the god Prācīneśvara— / where the east-flowing Sarasvatī is present, what higher thing is sought?

16.35.s:
nivṛtte bhārate yuddhe tatra tīrthe kirīṭinā ..
prāyaścittaṃ purā cīrṇaṃ viṣṇunā preritātmanā .. 7.1.35.60 ..
16.35.d:
निवृत्ते भारते युद्धे तत्र तीर्थे किरीटिना ..
प्रायश्चित्तं पुरा चीर्णं विष्णुना प्रेरितात्मना .. 7.1.35.60 ..
16.35.m: When the Bhārata war ended, the Diademed One [Arjuna], / inspired by Viṣṇu, formerly performed expiation at that sacred ford.

16.35.s:
tena tasmādvinirmuktaḥ pātakātpūrvasaṃcitāt ..
naratīrthaṃ tataḥ khyātaṃ tatra pāpabhayāpaham .. 61 ..
16.35.d:
तेन तस्माद्विनिर्मुक्तः पातकात्पूर्वसंचितात् ..
नरतीर्थं ततः ख्यातं तत्र पापभयापहम् .. 61 ..
16.35.m: By that he was freed from that sin accumulated previously; / hence it became renowned there as Naratīrtha, removing the fear of sin.

16.35.s:
naratīrthādanyatīrthaṃ puṃḍarīkamiti smṛtam ..
arjunena sahāgatya yatra snāto hariḥ priye .. 62 ..
16.35.d:
नरतीर्थादन्यतीर्थं पुंडरीकमिति स्मृतम् ..
अर्जुनेन सहागत्य यत्र स्नातो हरिः प्रिये .. 62 ..
16.35.m: Beyond Naratīrtha is another sacred ford remembered as Puṇḍarīka, / where Hari, having come with Arjuna, bathed, O beloved.

16.35.s:
prācīneśātparaṃ tīrthaṃ vālakhilyeśvaraṃ mahat ..
tatra tasmānmahātīrthāttīrthamanyanmahodayam.. 63 ..
16.35.d:
प्राचीनेशात्परं तीर्थं वालखिल्येश्वरं महत् ..
तत्र तस्मान्महातीर्थात्तीर्थमन्यन्महोदयम्.. 63 ..
16.35.m: Beyond Prācīneśa is the great sacred ford Vālakhilyeśvara; / from that great sacred ford is another of great fruit,

16.35.s:
gaṃgāsamāgamaṃnāma tīrthamanyanmahodayam ..
tatrālokya punardevīṃ dīnāsyāṃ dīnamānasām .. 64 ..
16.35.d:
गंगासमागमंनाम तीर्थमन्यन्महोदयम् ..
तत्रालोक्य पुनर्देवीं दीनास्यां दीनमानसाम् .. 64 ..
16.35.m: another great, auspicious sacred ford named Gaṅgāsamāgama. / Seeing the goddess there once more with a dejected face and sorrowful mind,

16.35.s:
brahmāsṛjatsakhīṃ tasyāḥ kapilāṃ vipulekṣaṇām ..
hariṇīṃ harirapyāśu vajriṇīmapi devarāṭ ..
nyaṃkuṃ vinodanārthaṃ ca sarasvatyā dadau haraḥ .. 65 ..
16.35.d:
ब्रह्मासृजत्सखीं तस्याः कपिलां विपुलेक्षणाम् ..
हरिणीं हरिरप्याशु वज्रिणीमपि देवराट् ..
न्यंकुं विनोदनार्थं च सरस्वत्या ददौ हरः .. 65 ..
16.35.m: Brahmā created for her a companion, Kapilā with wide eyes; / Hari swiftly gave Hariṇī, the king of the gods gave Vajriṇī, / and Hara gave a deer for the recreation of Sarasvatī.

16.35.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭā sā devī devādeśātsarasvatī ..
tasmādgantuṃ samārabdhā prācīnā pāpanāśinī .. 66 ..
16.35.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टा सा देवी देवादेशात्सरस्वती ..
तस्माद्गन्तुं समारब्धा प्राचीना पापनाशिनी .. 66 ..
16.35.m: Delighted then at the command of the gods, the goddess Sarasvatī, / the ancient destroyer of sins, set out to proceed from there.

16.35.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāsthāya punaḥ paścānmukhī tadā ..
sarasvatī mahādevī vaḍavānaladhāriṇī ..
taduttare taṭe tīrthamekadvāramiti smṛtam .. 67 ..
16.35.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय पुनः पश्चान्मुखी तदा ..
सरस्वती महादेवी वडवानलधारिणी ..
तदुत्तरे तटे तीर्थमेकद्वारमिति स्मृतम् .. 67 ..
16.35.m: Īśvara said: / Taking a southern direction and then turning westward once more, / the great goddess Sarasvatī, bearing the submarine fire— / on her northern bank is the sacred ford remembered as Ekadvāra,

16.35.s:
ekadvāreṇa yatsenā svargaṃ prāptā tato varāt ..
tasmāttīrthātpunaścānyattīrthaṃ yatra guheśvaraḥ .. 68 ..
16.35.d:
एकद्वारेण यत्सेना स्वर्गं प्राप्ता ततो वरात् ..
तस्मात्तीर्थात्पुनश्चान्यत्तीर्थं यत्र गुहेश्वरः .. 68 ..
16.35.m: through which a single army attained heaven by its boon. / From that sacred ford is another sacred ford where Guheśvara resides.

16.35.s:
guhena sthāpitaḥ pūrvaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ ..
guheśvarānnātidūre vaṭeśvaramiti smṛtam .. 69 ..
16.35.d:
गुहेन स्थापितः पूर्वं यत्र देवो महेश्वरः ..
गुहेश्वरान्नातिदूरे वटेश्वरमिति स्मृतम् .. 69 ..
16.35.m: Where the god Maheśvara was formerly installed by Guha. / Not far from Guheśvara, it is known as Vaṭeśvara,

16.35.s:
divyaṃ sarasvatītīre vyāsenārādhitaṃ purā ..
āmarddakī nadī yatra sarasvatyā sahaikatām .. 7.1.35.70 ..
16.35.d:
दिव्यं सरस्वतीतीरे व्यासेनाराधितं पुरा ..
आमर्द्दकी नदी यत्र सरस्वत्या सहैकताम् .. 7.1.35.70 ..
16.35.m: a divine [sacred ford] on the bank of the Sarasvatī, formerly worshipped by Vyāsa. / Where the river Āmardakī unites with the Sarasvatī,

16.35.s:
saṃprāptā tanmahātīrthaṃ phaladaṃ sarvadehinām ..
āmardakī saṃgamaṃ taṃ nāpuṇyo veda kaścana ..
saṃgameśvaranāmeti tatra liṃgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 71 ..
16.35.d:
संप्राप्ता तन्महातीर्थं फलदं सर्वदेहिनाम् ..
आमर्दकी संगमं तं नापुण्यो वेद कश्चन ..
संगमेश्वरनामेति तत्र लिंगं प्रतिष्ठितम् .. 71 ..
16.35.m: that great sacred ford grants fruits to all embodied beings. / No one devoid of merit knows that confluence of the Āmardakī. / A liṅga is consecrated there named Saṃgameśvara;

16.35.s:
muṇḍīśvareti ca tathā prasiddhimagamatkṣitau ..
muṃḍīśvarasamīpasthaṃ sarasvatyāṃ mahodayam .. 72 ..
16.35.d:
मुण्डीश्वरेति च तथा प्रसिद्धिमगमत्क्षितौ ..
मुंडीश्वरसमीपस्थं सरस्वत्यां महोदयम् .. 72 ..
16.35.m: and it likewise attained renown on earth by the name Muṇḍīśvara. / Situated near Muṇḍīśvara on the Sarasvatī is the glorious [ford],

16.35.s:
nāmnā yatprāṅmukhaṃ tīrthaṃ sarasvatyāstaṭe sthitam ..
māṃḍavyeśvaranāmnā vai yatreśaḥ saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ .. 73 ..
16.35.d:
नाम्ना यत्प्राङ्मुखं तीर्थं सरस्वत्यास्तटे स्थितम् ..
मांडव्येश्वरनाम्ना वै यत्रेशः संप्रतिष्ठितः .. 73 ..
16.35.m: the sacred ford facing east by name, situated on the bank of the Sarasvatī, / where the Lord is indeed consecrated under the name Māṇḍavyeśvara.

16.35.s:
pīlukarṇikasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthamanyatpunastataḥ ..
sarasvatītīragatamṛṣiṇā sevitaṃ mahat .. 74 ..
16.35.d:
पीलुकर्णिकसंज्ञं तु तीर्थमन्यत्पुनस्ततः ..
सरस्वतीतीरगतमृषिणा सेवितं महत् .. 74 ..
16.35.m: Then, beyond that, is another sacred ford named Pīlukarṇika, / situated on the bank of the Sarasvatī, a great [ford] frequented by the seer.

16.35.s:
tasmādanyatsarasvatyāṃ tīrthaṃ dvāravatī smṛtam ..
tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ devi yatra saṃnihito hariḥ .. 75 ..
16.35.d:
तस्मादन्यत्सरस्वत्यां तीर्थं द्वारवती स्मृतम् ..
तीर्थानां प्रवरं देवि यत्र संनिहितो हरिः .. 75 ..
16.35.m: Beyond that, another sacred ford on the Sarasvatī is known as Dvāravatī, / the foremost of sacred fords, O goddess, where Hari is present.

16.35.s:
tatastasya samīpasthaṃ tīrthaṃ govatsasaṃjñitam ..
yatrāvatīrya govatsasvarūpeṇāṃbikāpatiḥ .. 76 ..
16.35.d:
ततस्तस्य समीपस्थं तीर्थं गोवत्ससंज्ञितम् ..
यत्रावतीर्य गोवत्सस्वरूपेणांबिकापतिः .. 76 ..
16.35.m: Then, situated near it, is the sacred ford named Govatsa, / where Ambikā's lord, having descended in the form of a cow and calf,

16.35.s:
svayaṃ bhūliṃgarūpeṇa saṃsthitastejasāṃ nidhiḥ ..
govatsānnairṛte bhāge dṛśyate lohayaṣṭikā .. 77 ..
16.35.d:
स्वयं भूलिंगरूपेण संस्थितस्तेजसां निधिः ..
गोवत्सान्नैरृते भागे दृश्यते लोहयष्टिका .. 77 ..
16.35.m: abides himself in the form of a svayambhu liṅga, a treasure of splendours. / To the southwest of Govatsa, an iron post is seen.

16.35.s:
svayaṃbhūliṃgarūpeṇa rudrastatra svayaṃ sthitaḥ ..
ekaviṃśati vārasya bhaktyā piṃḍasya yatphalam .. 78 ..
16.35.d:
स्वयंभूलिंगरूपेण रुद्रस्तत्र स्वयं स्थितः ..
एकविंशति वारस्य भक्त्या पिंडस्य यत्फलम् .. 78 ..
16.35.m: Rudra himself resides there in the form of a svayambhu liṅga. / The fruit that is obtained in the Gaṅgā by offering a piṇḍa with devotion

16.35.s:
gaṃgāyāṃ prāpyate puṃsāṃ śrāddhenaikena tatra tat ..
tatastasmānmahātīrthādbālakrīḍanakī yathā .. 79 ..
16.35.d:
गंगायां प्राप्यते पुंसां श्राद्धेनैकेन तत्र तत् ..
ततस्तस्मान्महातीर्थाद्बालक्रीडनकी यथा .. 79 ..
16.35.m: twenty-one times, men attain there through a single śrāddha. / Then, like a playing girl, from that great sacred ford,

16.35.s:
sakhībhiḥ sahitā tatra krīḍatā'sau yathecchayā ..
ānulomyavilomyena dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca .. 7.1.35.80 ..
16.35.d:
सखीभिः सहिता तत्र क्रीडताऽसौ यथेच्छया ..
आनुलोम्यविलोम्येन दक्षिणेनोत्तरेण च .. 7.1.35.80 ..
16.35.m: accompanied by her female companions, playing there as she wished, / forwards and backwards, to the south and to the north,

16.35.s:
rullaṃ prāpya punardevī samudbhūtā manoramā ..
rullaṃ nāma puraṃ yatra sṛṣṭaṃ devena śaṃbhunā .. 81 ..
16.35.d:
रुल्लं प्राप्य पुनर्देवी समुद्भूता मनोरमा ..
रुल्लं नाम पुरं यत्र सृष्टं देवेन शंभुना .. 81 ..
16.35.m: having reached Rulla, the charming goddess arose again. / Where the town named Rulla was created by the god Śambhu

16.35.s:
saha devaistu pārvatyā dhārāyaṃtraprayogakaiḥ ..
ekaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu śaṃbhunā tatra rullitam .. 82 ..
16.35.d:
सह देवैस्तु पार्वत्या धारायंत्रप्रयोगकैः ..
एकं वर्षसहस्रं तु शंभुना तत्र रुल्लितम् .. 82 ..
16.35.m: together with the gods and Pārvatī, by operations of mechanical water sprays, / Śambhu sported there for one thousand years.

16.35.s:
rullaṃ tatra hradaṃ nāma sarasvatyāṃ mahodayam ..
sākṣāttatra mahādeva ānaṃdeśvarasaṃjñitaḥ .. 83 ..
16.35.d:
रुल्लं तत्र ह्रदं नाम सरस्वत्यां महोदयम् ..
साक्षात्तत्र महादेव आनंदेश्वरसंज्ञितः .. 83 ..
16.35.m: The pool there is named Rulla, most auspicious on the Sarasvatī. / Mahādeva is directly present there under the name Ānandeśvara.

16.35.s:
paścimena sthitaṃ tatra śambhorāyatanasya tu ..
sa merordakṣiṇe pāde nakhastu parikīrtitaḥ .. 84 ..
16.35.d:
पश्चिमेन स्थितं तत्र शम्भोरायतनस्य तु ..
स मेरोर्दक्षिणे पादे नखस्तु परिकीर्तितः .. 84 ..
16.35.m: To the west of the abode of Śambhu situated there, / it is renowned as a claw on the right foot of Meru.

16.35.s:
paśyaṃti ye narāḥ samyakte'pi pāpavivarjitāḥ ..
aśvamedhasahasrasya prāpnuvaṃti phalaṃ dhruvam .. 85 ..
16.35.d:
पश्यंति ये नराः सम्यक्तेऽपि पापविवर्जिताः ..
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य प्राप्नुवंति फलं ध्रुवम् .. 85 ..
16.35.m: The men who behold it properly, freed from sin, / surely attain the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.

16.35.s:
paratastasya kūṣmāṃḍamunestatrāśramaṃ mahat ..
kūṣmāṃḍeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam .. 86 ..
16.35.d:
परतस्तस्य कूष्मांडमुनेस्तत्राश्रमं महत् ..
कूष्मांडेश्वरसंज्ञं तु तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् .. 86 ..
16.35.m: Beyond that is the great hermitage of the sage Kūṣmāṇḍa; / the sacred ford, named Kūṣmāṇḍeśvara, is renowned throughout the three worlds.

16.35.s:
kollādevī sthitā tatra sarvapāpabhayāpahā ..
antarddhānena tāṃ kollāṃ saṃprāptā sā mahānadī .. 87 ..
16.35.d:
कोल्लादेवी स्थिता तत्र सर्वपापभयापहा ..
अन्तर्द्धानेन तां कोल्लां संप्राप्ता सा महानदी .. 87 ..
16.35.m: The goddess Kollā is present there, taking away the fear of all sins. / By disappearance, that great river reached that Kollā.

16.35.s:
tato'pyaṃtarhitā bhūtvā saṃprāptā tu manoramam ..
sānuṃ madanasaṃjñaṃ tu kṣetraṃ siddhaniṣevitam .. 88 ..
16.35.d:
ततोऽप्यंतर्हिता भूत्वा संप्राप्ता तु मनोरमम् ..
सानुं मदनसंज्ञं तु क्षेत्रं सिद्धनिषेवितम् .. 88 ..
16.35.m: Disappearing from there too, she reached the charming / peak named Madana, a sacred field frequented by perfected beings.

16.35.s:
tato'pyaṃtarhitā bhūtvā punaḥ prāptā himācalam ..
khādirāmodanāmānaṃ sarvartukusumojjvalam .. 89 ..
16.35.d:
ततोऽप्यंतर्हिता भूत्वा पुनः प्राप्ता हिमाचलम् ..
खादिरामोदनामानं सर्वर्तुकुसुमोज्ज्वलम् .. 89 ..
16.35.m: Disappearing from there too, she again reached the snowy mountain / named Khādirāmoda, radiant with flowers of all seasons.

16.35.s:
tatrāruhya vilokyātha dadarśa sumanoramama ..
kṣārodaṃ paścimāśāsthaṃ ghanavṛṃdamivonnatam .. 7.1.35.90 ..
16.35.d:
तत्रारुह्य विलोक्याथ ददर्श सुमनोरमम ..
क्षारोदं पश्चिमाशास्थं घनवृंदमिवोन्नतम् .. 7.1.35.90 ..
16.35.m: Having climbed there and looked out, she then beheld the most delightful / salt ocean situated in the western quarter, towering like a mass of clouds.

16.35.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ ca taṃ tatra sā vilokya mahāprabhā ..
harṣātpaṃcānanā bhūtvā devakāryārthamudyatā .. 91 ..
16.35.d:
एवंविधं च तं तत्र सा विलोक्य महाप्रभा ..
हर्षात्पंचानना भूत्वा देवकार्यार्थमुद्यता .. 91 ..
16.35.m: Seeing it thus situated there, she of great radiance, / having become five-mouthed out of joy, set out for the purpose of the gods' work.

16.35.s:
hariṇī vajriṇī nyaṃkuḥ kapilā ca sarasvatī ..
paṃcasrotāḥ sthitā tatra muninoktā sarasvatī .. 92 ..
16.35.d:
हरिणी वज्रिणी न्यंकुः कपिला च सरस्वती ..
पंचस्रोताः स्थिता तत्र मुनिनोक्ता सरस्वती .. 92 ..
16.35.m: Hariṇī, Vajriṇī, Nyaṅku, Kapilā, and Sarasvatī: / the Sarasvatī, proclaimed by the sage, remained there with five streams.

16.35.s:
śramāpanodaṃ kurvāṇā munīnāṃ yatra saṃsthitā ..
tattatpādakamityuktaṃ tīrthaṃ tīrthārthināṃ nṛṇām ..
sarveṣāṃ pātakānāṃ ca śodhanaṃ tadvarānane .. 93 ..
16.35.d:
श्रमापनोदं कुर्वाणा मुनीनां यत्र संस्थिता ..
तत्तत्पादकमित्युक्तं तीर्थं तीर्थार्थिनां नृणाम् ..
सर्वेषां पातकानां च शोधनं तद्वरानने .. 93 ..
16.35.m: Where she stood dispelling the weariness of the sages, / that sacred ford is called Tatpādaka for men seeking sacred fords, / and a purifier of all sins, O fair-faced one!

16.35.s:
khādirāmodamāsādya tatrasthā vīkṣya sāgaram ..
gantuṃ pravṛttā taṃ vahnimādāya surasundari .. 94 ..
16.35.d:
खादिरामोदमासाद्य तत्रस्था वीक्ष्य सागरम् ..
गन्तुं प्रवृत्ता तं वह्निमादाय सुरसुन्दरि .. 94 ..
16.35.m: Having reached Khādirāmoda and standing there, beholding the ocean, / she set forth to go, carrying that fire, O beauty among the gods!

16.35.s:
dagdhvā kṛtasmaraṃ devī punarādāya vāḍavam ..
samudrasya samīpasthā sthitā hṛṣṭatanūruhā .. 95 ..
16.35.d:
दग्ध्वा कृतस्मरं देवी पुनरादाय वाडवम् ..
समुद्रस्य समीपस्था स्थिता हृष्टतनूरुहा .. 95 ..
16.35.m: Having burned Kṛtasmara, the goddess, taking the submarine fire once more, / stood near the ocean with her hairs bristling with joy.

16.35.s:
tataḥ praviṣṭā sā devī agādhe lavaṇāṃbhasi ..
vāḍavaṃ vahnimādāya jalamadhye vyasarjayat .. 96 ..
16.35.d:
ततः प्रविष्टा सा देवी अगाधे लवणांभसि ..
वाडवं वह्निमादाय जलमध्ये व्यसर्जयत् .. 96 ..
16.35.m: Then that goddess entered into the unfathomable salty water. / Taking the submarine fire, she cast it into the midst of the waters.

16.35.s:
tatastasyāḥ punaḥ prītaḥ svayameva hutāśanaḥ ..
taddṛṣṭvā duṣkaraṃ karma vacanaṃ cedamabravīt .. 97 ..
16.35.d:
ततस्तस्याः पुनः प्रीतः स्वयमेव हुताशनः ..
तद्दृष्ट्वा दुष्करं कर्म वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् .. 97 ..
16.35.m: Then the fire, exceedingly pleased with her, / seeing that difficult deed, himself spoke these words:

16.35.s:
parituṣṭo'smi te bhadre varaṃ varaya suvrate ..
tatte dāsyāmyahaṃ prīto yadyapi syātsudurlabham .. 98 ..
16.35.d:
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भद्रे वरं वरय सुव्रते ..
तत्ते दास्याम्यहं प्रीतो यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम् .. 98 ..
16.35.m: ‘I am well pleased with you, gentle lady; choose a boon, O lady of good vows! / Being pleased, I shall grant it to you, even if it is very difficult to obtain.’

16.35.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
pragṛhya valayaṃ hastādidaṃ vacanamabravīt ..
idaṃ me valayaṃ vahne vaktre dhāryaṃ sadā tvayā .. 99 ..
16.35.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
प्रगृह्य वलयं हस्तादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ..
इदं मे वलयं वह्ने वक्त्रे धार्यं सदा त्वया .. 99 ..
16.35.m: Īśvara said: / Taking a bangle from her hand, she spoke these words: / ‘This bangle of mine must always be held in your mouth, O Fire!

16.35.s:
anena śakyate yāvattāvattoyaṃ samāhara ..
na tvayā śoṣaṇīyo'yaṃ samudaḥ saritāṃpatiḥ .. 7.1.35.100 ..
16.35.d:
अनेन शक्यते यावत्तावत्तोयं समाहर ..
न त्वया शोषणीयोऽयं समुदः सरितांपतिः .. 7.1.35.100 ..
16.35.m: Consume only as much water as is possible through this; / you must not dry up this ocean, the lord of rivers!’
